Its time is nearly all compiling: half an hour, three times `acceptance-far`'s ten minutes, so the census and not the gate. The code it exercises - cftc, the software backend, seq.py and both auditors - is what the gate's `acceptance` stage already exercises.
- Gray-Scott extended and Riccati extended are left to a card day, which reads the box's compile back through `--images`. Their compiles took 40 minutes and 2.2 hours on the box.
- The runner has 52 stages, with 31 in quick and 44 in gate as before. `--list`'s name column is one character wider, so the stage's fifteen-character name keeps a space before its description.

**Known limits.**
- **No golden audit on any entry**, because of seq.py's cost. The golden ties are the spot check and the oracle's one step on the pack's three lanes.
- **Eight steps of each workload's dynamics.** The record holds bit-exactness over four segments of two steps, a short trajectory, as the acceptance set's 8 to 32 steps do.
- **One image per workload.** The quad's nine are not run on the deep, by the rule. rev8a gets no entry, since no workload needs R21.
- **The identity check reads the certificate's device-tiles and audited depth**, which tell the three images apart, and not the CAPS words. The card legs' device-test -i reads those.
- **Gray-Scott and Riccati extended were compiled only on the box,** by cftc's command line at ab51655. The record holds those images' digests, and the desktop never compiled them. A fresh compile of them in the driver is a card day's software check (about 40 minutes and 2.2 hours there), and the census stage leaves them out.
- **Lorenz-tangent extended** is refused by cftc's allocation on the deep. Whether any allocation fits 8,192 is not shown.
- **The compile times** are from a desktop in and out of use and a loaded box. One compile varied by up to 30% between runs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky extended, 509.8 to 663.9 s).

## 2026-10-12 - does RETIMING=1 retime? No: a kernel's synthesis in the link has never had a clock, so Vivado declines `-retiming`, and the flag changes no netlist (the whole revision-8 kernel on the box; revision 7's q135 link); with a clock it would make 1,250 retiming moves for +0.669 ns out of context; the 2026-09-02 gain was not retiming's; SYNTH_CLOCK=1 merged off by Logan's word (parcel RT)

**Why.**
- Step 6's close left it open (the entry above, its known limits, from verifier-VI9b): every revision-8 kernel synthesis log says "INFO: [Synth 8-11322] No global retiming is needed without any clock constraint". Yet hw/rebuild-2022.sh's comment credited retiming with an out-of-context gain measured 2026-09-02, revision 7's quad is recorded as "all four tiles retimed", and every image built to the recipe since 2026-09-02, revision 8's three among them, was built with RETIMING=1 (the first sweep script's points, 2026-09-23, were built without it).
- Parcel RT, from ab51655 (brief and ledger under `Data/runs/2026-10-12-step6-leftovers/`: briefs/RT.md, ledger/RT.md, the toys' scripts and logs in ledger/RT-toys/, and the box run's copies in box/probe-rt-949e56c/). Marks: MEASURED by RT in WSL cft2204's Vivado 2022.2, or by the lead on amd-arc-box where so named; READ in a named record; COMPUTED; BELIEVED. No image was built, and RT touched neither amd-arc-box nor the card. Verifier-VRT checked 949e56c and verifier-VRTb the follow-up, 30bade6 (neither found a regression or a wrong answer; their notes are taken below).

**What the builds did (READ, the logs copied under the step-6 round's box/).**
- rev8a's kernel synthesis: `Command: synth_design -top ulp_cft_krnl_1_0 -part xcu50-fsvh2104-2-e -retiming -incremental_mode off -mode out_of_context`. No "Parsing XDC File" line; "Processing XDC Constraints" and "Applying XDC Timing Constraints" with nothing between them. Synth 8-11322 22 times, all inside "Technology Mapping". **What Xilinx's documentation says (READ).**
- Vivado 2022.2's `help synth_design`: -retiming "Seeks to improve circuit performance for intra-clock sequential paths by automatically moving registers (register balancing) across combinatorial gates or LUTs"; and synthesis is timing-driven by default (-no_timing_driven "ignores the effect of timing on synthesis").
- UG901, the 2022.1 and 2022.2 editions, RETIMING_BACKWARD: "Unlike the retiming global setting, this attribute is not timing driven and will work regardless of whether the retiming global setting is active or if there are even timing constraints." The global setting is timing-driven. rtl/ carries no such attribute.
- No public page for Synth 8-11322 turned up in two searches; its text is the tool's own.

**The toys (MEASURED; WSL cft2204, Vivado 2022.2, general.maxThreads 4, nice 10, one at a time).**
- toy0, a 64-bit pipeline with all its logic in one stage and two empty stages after it, out of context at 600 MHz, four ways. a (no flag, no clock): WNS -0.814, 498 LUT, 448 FF. b (the flag, no clock): Synth 8-11322 once, and the funcsim netlist (comment lines removed) byte for byte a's, sha256 8a685cd7...; a run again gives 8a685cd7... too. c (the flag, a clock read before synth_design): Synth 8-5816 twice, a "Retiming Report:" (forward 0, backward 38, 801 registers added, 64 deleted), 760 FF, WNS -0.071. d (the clock alone): a netlist of its own (0741931c...), 560 LUT, WNS -0.754. Verifier-VRT re-ran it under Vivado 2022.2 and, beyond its brief, under the desktop's Vivado 2026.1: a == b and c retimed in both, so a clockless -retiming is a no-op in both versions the project used out of context.
- toy3 and toy5, hw/probe_rt.sh on one fp32 FMA pipe (cft_fpfma_pipe at EXP_W=8, MAN_W=23, LATENCY=16; rtl 44b963dd) at 135 MHz, about 1.2 to 1.6 min and 2.5 to 3.2 GB a way. toy3 ran the script before the commit, toy5 the committed script at 949e56c with LINK_LOG set; the four netlists hash the same in both. a and b byte for byte the same, comment lines removed (152074bd...: 2,591 LUT, 1,620 FF, WNS +3.803 with the clock applied after synthesis). c: forward 71, backward 35, 204 added, 80 deleted, 1,719 FF, WNS +4.717. d: 2,583 LUT, WNS +3.786, its own netlist. DSP registers the same in all four (two DSP48E2, PREG on one, MREG on none).
- toy1, the link's situation in miniature: a user IP packaged the way hw/package_kernel.tcl packages cft_krnl (user parameters removed), in a block design, synthesized per IP with STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.RETIMING true. The run's command line is the link's exactly, and it prints Synth 8-11322 and reads no XDC: a user IP's run gets no clock. The same run with a STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.TCL.PRE hook that does `read_xdc -mode out_of_context` of a clock: the XDC parsed, Synth 8-5816, backward 38. In the generated run script (READ) the hook is sourced after `create_project -in_memory` and before `read_ip` and `synth_design`; and with a hook the script has no `config_ip_cache` at all, where without one the cache check is `config_ip_cache -export -no_bom -synth_opts { -retiming }`.
- toy2: the BD's wrapper as top with a 10 ns clock of its own, the IP's run given 1.667 ns by the hook (`read_xdc -mode out_of_context` in both forms), with and without `set_property used_in_implementation false` on the XDC. Opened in context (the top synthesized, as an implementation links it), the design carries the 10 ns clock alone in both: with the mode, the property is not needed to keep the hook's clock out. With the property the IP's run parses the XDC once, for synthesis, and still retimes (Synth 8-5816 twice); without it, twice. Vivado's own IP runs mark an IP's out-of-context XDC that way (READ: a clk_wiz's generated run script), and the hook does too. Verifier-VRT ran the hook rebuild-2022.sh generates through the same toy, to opt_design: no leak with or without the property. No toy ran a plain `read_xdc`, so the mode was never varied (the fix, below).
- toy4: hw/ooc_retime.tcl's DSP loop, on the fp32 pipe, counts PREG twice for its one DSP with PREG: the DSP48E2 g_mul_local.s2_pp_reg[0] and its DSP_OUTPUT_INST. That register is the RTL's own partial-product register, which DSP inference absorbs with no retiming.

Its LUT and WNS are those of 2026-09-01's "shared array, seq diet, ladders off" row (ROADMAP); its 292 DSP is ARCHITECTURE's figure for that tile; its 55,362 FF are in no earlier record. That row was measured on "the merged tree" - BELIEVED a445268, the seq-diet merge (16:19), whose rtl has the ladders off and no register on the reduce operands - before 1efd681 (ladders on by default, 17:37) and 8f5f149 (21:08). 8f5f149 put that register in, 2 x 256 + 1 bits, and its message says the path "read +0.307 and hid" out of context. 2b57cf0 (09-02 04:40) carries it (READ: red_add_a_q in cft_engine_stream.sv). BELIEVED: the "retimed" row is that later tree, and the +1.374 ns and +354 FF are 8f5f149's register.

**The fix, behind a flag that is off: SYNTH_CLOCK=1** (hw/rebuild-2022.sh; docs/BITSTREAM-BUILDS.md, "SYNTH_CLOCK=1"). It writes BUILD/synth_clock.xdc (a create_clock on ap_clk at 1e9/KERNEL_FREQ ns, named cft_synth_ooc_clk) and BUILD/synth_clock_pre.tcl (`read_xdc -mode out_of_context` of it, then `used_in_implementation false`, and a CFT_SYNTH_CLOCK: line into the run's log), and hands every CU's synthesis run the hook as `{STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.TCL.PRE}`, on hw links alone. What keeps that clock out of the implementation is BELIEVED: toy2 shows only that, with the mode, the property is not needed; that the mode does it rests on Vivado's documentation of the option, and verifier-VRTb's alternative, that the IP's run is a project of its own whose read never reaches the top, is not excluded. Both guards stay, so the hook does not depend on which. With SYNTH_CLOCK=1, KERNEL_FREQ must be Hz, or it stops by name before v++. SYNTH_CLOCK, RETIMING and PHYS_OPT must each be 0 or 1, or it stops by name before any work (the test's mark: no BUILD directory made); until 2026-10-12 RETIMING=true or yes, and PHYS_OPT=true or yes, built quietly with the flag off, and no caller in the repo passes another value (`git grep`). hw/build-pair.sh refuses the same SYNTH_CLOCK values among its assertions, so its --dry-run cannot pass one the build would refuse. Carried as code, not a patch: with SYNTH_CLOCK unset, v++'s argv is byte for byte ab51655's script's under the buildargs stubs (MEASURED by RT at 949e56c, single and quad, RETIMING 0 and 1; at the follow-up, TARGETS hw and "hw hw_emu" too, 8 of 8 with the same exit status; at the third commit those 8 again and with PHYS_OPT=1, 16 of 16; by verifier-VRT at 949e56c, 14 of 14 cases, and by verifier-VRTb at 30bade6, 18 of 18). Costs, and the open question, are in BITSTREAM-BUILDS: a quad synthesizes all four CUs (no IP cache with a hook), and the vpl's dynamic-region flow is toy2's BELIEVED until an image's manifest and routed report show it.
- **Logan, 2026-10-12:** "Keep it off for now (Recommended)". Merged off, with the finding recorded; to be revisited when a build needs margin, with a routed A/B.

**The manifest.** `retiming:` stays the request and `retimed_runs:` the CUs whose synthesis was given -retiming, now taken from retime_effect's own first test, so the two cannot disagree; that test reads the flag as a token, ` -retiming` followed by a space or the line's end, so a path holding "-retiming" is not the flag (verifier-VRTb's fabricated case; a link's command line has no paths). New: `retiming_effect:`, each CU's from its producing run's log - `retimed(forward=F,backward=B,reports=N)` when a report shows a move, `ran-no-moves(reports=N)` when reports show none (not "retimed", since the line exists so that the manifest never claims a retiming that did not happen), `declined-no-clock` (Synth 8-11322 and no report), `asked-no-report`, and `not-asked` when the synth_design had no -retiming, whatever else the log says; a report and a decline in one log add `,declined=K` rather than let one hide the other. The decline is matched as Vivado's tagged message, `[Synth 8-11322]`, so a script's echoed text is not one. Then `synth_clock:` (1 with the period for an hw target built with the flag, else 0) and, with it, `synth_clock_runs:`. On the real logs (MEASURED): rev8a, rev8d and rev8q's krnl_4 `declined-no-clock`, probe S3 and toy0's way a `not-asked`, toy1's hooked run `retimed(forward=0,backward=38,reports=1)`, the box's way c `retimed(forward=561,backward=689,reports=1)`. Every reader of the manifest reads its keys by name (build-pair.sh, verify-image.sh, card-identity.sh, sweep_freq.sh), so the new keys break none. build-pair's read-back, under a comment saying it shows what "ACTUALLY applied", printed only the requests; it now prints `retiming_effect:` and `synth_clock:` too, and its comment says which lines are requests.

**The IP cache, a side finding (READ).** rev8a's krnl_1, rev8d's krnl_1 and rev8q's krnl_4 each added cache-ID ebc05e65b15fbbd4, for three different netlists (183,370, 180,003 and 167,534 LUTs): the key does not cover the packaged generics. Each build ran in its own clone, and the cache is the checkout's .ipcache, so nothing was mixed. BELIEVED: two builds from one checkout with different CFT_GENERICS and the same RETIMING would share the first one's netlist. BITSTREAM-BUILDS now says to build different CFT_GENERICS from separate clones.

**Why.**

## 2026-10-12 - the math library's first routine, exp, golden-first: fp32 (triple word), fp64, fp128 and fp256 under every attribute, held to the study's section 8 with a planted fault for every check (parcel E1, arm a)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "The math library: experiment E1, then M1's build and M2 to M4") starts the library with one function built golden-first, exp (Logan's choice over the plan's exp2). This parcel is that build. It is one of two builds of one brief that the lead compares blind, so this entry says what was built and measured and compares nothing.
- It adds the golden generator `python/cft_golden/mathlib.py`, exp's fragment at the four formats and five attributes in C4's Fragment shape, its constants with a `--check`, the study's section 8 items 1 to 5 for exp, and a planted fault for every check. It changes no existing code and wires nothing into `routines.ROUTINES`, cftc, the language, program.c or the card.
- The brief and its first correction are the lead's (outside the tree). The correction's seven rules, and where each is held: (1) fp32 has no window, so the windows are listed and tested at fp64, fp128 and fp256 and fp32's census run is recorded, with a plant that makes its emptiness check fail; (2) the budget's reference files include m1measure.py and meas32.py, both read; (3) fp32's reduction is the study's 2.5 (ln2/8 in five words, r in three); (4) "TwoSum, not augadd" means no augmented addition, the study's Fast2Sum and TwoSum kept; (5) the mark-rate law at G' = 6, 2,000 lanes a cell as m1rate.py draws them, the 15 cells of fp64, fp128 and fp256, three sigma; (6) nothing in `python/cft_golden/routines.py` is assigned, even at run time: the widened flag-word set and live cap are mathlib.py's own, and no plant patches anything: each is a builder parameter, a fault of a tool or a mutation of a fresh build; (7) a mark in the pools off the committed structured list fails test 1.
- Marks: MEASURED is a run of this parcel's, its command and time given, on the desktop, niced, one process at a time; READ is a file, named; COMPUTED is arithmetic on those; BELIEVED is mine and not shown.

**What was built** (six new files, one dated note in the study, this entry, docs/README.md recounted).
- `python/cft_golden/mathlib.py` (1,774 lines): exact helpers (a constant is an exact rational rounded once into the format, through `round_pack`); the constants, derived from mpmath at 3,000 bits (ln 2, 2^(j/8)) or exact rationals (1/(i+1)!); the plan K and D in exact rational arithmetic; `Build`, the builder (straight-line SSA hash-consed on opcode, attribute and operands, `routines.simplify` applied as an instruction is made) and its instrumented form (the unpruned body, each instruction's phase, the probes V_h, V_l, Bv, Ek and the values between, and every derived constant by role; `Build.run` runs it, with a probe's value replaced where asked); the double-word builder (fp64, fp128, fp256) and the triple-word builder (fp32); `fragment(name, fmt, rnd)` and `evaluate(f, x)`; the widened `invariants()` and `flag_words()`; `check_constants()` and `python -m cft_golden.mathlib --check`; `PLANTS`, eighteen faults of the builder.
- `python/tests/test_mathlib.py` (252 tests), `python/tests/mathlib_harness.py` (the lanes, the samplers and the checks, each check returning findings that begin with its own name), `python/tests/mathlib_budget.py` (verifier-VM1b's first-order budget, ported), `python/tests/mathlib_family.py` (the structured family's theory and its committed list, generated), `python/tests/mathlib_runs.py` (the larger runs as a script).
- No file added or changed imports anything from `docs/studies/`. `python/cft_golden/mathlib.py` imports mpmath, as transcend.py does.

**The design as built** (READ: docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, sections 2.2, 2.4 to 2.6, 3.1, 4 and 5.1).
- exp as the study designs it: classify; n = round(x 8/ln2) by the magic-number FMA; r = x - n ln2/8 by Cody-Waite (ln2/8 in three words and r a double word at fp64, fp128, fp256; in five words and r in three at fp32); T_j = 2^(j/8), N = 8, a SELECT tree over bank words; Y(r) = (e^r - 1)/r by Taylor, a single-word Horner tail and K double-word steps (three-word steps at fp32); V = T (1 + Z); one rounding from V under the program's attribute; the in-lane test (V_l - Bv rounded down and V_l + Bv rounded up, each added to V_h under the attribute, a lane where the two roundings differ marked), Bv = 2^-(p+G) |V_h|; the fixed grid for a result that may be subnormal, with its own test; the specials in the study's order; the flag word exactly the operation's IEEE flags in [4:0] with bit 7 the mark.
- Logan's decisions, all "as recommended" (the study's section 9): G = 44 at fp64, 46 at fp128 and fp256, 40 at fp32; the SELECT tree at N = 8; the structured families keep their marks; no augmented addition.
- **Plan** (MEASURED, `python -m cft_golden.mathlib --check` prints it; COMPUTED by `plan_exp` in exact rationals): K = 7 and D = 12, 20, 33 at fp64 (G = 44), fp128, fp256; fp32 K3 = 3, K2 = 4, D = 9. **Error-free sums** (MEASURED, `Build.meta`): the double-word exp holds nine Fast2Sums and one TwoSum, fp32's 20 and 18.
- **Shape** (MEASURED, `python -m cft_golden.mathlib`; READ against the study's 5.1, below): instructions, bank words and values live, rne / rtz / rdn / rup / rmm.
  - fp32: 382, 380, 380, 379, 382 instructions; 71, 71, 71, 70, 71 words; 34, 33, 33, 33, 34 live.
  - fp64: 180, 178, 178, 177, 180; 63, 63, 63, 62, 63; 23, 22, 22, 22, 23.
  - fp128: 188, 186, 186, 185, 188; 72, 72, 72, 71, 72; 23, 22, 22, 22, 23.
  - fp256: 201, 199, 199, 198, 201; 85, 85, 85, 84, 85; 23, 22, 22, 22, 23.
  - By phase at fp64 rne (MEASURED, `Build.phase_of`): classify 10, reduce 14, lookup 17, scale 15, tail 5, head 53, Z 5, reconstruction 13, final 15, fixed grid 21, specials 12 (the study's, with G = 44's tail of 5 for 6); at fp256 the tail is 26.
  - **Against the study's 5.1** (READ): it agrees at fp128 (185 to 188) and fp256 (198 to 201), in fp32's 382 instructions at G = 40 (rne) and in 34 values live. It differs where it measured at G = 46: fp64's 178 to 181 instructions, one more than this tree's 177 to 180 at G = 44 (the tail is a step shorter), and fp32's bank words, 72 to 73, against 70 to 71 at G = 40. MEASURED in a scratch script, not committed because it imports `docs/studies/`: the study's model, built at the decided G and at G = 46 under the five attributes, equals this tree's in instructions, bank words and values live in every cell (fp32 at G = 40 and 46, fp64 at 44 and 46, fp128 and fp256 at 46), so the differences are G's. (The first version of this entry, and the ledger's first entries, said the study's 5.1 "has the same": that was wrong at fp64 and in fp32's words.)
- **Identical to the study's model** (MEASURED in a scratch script, not committed because no tree file may import `docs/studies/`): at all 20 configurations the specialised body, with each word read as its bits, the result and the flag word equal `m1exp.build_exp`'s at G = 44 (fp64) and 46 (fp128, fp256) and `m1exp32.build_exp32`'s at G = 40, instruction for instruction. So the design is the study's, ported; what the tree adds is checked below against transcend.exp and mpmath, which share nothing with the model.

**Held to the study's section 8** (every command from the repository root, niced; each prints "RESULT: ok" or its findings and exits 0 or 1).
- **Item 1, against transcend.exp** (`python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py pools --seq`, 30 s): the transcend pools - `host/tests/transcend_check.py`'s unary pool at its default (64 random encodings at fp32 and fp64, 16 at fp128 and fp256) and seed 5, the vector sets' `python/cft_golden/vectors.py` pool at seed 9 and `python/tests/test_transcend.py`'s brute pool - are 330, 367, 350 and 512 lanes, each through every attribute through `evaluate`, and at fp64, fp128 and fp256 as a stand-alone program on seq.py through `routines.program` and `routines.run`: 0 wrong unmarked in all 20 and all 15. The marked lanes: fp32 none; fp64, fp128, fp256 exactly one each, exp(+2^-p) under rne and rmm and exp(-2^-p) under the directed three, both on the committed structured list; its guess is wrong under rne (1 of 1) and right under the other four. A mark off the list fails the check (rule 7), and so does a lane on the list that is not marked: each listed centre is one the theory puts inside its window.
  - `python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py lanes --n 2000 --seed 5` (168 s): 3,954 to 3,977 random and weighted arguments a cell (every bit of the argument random), all 20 cells: 0 marked, 0 wrong unmarked, 79,280 lane-attribute pairs in all.

- **Item 2, the bound** (`python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py bound --format fp32,fp64,fp128,fp256 --random 3000 --weighted 3000 --seed 5`, 53 s): the largest |V - exp(x) 2^-k| / Bv found, mpmath at 4p + 200 bits, as log2 - over 3,000 random arguments with every bit random, over 258 placed at each path's largest |r| (x next to (n +- 1/2) ln2/8 for the study's n, every residue j at k = emin - 1 to emin + 1, -1 to 1 and the ends of the main path, each with its two neighbours), and over 3,000 of VM1's weighted sampler:
  - fp32 (G = 40): -5.66, -4.95, -5.24; fp64 (G = 44): -2.69, -2.64, -2.64; fp128: -6.37, -6.09, -6.09; fp256: -6.03, -5.82, -5.79.
  - These are lower bounds on the true worst. **The budget states the bound** (`python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py budget --format fp64,fp128,fp256 --unit 300 --weighted 300 --seed 5`, 78 s; 858 lanes a format: 300 uniform on [-1, 1], 300 weighted, the 258 placed): fp64 at G = 44 0.1644 Bv, 2^-2.60 (M 0.1558 + capacities 0.0086; the study's 0.164, READ), fp128 at 46 0.0148, 2^-6.07 (M 0.0008 + 0.0140), fp256 0.0193, 2^-5.69 (M 0.0053 + 0.0140); the largest errors found, 0.1604, 0.0147 and 0.0177 Bv, are under them. At fp64 the margin is the planners' two-bit target, set by the truncation of Y at degree 12, not by a rounding. exp has no amplified place: V = T (1 + Z) with |Z| under 0.044 and T from 1 to 1.84, no term is large beside the result (COMPUTED from the table and rho). fp32 has no budget (its V is three words); its bound is the measurement above.
  - **The budget port is the original's** (MEASURED in a scratch script, not committed, since it imports `docs/studies/`): the same 45 lanes a format (weighted, uniform and placed) through verifier-VM1b's `adlib.Analyzer` on the model's build and through `mathlib_budget.Analyzer` on this parcel's: V, the twin's V, Bv and every instruction's rounding error, its delta_i s_i and its capacity are equal, 4,770 contributions at fp64 and 5,130 at fp128, 0 differences.
- **Item 3, the mark-rate law** (`python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py rate --format fp64,fp128,fp256 --n 2000 --seed 7`, 46 s): the bound inflated to 2^-(p+6) (G' = 6), 2,000 uniform arguments a cell as m1rate.py draws them, predicted 2^(0.53 - 6) = 2.25%, 45.1 marks, sigma 6.6. The 15 cells marked 42, 52, 52, 52, 42 (fp64, rne to rmm), 52, 36, 36, 36, 52 (fp128), 39, 46, 46, 46, 39 (fp256): the largest deviation 1.37 sigma. 0 wrong unmarked and 0 wrong marked guesses in all 15.
- **Item 4, the structured family** (`python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py family`, 42 s; `mathlib_family.py`): the committed list is the study's census (240 arguments c 2^-e, |c| <= 16, e from p - 10 to p + 3) whose theory distance d - exp(x) to the nearest rounding boundary of the result in units of the nominal bound, mpmath - is under 0.7: 16 centres under rne and rmm and 34 under the directed three at fp64, 16 and 184 at fp128 and fp256, none at fp32. It is generated from the theory alone and the tests hold it to a fresh generation. The run tests every centre with its neighbours at 1, W/8, W/4 and 0.65 W ulps inside its window and 1.35 W, 2 W, 8 W and 1024 W outside it, the census arguments that are not centres and, at fp128 and fp256, the 156 and 528 deep arguments between (p + G)/2 and the census; RESULT: ok in all 20 cells - every lane the theory puts inside (d < 0.7) was marked, none outside (d > 1.3), 0 wrong unmarked. For example fp64 under rtz: 34 centres, 784 lanes, 280 inside and all marked, 433 outside and none marked, 71 between 0.7 and 1.3 of which 42 marked; fp256 under rup: 184 centres, 3,698 lanes, 2,175 inside all marked, 1,492 outside none marked, 31 between of which 15 marked; under rmm: 16 centres, 1,010 lanes, 146 inside all marked, 862 outside none marked, 2 between of which 1 marked; 0 wrong unmarked in every cell. Wrong guesses among the marked: 1 under rne at fp64, fp128 and fp256, none elsewhere. (A first run of this command, before the deep lanes and the 0.65 W and 1.35 W offsets joined it, took 38 s; a later one took 959 s of wall on the busy desktop, niced, for about 45 s of CPU: a niced process on this desktop is starved when others run.)
  - **The census through the fragment** (MEASURED, `census_run`): marked of 240: fp32 0 under every attribute; fp64 (G = 44) 16 under rne and rmm and 39 under the directed three (the study's 23 is at G = 46, READ; the plan's verifier measured 39, the lead's first correction, READ); fp128 and fp256 16 and 184, the study's. The 5 marks of fp64 above the 34 centres have d between 0.7 and 1.3.
  - fp32's census finds no window, as (p + G)/2 = 32 is past p = 24; the theory is not vacuous: at a guard of 16 it finds windows at fp32.
- **Item 5, the constants** (`python -m cft_golden.mathlib --check` from python/, 5.5 s): "mathlib --check: 4 formats, 0 differences": 300, 245, 285 and 350 derived constants in five fragments each (fp32, fp64, fp128, fp256) - the table, the Cody-Waite words, the coefficients, the screens, MAGIC, 8/ln2, 2^-(p+3), 2^-4, 2^-(p+G), the answers of the screens under the attribute - and 315 lanes of the scale, fixed-grid and table words a format. Each constant is checked by asking whether the bits the BUILT fragment holds are what the rounding rule gives for every value of an enclosure of the true number: ln 2 by 2 atanh(1/3) in integers (width 2^-3190), 2^(j/8) by an integer 8th root (2^-1700), 1/(i+1)! exact; the rules (nearest, up, down, truncated to p - nb bits) through `softfloat.next_up` and `next_down` and exact fractions, not the generator's rounding; an enclosure across a boundary is refused, never passed. The scale offsets, the fixed grid's C and u/2 and the table's wiring are run through the fragment's own instructions at 315 lanes against 2^k exactly.

**The planted faults** (`python/tests/test_mathlib.py`, last section; each red check must return a finding beginning with its own name, and each green one nothing). 25 plants in 29 rows, MEASURED red by the check named and green where stated (the run is the test file's, on 4ad5cea's tree plus this parcel): 18 faults of the builder (`mathlib.PLANTS`), one of the budget tool (`mathlib_budget.PLANTS`), two of an independent derivation (`TOOLS`) and four mutations of a fresh build or of its fragment (`MUTATIONS`), none of which touches a module-level cache. The checks a plant is run through are `pools`, `edges` (the thresholds the pools lose, below), `lanes` (60 random and 60 weighted arguments through the pools' comparison, a mark allowed only on the list and every listed lane required to be marked), `bound`, `budget`, `rate`, `family`, `census` (fp32's emptiness), `census_counts` (the census's marks counted, every committed centre among them), `shape` (the pinned instruction, word and live counts), `sums` (the design's eighteen opcodes, and its error-free sums counted), `specialised` (C4's specialised form, and the instrumented form beside it), `fixed_grid` (the fixed grid's rounding on states no argument is known to reach), `spot` (ln 2, the table's high words and the Cody-Waite sum against an enclosure independent of the generator) and `constants`. The comparison found that `shape`, `sums`, `specialised`, `census_counts`, `spot` (then assertions in tests without a plant) and the second branch of `budget` had no fault that made them fail; each has its plants now (the lead's after-end fixes 1), and `fixed_grid` is new. Two tests hold the table to the harness, and each fault below is caught by the one named (MEASURED in a scratch script, each fault applied to the table or the harness and both tests run). `test_every_check_of_the_harness_has_a_plant_that_turns_it_red`: every `check_` function of `mathlib_harness.py` but the helper `check_lanes` (HELPERS, whose findings come through the `pools`, `edges` and `lanes` columns and the seq test) is a column of the table with a plant red in it, or has a plant test of its own; it fails on a table whose rows list no plant red in `spot` and on a check function the table does not name, and the other test passes on both. `test_every_plant_is_in_the_table_and_every_row_names_a_plant`: every plant has a row and every row names a plant; it fails on a row for no plant and on a plant with no row, and the first test passes on both as tried (a row for `ghost_plant`; `odd_dropped`'s, `probe_dropped`'s or `bound_loose`'s rows removed), though not where the plant's rows were a column's only red row, as `bound_wide`'s fp32 row is `census`'s (verifier-VE1-a3; restated by the lead at the merge, by Logan's waiver):
- `table_entry` (T_3's high word one ulp off), at fp64: red in pools, edges, lanes, bound, budget, rate, constants (TH3 and TL3) and spot (2^(3/8) over half an ulp from its table word); green in family, shape, sums, specialised, fixed_grid and census_counts. `c1_ulp`: red in pools, edges, lanes, bound, budget, rate, constants and spot (the Cody-Waite words sum to ln 2/8 1.4e-17 off); green in family and the same five.
- `bound_loose` (Bv 2^-40 smaller): red in bound, budget, rate (0 of 1,000 marked, 22 expected), family, constants and census_counts (2 of the census's 240 marked, 16 expected); green in pools and edges. `bound_wide` (2^16 wider): red in rate (all 1,000), family, constants and fixed_grid (its states have |V_l| = 8 Bv, under the wider bound, so they are marked); green in bound (a wider claimed bound is trivially true) and census_counts. At fp32 `bound_wide` turns the census-empty check red.

- `mark_silenced`: red in pools (the structured lane exp(+-2^-p) is on the list and not marked), rate, family, shape, sums (`ixor` and `abs`, which only the marks use, are gone) and census_counts (0 of 240 marked, a census lane wrong unmarked); green in bound and constants, and, under rdn, in `lanes` (its 120 lanes meet none of the list's 34 centres, MEASURED).
- `rl_through_y` (the study's defect 1: r_l carried through Y(r_h)): red in the bound and the budget and, of the checks of values, in nothing else (an error of 2^33.5 Bv at its worst lane); pools, edges, rate, family, constants green, as the study found; the shape pin sees it too (179 instructions for 180). `c3_dropped` (Cody-Waite in two words): red in bound, budget, constants ("no constant C3"), spot ("no Cody-Waite word C3") and shape; green in pools, edges, rate, family. `head_short` (two fewer head steps): red in bound, budget, constants (the plan), shape and sums (7 Fast2Sums for 9).
- `tiny_gate_off`: red in the pools at rdn, a mark off the list, and in shape; green at rne (V = 1 + Z cannot straddle a midpoint of 1), as the study's table says "under the directed attributes". `screen_ulp`: red in pools, edges, constants. `tininess_klt_only` and `c0_wrong` (the fixed grid's offset 2^-3): red in the edges pool and, for c0_wrong, constants; green in the transcend pools - see the finding below; `tininess_klt_only` is also red in shape and sums (its `cmplt` was the only one). `square_term_dropped` (fp32, the study's defect 7): red in bound (2^+5.0), constants and shape (379 instructions for 382), green in pools and the census.
- **The plants of the checks of the fragment's form** (the lead's after-end fixes 1; the table's rows, the findings quoted from them):

There is no augmented addition to plant: AUGADD and AUGERR are control instructions, which an ALU fragment's body cannot hold, so what the check pins is the opcode set and the counts.

No plant of the builder fires that branch (MEASURED at fp64 and fp128 on the table's lanes: the first branch, a bound not under 1, for table_entry, c1_ulp, bound_loose, rl_through_y and head_short, and for c3_dropped at fp64; nothing for the rest).
- **The fixed grid's rounding** (MEASURED, `check_fixed_grid` and `Build.run(over=...)`, which runs the unpruned body with a probe's value replaced; the lead's after-end fixes 1). States of (V_h, V_l) that no argument is known to reach: at k = emin - p + 1 + g the result's grid, in the scaled domain V lives in, is u = 2^-g, and V_h = 1 + u/2 sits exactly on a half-grid point; V_l = +-8 Bv, so the fixed grid's own test (it marks where |V_l| <= Bv) does not mark, and V_l is under half an ulp of the remainder u/2, so a sum rounded to nearest keeps nothing of it. The fragment's own instructions are run with V_h, V_l and the exponent handed to them (at fp32 V_0, V_1 and V_2 = 0) at g = 16 and 8 and held to the exact rounding of V 2^k under the attribute (`mathlib._enc`), unmarked: right in all 80 states (4 formats, 5 attributes, 2 grids, 2 signs). The plant `odd_dropped` (round-to-odd of V_l's share built as round-to-nearest) is wrong in 16 of them - rne with V_l > 0 and rmm with V_l < 0, at both grids of every format, unmarked: "fixed_grid: fp64 rne k = emin - 36, V_l > 0: the result is 0x10000, the rounding of V 2^k is 0x10001" - and right in the other 64 (the directed three, rne with V_l < 0, rmm with V_l > 0). It is red in shape (176 instructions at fp64 for 180) and in no other check of the table (MEASURED: green in pools, edges, lanes, bound, budget, rate, family, constants, census_counts, sums, specialised, spot, and at fp32 in the census).
- The other checks: the eight invariant clauses each fail on a mutated fragment (the mark bit moved to bit 6; the mark ORed by an add the walk cannot read, flag word None; a foreign attribute; an instruction reading only the input; a SELECT of one value twice; a read before its definition; an unknown word; a result that is an input), the live cap can fail (23 against a cap of 22), seq's comparison sees an evaluator that ignores the attributes, the R24 check sees the first flag-raising instruction left outside the quiet region (the lanes whose stray overflow is not in the operation's flags), the family-list check sees a tampered list, and the `--check` as a program exits 1 with `TH3` named when exp is built with a wrong table word.

**Findings, for the lead** (none changes code outside this parcel).
- **The transcend pools lose their negative thresholds** (MEASURED, test_mathlib's test of it): `python/cft_golden/vectors.py` (`transcend_unary_pool`) and `host/tests/transcend_check.py` (`unary_pool`) take x = n ln2 from `mpmath.libmp.to_man_exp`, which returns the mantissa UNSIGNED, so every negative n comes out positive. The pools hold exp(+708.396...), exp(+744.44...) and exp(+745.13...), overflowing, where exp's underflow argument emin ln2 and its screen (emin - p) ln2 should be, at every format. So the tininess decision at k = emin and the fixed grid's offset were never met by the pools: `tininess_klt_only` and `c0_wrong` pass them and fail `edge_pool`, the thresholds with their signs and the ends of every cell of n. The same call sits at `python/cft_golden/vectors.py` line 599 and `host/tests/transcend_check.py` line 595 for other pools. E1 edits no existing code; `mathlib._frac` reads the sign from the mpf.
- **fp32 fits seq.py's 32 registers by a reorder alone** (MEASURED, `python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py live`, 24 s): emitting each special's condition and the scale words just before their use - the same instructions, the same words, a depth-first order from the flag word and the result, the larger subtree first - takes the live count from 33 or 34 to 25 at fp32 and from 22 or 23 to 11 at fp64, fp128 and fp256, under every attribute; the reordered fp32 fragment is accepted by `routines.program`, which refuses the built one ("no register for the harness"), and on seq.py equals `evaluate` on 165 pool lanes under each attribute (`--lanes 120` took every second lane or so: 123 to 175 lanes a format, all equal). Not applied: `fragment()` returns the study's order, since fp32's fit is M1's build. The reordered exp family's 11 is under C4's `routines.LIVE_MAX` of 16.
- **C4's `routines.invariants` fails these fragments** (MEASURED on exp at fp64 rne): "the flag word's values None are not within [0, 1, 2, 16, 20, 24]" (its walk has no IOR rule), "23 values live at once, past 16", and the RDN and RUP attributes as not the routine's own (and RMM under rmm) - the study's question 12, which `mathlib.invariants` widens; `routines.py` is untouched.

**Known limits, recorded rather than fixed** (Logan's rule).
- The identity with the study's model, and the budget port's with the original's, are scratch comparisons, not reproducible from the tree; what the tree holds is the pinned shape table (this parcel's counts, which the study's agree with where it measured at the same G) and checks that share nothing with the model.
- The larger samples are the lead's, on amd-arc-box: the bound at 10^5 or more lanes a format, the budget at 3,000 lanes a region, the rate law past 2,000 a cell, the exhaustive fp32 sweep. The commands and their costs are in the report; `python/tests/mathlib_runs.py` runs all of them. This entry's samples are the desktop's, at the study's scale.
- The budget is first order and bounds a region as far as its sample reaches the region's extremes (mathlib_budget's docstring; the study's 3.2): VM1d's second-order residue for exp at G = 44 is 6e-5 Bv (READ). The weighted sampler and the placed points reach each path's largest |r|; a lane the sample never meets is not covered by it.
- The mark-rate law is measured at G' = 6 and carried to G = 44 and 46 (BELIEVED): the same instructions run, one bank word, 2^-(p+G), differs.
- **The fixed grid's round-to-odd decides on states that exist, and no argument is known to reach one.** V_h exactly on a half-grid point of the result's grid and Bv < |V_l| < half an ulp of the remainder u/2: the fixed grid's own test does not mark (it marks where |V_l| <= Bv), and round-to-nearest of V_l's share loses V_l, so the tie goes to even (rne) or away from zero (rmm) and is wrong for one sign of V_l; only round-to-odd keeps it. MEASURED here by `check_fixed_grid` (the entry's section above: round-to-nearest wrong in 16 of 80 states, round-to-odd in none), and, READ from the lead's after-end fixes 1, on the fixed grid's own instructions through `softfloat.compute` by the lead's comparison (8 of 16 cases, at fp64 k = emin - 20 and -30 and fp32 k = emin - 5 and -10) and by this arm's verifier (fp64 rne, k = emin - 52, V_h = 1.5, V_l = -2^-60). The first version of this entry (c760d7d) called round-to-odd redundant and round-to-nearest an equivalent mutant, COMPUTED from the code: that was wrong, since the sign of V_l is known wherever |V_l| > Bv. What is not shown is a real argument that reaches such a state: the pools, the random and weighted lanes, the thresholds and the structured family do not (MEASURED: `odd_dropped` is green in all of them). None is expected (COMPUTED, V_l uniform within a rounding cell: the arguments with k <= emin are 2,271,306 at fp32, 3.3e14 at fp64, 5.0e31 at fp128 and 1.4e68 at fp256, and about 3 x 2^-(p+2) of them give such a state, so 0.10, 0.027, 0.0036 and 0.0005 expected); an exhaustive scan of fp32's 2,271,306 arguments, 2.1 ms a lane on this desktop (MEASURED, 2,000 lanes), about 80 minutes, would settle fp32 and was not run. The fixed grid's flags and offsets are held by `tininess_klt_only` and `c0_wrong`.
- fp32's bound is measured at G = 40, no budget: 2^-4.95 at its placed points and 2^-5.66 over 3,000 random (this entry), against the study's 2^-4.7 over 150,000 on the box.
- The quick tests (252): `python -m pytest python/tests/test_mathlib.py python/tests/test_routines.py -q` passed 311 (252 and test_routines.py's 59, in one session, so that nothing here disturbs it) in 232 s niced, and in 82 s at `-n 4` (pytest-xdist 3.8.0). The same 311 passed with the tests collected in reverse order (234 s) and in a seeded shuffle (233 s), and both again at `-n 4` (87 s and 79 s), by a scratch plugin that is not committed; and each of the 67 tests this change added or changed passed alone, in a process of its own (4 minutes in all). The whole golden suite, `python -m pytest python/tests -q -rs --color=no -n 4` niced on the desktop, passed 3,619 with the stage's three known skips (two for the Arduino loopback binary, one `math.fma` on Python 3.13+) in 290 s: 3,622 collected with these 252, against 3,370 before. At this parcel's first commit, c760d7d, the pair was 291 (232 and the 59) in 233 s, and 298 s and 202 s at two earlier states, on a desktop others were using; the largest parts are the 15 rate cells (about 3 s each), the 15 family cells (to 5 s), the plants (29 rows in 65 s) and the constants check (about 5 s). Peak working set of the larger commands, by psutil: 41 MiB for `family`, 33 MiB for the fp256 budget and for the bound and rate commands.
- Thresholds in the tests (`BOUND_ROOM`, `BUDGET_ROOM`) are this parcel's, a bit under what was measured: the fp64 bound keeps at least two bits and the budget under 0.25 Bv there.

## 2026-10-13 - the math library round's experiment E1: exp's routine authored from one brief by Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, verified apart and compared blind; the Sonnet arm merged

**What E1 was.** Logan, on 2026-10-12, verbatim: "Start the math library round's plan, though include an experiment to run first, the first function worked on will have a matching parcel dispatched to an Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 model to perform the parcel work, to see if Sonnet class is capable at this level of work with proper guidance from the lead briefs. If it proves successful, the other parcels for the round may follow similar patterns."
- **The plan of record** is docs/ROADMAP.md's section "The math library: experiment E1, then M1's build and M2 to M4 (plan of record, 2026-10-12)". It sets E1's design, its rubric and its rules for the verdict, and records E1's result.
- **The function was exp** (Logan's choice). The parcel built its routine golden-first in a new module, python/cft_golden/mathlib.py, with the study's section 8, items 1 to 5, as its tests.

**The design** (READ, the plan):
- **One brief, two arms.** Each arm got the same brief, its copies differing only in the clone, branch and ledger names. Each worked in a clone of 4ad5cea with no remote. The two were dispatched at once (15:03, 2026-10-12).
- **A coin** gave one arm to each model, sealed as a salted sha256 until the comparison had reported.
- **Verification:** each arm was checked by its own verifier on Sonnet, from one verifier brief.
- **The lead's common battery:** the same arguments and seeds through each arm's `mathlib.fragment` and `mathlib.evaluate`, against transcend.exp.
- **The comparison:** a third agent on Opus read both arms, exported without git and with commit trailers stripped. It scored them on a five-item rubric, named its cases and the branch to merge, and only then guessed which arm was which model.
- **Sonnet's parcel succeeds when** all three criteria hold:
  1. its arm ends clean within a cap of two send-backs, with at most one more than Opus's arm;
  2. its last verifier finds every must-have met;
  3. it is not materially worse on rubric item 1 (correctness) or item 2 (tests that can fail). That means not more of the cases that the other arm does not share, item by item.

**The plan's own checks** (MEASURED, the round's ledger):
- Nine verifiers checked the plan before and while E1 ran: P7 and P7b on Sonnet, P7c to P7i on Haiku.
- Their (b)s numbered 2, 1, 2, 4, 1, 2, 1, 2 and 0. P7's two were in the plan's first draft and P7b's one was in E1's brief. Every later one was in the lead's own text written to answer the pass before: dates, statements of fact, rules that could not be decided, and lists left incomplete.
- The criteria were revised after dispatch: at 15:48 and 16:14 before either arm had reported, then five more times as the passes found gaps, each before any verifier of an arm had reported. Each is dated in the plan by its commit, the last as the commit that followed P7h (18:34:12 by git).
- **Logan's answer to the first revision:** "Keep the more fair rule you went with". It made "materially worse" a count, item by item, against the other arm's count, where the old rule had failed Sonnet's arm on any case of its own.

**What the authors and the verifiers were told after dispatch** (READ, the briefs):
- **Brief correction 1,** to both arms word for word at 15:44, before either reported. It came from verifier-P7b's check of the brief, and has seven items.
  - Its first item rested on a premise of the lead's, "at fp32 there is no window", which is wrong. The arms' verifiers found a few fp32 arguments that mark, the floats nearest ln(1 + t) for t = 2^-23, 2^-22, 2^-21, -2^-22 and -2^-21: VE1-a all five, VE1-b two of them. Each mark is justified and its guess right.
  - The census, which the item asked about, does find none.
- **A clarification of M4** went to both verifiers at 18:12, word for word.

**Arm a (Sonnet 5.5):**
- **Commits:** c760d7d, then 6c4666e, then two after-end fix commits (below). 162 min.
- **First check:** verifier-VE1-a found no (a) and no (b), with M1 to M7 met. Its own instruments:
  - the fragments are equal to the study's model at all 20 configurations;
  - the budget port is equal to verifier-VM1b's tool on 18,160 contributions;
  - a signed-threshold pool and the true window centres: 0 wrong unmarked lanes;
  - 26 planted constant faults, each red in `--check`.
- **So arm a ended clean at its first check, with 0 send-backs.**

  - CONFIRMED by the lead: for t = -1022 ln 2 the mantissa is non-negative and `_mpf_[0]` is 1.

**Arm b (Opus 5.5):**

**The lead's instruments, the same on both arms** (MEASURED):

A first run on arm a's working tree, while its author was still at work, is set aside.

**The comparison** (Opus, 49 min; its ledger is in the round's scratch records):
- **The two arms built the same fragment.** It is identical at fp64 to fp256. At fp32 it computes the same values, with one adjacent pair of instructions (two SELECTs of the specials) emitted in the other order, so four body entries differ. So every lane, flag word and mark is the same in both.
- **Rubric** (a / b): correctness 3 / 3; tests that can fail 3 / 2; completeness 3 / 3; clarity 2 / 3; honest marks 2 / 3. Totals 13 / 14.

  - on item 1, none;
  - on item 2, checks with no plant: two shared (the shape-count and census-count pins), four in arm a only and three in arm b only.

- **Outside the rubric's case wording,** CONFIRMED by the lead from its reproduction: arm b's tests miss arm a's planted fixed-grid offset at k = emin, which gives wrong unmarked results at fp32, fp64 and fp128. Arm a's tests catch it. Its mirror finding: arm a's tests miss arm b's planted removal of the fixed grid's own test, which it believes reaches no wrong lane at the decided G.

- **The coin, opened after its report:** the line hashes to the sealed value. **Arm a was Sonnet 5.5 and arm b Opus 5.5.** Every response's model in the agents' transcripts agrees. The guess was wrong.

**E1's verdict, the criteria applied as fixed** (COMPUTED from the above):
1. **Met.** Sonnet's arm needed 0 send-backs, Opus's 1.
2. **Met.** VE1-a found M1 to M7 met.
3. **Not met, by the letter.**
   - Item 1: 0 cases each.
   - Item 2: Sonnet's arm has 4 unshared cases and Opus's 3, so Sonnet's count is the larger. All seven are checks with no plant, and none is a wrong answer.

## 2026-10-13 - CI's golden job runs test_transcend.py: its gmpy2 skip narrowed to the one test that calls MPFR, and the job installs gmpy2 2.2.1 (the lead's fix CG)

**What was wrong** (READ and MEASURED):
- **CI's golden job** (.github/workflows/gates.yml) installed pytest and mpmath, then ran `python -m pytest python/tests -q`. It installed nothing else in any version of the workflow before this fix: verifier-VIE1d read the job's two lines unchanged in all thirteen, 644ee2d (2026-08-28) to 5246ad0 (2026-09-25), the last before bcf36ac.
- **test_transcend.py** opened its section 4 with `gmpy2 = pytest.importorskip("gmpy2", reason="gmpy2/MPFR not installed")` at line 608, there since the file was created (788708b, 2026-09-02; VIE1d). A module-level importorskip skips the module whole at collection. So on a host without gmpy2 none of the file's 884 tests ran, though only one test calls MPFR: test_mpfr_parity, 16 cases (four formats, four attributes).
- **test_mathlib.py's tests reach it too:** mathlib_harness.py's `pools()` imports `_brute_pool` from it. Since E1's merge (b9d96be), 77 of test_mathlib.py's 252 tests skipped by name on such a host (verifier-VIE1, MEASURED).
- **CI's logs show both** (READ, the golden job's log of each run, through `gh api repos/loganw234/cft-fp256/actions/jobs/<id>/logs`):
  - run 38305163767 at 0893b2c: "2484 passed, 3 skipped in 681.08s (0:11:21)";
  - run 38399252055 at bcf36ac: "2659 passed, 80 skipped in 614.05s (0:10:14)".
  - COMPUTED, the 80: test_mathlib.py's 77, the two tests that need the Arduino loopback binary, and test_transcend.py's module, counted once. 2,659 + 80 = 2,739, the 2,738 tests collected without gmpy2 plus the module. The desktop's third skip, test_softfloat.py's math.fma test, needs Python 3.13+, which CI runs.
- **Found** by the math library round's verifiers: VIE1 the 77, VIE1c the module's skip and the 2,738. VIE1d confirmed "never" from the histories of the workflow and of the line, and from CI's logs.

**The fix** (ad7c409, branch ci-golden; its import made strict after verifier-VCG, in the commit that restates this entry):
- **test_transcend.py:** gmpy2 is imported in a try block. Without it, test_mpfr_parity skips by name, with the old reason, and nothing else does.
  - The except clause catches ModuleNotFoundError, which is what a missing package raises. pytest 9.1.1's importorskip skipped on it and failed on a plain ImportError (MEASURED: the lead's first probe raised ImportError, and bcf36ac's collection ended with an error, not a skip).
  - **verifier-VCG's (b):** at ad7c409 the clause caught every ModuleNotFoundError. So a gmpy2 package whose compiled module is missing, which raises `No module named 'gmpy2.gmpy2'`, skipped test_mpfr_parity, where ad7c409's message and its comment said a broken gmpy2 still fails at collection. VCG reproduced it with a fake package, and with the desktop's Python 3.13.5 importing Miniconda's 3.12 gmpy2. bcf36ac skipped the whole module in that case.
  - **Since the restating commit,** the clause re-raises unless the module missing is gmpy2 itself. MEASURED, collecting test_transcend.py with gmpy2 present, absent, raising a plain ImportError, and as a package without its compiled module: 884, 884, an error and an error (rc 0, 0, 2 and 2). Run: present "884 passed in 15.97s"; absent "868 passed, 16 skipped in 29.26s", the 16 "SKIPPED [16] python\tests\test_transcend.py:705: gmpy2/MPFR not installed".
- **gates.yml's golden job:** installs `gmpy2==2.2.1` beside pytest and mpmath, then imports it in a step of its own that prints gmpy2's, MPFR's and GMP's versions. A gmpy2 that does not load fails the job there, where test_mpfr_parity would only skip.
  - 2.2.1 is the desktop's, with MPFR 4.2.1 and GMP 6.3.0 (MEASURED).
  - PyPI lists gmpy2-2.2.1-cp313-cp313-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl (READ, PyPI's JSON for the release), so the job builds nothing.
  - The latest gmpy2 is 2.3.2 (READ). With the pin, CI's MPFR is the desktop's; moving it is a change of its own.
- **Why both halves:**
  - Installing gmpy2 alone would have left every other host without it skipping 868 tests that need no MPFR, and test_mathlib.py's 77.
  - Narrowing the skip alone would have left test_mpfr_parity unrun on CI.

**What was run** (MEASURED):

## 2026-10-13 - the transcendental pools' lost signs: 3,500 signed cases added to the twenty transcendental sets, the pool generators made independent of mpmath's version, and the conformance profile's minor step to 3.1 (parcel PS)

**Why.**
- Parcel E1 (the math library's first routine, above) found that the two unary transcendental pools lose the sign of every negative threshold n ln2, and the lead confirmed it on 2026-10-12: both generators take x = n ln2 from `mpmath.libmp.to_man_exp`, whose mantissa is unsigned by default, and test its sign, which is never negative. So exp's underflow edges, emin ln2 and (emin - p) ln2, were in no exp-family pool (exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p, log2, log10) and in none of those functions' published sets, at any profile through 3.
- Logan, 2026-10-13, asked which way the fix should step the profile. His answer, verbatim: "Add signed cases, 3.1 (Recommended)". The option's text: "Keep every recorded case and add the 25 signed threshold arguments each pool lacks: 175 more cases in each of the 20 transcendental sets, 3,500 in all. CONFORMANCE.md's rule makes an addition that changes no recorded case a minor step, 3.0 to 3.1. Profile-3 certificates stay covered; the golden corpus is re-made at 3.1, as it was at profile 3." The other two options were replacing the positive images with the signed ones (a major step, 4) and leaving the sets at profile 3 (READ, the lead's ledger).
- Brief correction 1 (the lead, after verifier-VCG's trace of CI's 64 warnings): CI's golden job installs mpmath unpinned, 1.4.1 there and 1.3.0 on the desktop, and mpmath 1.4 deprecates `to_man_exp`'s unsigned default ("Returning unsigned mantissa value per default is deprecated", 64 warnings at ad7c409: 8 n, 4 formats, 2 sites). Under an mpmath that returns it signed, the old code's `1 if man < 0 else 0` would give the signed images in place of the positive ones, and the published sets would move with the version of mpmath that generated them. The fix therefore had to make every generator independent of it.

**PS: the fix and profile 3.1** (branch pools-sign from bcf36ac: 18da8ce, then this entry's commit). Authored by parcel PS, Sonnet 5.5.
- **What was wrong (MEASURED, an oracle of my own):** n ln2 rounded to nearest even from GNU MPFR (two working precisions) and from mpmath (a third), the three equal for every n and format, the encodings written out by hand. At bcf36ac, at every format and in each of `vectors.transcend_unary_pool` (at the sets' counts), `host/tests/transcend_check.py`'s `unary_pool` (at the stage's) and `mathlib_harness.pools`: the 15 images of the positive n (emax, emax + 1, p + 1) 15 of 15 present, the 25 signed images of the five negative n (emin, emin - man_w, emin - man_w - 1, -(p + 2), -(p + 3), each with its neighbours at +-1 and +-2 ulps) 0 of 25 present, their 25 positive mirrors 25 of 25 present. The lead's figure, reproduced. Pool sizes at bcf36ac: the vector sets' 220, 257, 336, 498 (fp32, fp64, fp128, fp256), the stage's 256, 293, 324, 486, E1's union 330, 367, 350, 512.
- **The fix:** the two unary pools read the sign from the mpf's raw tuple, `sign, man, ex, _bc = (mpf(n) * log(2))._mpf_`, and for a negative n put both images in, the positive one they always held and the signed one, with the same neighbours; no image left. After it the pools are 245, 282, 361, 523, 281, 318, 349, 511 and E1's union 355, 392, 375, 537, and (MEASURED, element by element) the new pool is the old one and exactly the 25 signed images at every format, in all three. The two hyperbolic pools took the same dead sign test but add `b + d` and `(b + d) | sign_mask` for every image, so their sets were right; the code now takes the magnitude (the raw mantissa, its sign flag discarded by name) and adds both signs by the mask, and MEASURED each is equal before and after at every format, element for element and by digest.
- **The generators no longer depend on mpmath (correction 1):** none of the four calls `to_man_exp`, whose default is unsigned in 1.3 and deprecated in 1.4; the raw tuple's mantissa is unsigned in every version. MEASURED: an AST scan finds no name, attribute or import `to_man_exp` in any file under python/ or host/tests/ (comments and docstrings aside), where bcf36ac has four calls (vectors.py lines 278 and 599, transcend_check.py lines 259 and 595); and all 16 pools (unary and hyperbolic, the sets' generators and the stage's, four formats) made again with `mpmath.libmp.to_man_exp` replaced by a function that raises, and by the signed convention of 1.4's `signed=True`, equal the pools made with the real one - while bcf36ac's generators fail both (the raising stub trips on their first call; under the signed convention the positive images of the negative thresholds drop out of the pool, at fp32 from index 60, where 0x41902cb1, -(p + 2) ln2 less two ulps, is gone, and the signed images take their places at the top). The same 50 tests pass with gmpy2 blocked, on mpmath's pure-Python backend, so the pools do not depend on the backend either. A simulation of another mpmath, not one: 1.4.1 is not installed here, and installing it is a download. Why it matters to the profile's identity: a profile is the sets' digests, so the sets must be a function of the model and the generator and of no library's version. A pool that calls `to_man_exp` and tests its sign makes them a function of mpmath's.
- **The other sites** (READ, grep for `to_man_exp`, `man < 0`, `._mpf_`, `as_mantissa_exp`, `as_integer_ratio`, `1 if ... < 0 else 0`): `mathlib.py`'s `_frac` reads the sign from the raw tuple, right; `bindings/python/cftmpfr/core.py` (`from_mpfr`) reads the sign by `is_signed`, right; `python/tests/test_transcend.py`'s MPFR helper applies `abs` and `as_mantissa_exp` inside a p-bit context, right; `host/tools/gen_2opi.py` line 99 and `gen_mp_consts.py` line 60 call `to_man_exp` on positive constants after `assert man > 0`, unaffected by a signed default (they would print the deprecation warning); `docs/studies/m1/m1const.py` line 15 and `vm1b/vm1blib.py` line 43 drop a negative mpf's sign and no caller passes one (READ: every mpf they take is positive). The last four are outside python/ and host/tests/ and untouched.

**The vectors (MEASURED, the Makefile's parameters).**
- **The old generation**, from an export of bcf36ac, niced, `--jobs 4`, 2 min 15 s: 168 files, 1,068,915 lines, and `sed 's#  #  out/#' SHA256SUMS | diff vectors/SHA256SUMS -` empty: the unmodified code regenerates all 168 pins on this desktop (Python 3.12.9, mpmath 1.3.0).
- **The new generation**, `make vectors PYTHON=<Miniconda python>`, niced, 1 min 53 s, and again on the corrected generators, 1 min 43 s: 1,072,415 lines, 168 sets, `sha256sum -c` all OK, the two generations equal. Against the profile's record exactly 20 lines differ: the twenty transcendental sets (`fpN-transcend.jsonl` and `fpN-transcend-<rnd>.jsonl`, four formats, five attributes); the other 148 sets are byte for byte equal.
- **Each moved set against its old generation:** the old lines are an in-order subsequence of the new (none changed, none gone) and 175 are added, 25 for each of exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p, log2, log10 at exactly the 25 signed images; the hyperbolic functions gain none. Lines a set, old to new: fp32 21,964 to 22,139; fp64 34,655 to 34,830; fp128 23,850 to 24,025; fp256 26,184 to 26,359, at all five attributes. 20 x 175 = 3,500; 1,068,915 + 3,500 = 1,072,415. The lead's COMPUTED figures are the measured ones. vectors/SHA256SUMS moves by 20 lines.
- **What the new cases are:** fp64 exp at emin ln2 = 0xc086232bdd7abcd2 gives 0x001000000000007c, just above the smallest normal, flags 0x10, and so do the two arguments below it (0x...047c, 0x...027c); the two arguments above it give 0x000ffffffffffe7c and 0x000ffffffffffc7c, subnormal, flags 0x18: the tininess boundary of exp is in the sets. At (emin - p) ln2 the results go from the smallest subnormal to +0, flags 0x18. The log family at a negative argument is the invalid NaN (flags 0x1), expm1 is -1 inexact, exp2 a finite value.
- **They agree** (MEASURED, no disagreement to report): the 3,500 new lines through libcft (`cft.dll`, transcend_check's binding), 3,500 of 3,500; against GNU MPFR through gmpy2, an oracle of mine apart from test_transcend.py (value and inexact and overflow from a p-bit context with the format's range, NaN as invalid, underflow as 754 has it with tininess after rounding from a second context, the rmm lines against the rne oracle, no function value at these arguments being a tie), 3,500 of 3,500; the same oracle on an even spread of about 330 old lines of each moved set, 5,104 of 5,104 (1,276 rmm lines skipped: exp2 at an integer is an exact tie under rmm, profile 3's case) and libcft 6,605 of 6,605; `host/tests/transcend_check.py --formats fp64`, 28 s: 197,340 comparisons, C equal to the model on every one (196,465 at bcf36ac; the difference, 875, is 25 images x 7 functions x 5 attributes). No new mark: test_mathlib's twenty pool cells hold with the marked set unchanged.

**The tests (MEASURED).**
- **`python/tests/test_pool_signs.py` (new, 50 tests, 3 s, mpmath only, so it runs where gmpy2 is absent):** an oracle apart from the pools' code (ln2 from mpmath at 8p + 128 bits, an exact integer product, the sign n's own, `round_pack`), pinned to MPFR's encodings of emin ln2 and (emin - p) ln2 at every format; the signed images in both unary pools at every format; the fp64 example with the encodings written out (-1022 ln2 is 0xc086232bdd7abcd2, and +1022 ln2 still there); the positive images kept; each unary pool less its 25 images equal to profile 3's by digest (the structured part, extra = 0, MEASURED at bcf36ac); both hyperbolic pools both signs and unchanged by digest; the AST scan; the two stub runs. 13 of the 50 fail on bcf36ac's generators, by name: the signed-image tests (8), the fp64 tests (2), the AST scan, and both stub runs. Five planted faults, each in a scratch tree made from bcf36ac's export plus the fixed code with one fault, each turning the right tests red and no others: the one-line repair that drops the positive images (18: the positive-image, digest and fp64 tests), a hyperbolic pool losing a sign (16), a signed image for emin alone (8), a hyperbolic refactor that reads n's sign (16), a hyperbolic site back on `to_man_exp` (2: the scan and the raising stub).
- **E1's tests:** `POOL_SIZES` 355, 392, 375, 537; `test_the_pools_lose_their_negative_thresholds_and_the_edge_pool_has_them`, which pinned the bug and failed at once, rewritten and renamed `test_the_pools_and_edge_pool_hold_both_signs_of_each_negative_threshold` (all four formats, all five n; red on bcf36ac, green now); and one row of the plant table: `tininess_klt_only` (tininess decided on k alone) was listed with the pools among the checks that stay green, because no pool held emin ln2, and the pools now catch it (two unmarked lanes differ from transcend.exp, the first emin ln2 + 1 ulp, flags 0x10 against 0x18), so its row moves them to red. The docstrings that called the bug current are restated: `mathlib.py`'s `_frac`, `mathlib_harness.py`'s `edge_pool`, `test_mathlib.py`'s. `test_mathlib.py` 252 passed, 82 s at `-n 4`; python/tests collects 3,672 (3,622 at E1's merge).
- **The profile-naming tests:** `test_cert2.py` and `test_cert.py` 206 passed, unchanged by the step (they take the profile from profile.py); but "a profile-3 certificate stays covered" had no end-to-end test, only `cert2.covers` on explicit tuples. **Profile 3.1, a minor step by CONFORMANCE.md's rule (an addition that changes no recorded case).** Files: `python/cft_golden/profile.py` (VERSION (3, 1)); `host/include/cft.h` (CFT_PROFILE_MINOR 1, the ABI staying 0.18) and its Arduino copy and `bindings/arduino/vendor.json` (`sync.py --check`: 35 vendored files, all identical to host/); `vectors/SHA256SUMS` (20 lines); `CONFORMANCE.md` (the header, the test's count, the minor-step rule's examples, the note for 3.1 with Logan's decision in his words and the version-independence of the sets, profile 3 kept as history, the ABI paragraph); the golden corpus made again at 3.1; `docs/CERTIFICATES.md`, `COMPATIBILITY.md` (a section for 3.1, no ABI step), `HOSTAPI.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`, `DETERMINISM.md`, `EMBEDDED.md`, `SEQUENCER.md`, `verify/README.md`, `README.md` and the Arduino library's README, `cft_replay.h` and VectorReplay example, for the published count and the profile; docs/README.md recounted.

## 2026-10-13 - M2's design study, sin, cos and tan as tile routines: one Payne-Hanek reduction for every lane, carried exactly through the cancellation, 2/pi in bank words picked by a SELECT shifter, fp64's whole range and fp128's and fp256's to 2^1024, measured in a model; twelve questions for Logan (parcel M2S)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "M2, M3 and M4"): M2 starts as a design study like M1's, golden-first, measured in a model, its questions to Logan before its build: fp64's full range, a stated range at fp256 with 2^1024's cost measured, an L3 rule for each function.
- Logan, verbatim, on the round's extent (2026-10-12): "Hold once E1 finishes to determine how M1 + M2 will utilize models, M2-M4 builds becoming their own round"; on the models (2026-10-13): "Use Sonnet for M1's build parcels as you recommended, it performed well." The recommendation he accepted put M2's study on Opus, with Sonnet verifiers. So the study runs now, beside M1's build, and M2's build is a round of its own.

**M2S** (branch m2-study from 1337a13; authored by parcel M2S, Opus 5.5): docs/studies/M2-trig.md, and its Python model with every run's output as captured in docs/studies/m2/. Nothing is built: no file under python/, host/, rtl/ or tb/ changed, and nothing in the tree imports the model.

**What it designs (PROPOSED).**
- One fragment shape for sin, cos and tan in C4's form, inlined, quiet, raising transcend.py's flags, with bit 7 where M1's in-lane test cannot decide (Bv = 2^-(p+G) |V_h|, since V may be negative).
- **The reduction:** Payne-Hanek for every lane down to the tiny gate, and no Cody-Waite path, since with no branch a second reduction only adds its instructions (|x| < pi/4 takes r = |x| for 5). 2/pi in bank words of b bits (44, 108 and 233 at fp64, fp128 and fp256), the window picked from the exponent by a SELECT log-shifter, no scratch slot. The sum runs in units where every product has a fixed grid, so the generator proves each exact sum before any lane runs, the cancellation happens in an exact part, and an audit checks every claimed-exact instruction lane by lane.
- **Ranges:** fp64's whole (1,232 bits of 2/pi in 28 words, 30 with two zero words); fp128 and fp256 to 2^1024, a lane past it marked and replayed (certificate version 2's question 3).
- Taylor S(z) = sin r / r and C(z) = cos r with double-word heads of 8 steps and no table; tan by its own double-word quotient (19 to 23 instructions), not C4's division; the clamp |sin x|, |cos x| < 1 (Hermite-Lindemann, 4 instructions); G = 44 at fp64 and 46 at fp128 and fp256, M1's.
- fp32: the double word reaches G = 18 only; the triple word at G = 40, Logan's for M1's library, is not built (an ESTIMATE, about 930 instructions for sin).
- The language's three nodes (sin(0), cos(0) and tan(0) fold; every other constant argument `irrational-constant`), cftc's targets and versions, and the L3 rules `cos(a) * da`, `(-sin(a)) * da` and `fma(r, r, 1) * da`, with the pendulum as the committed reference.

**MEASURED in the model** (the desktop, niced, one process at a time; the runs and their times in the round's ledger, ledger/M2S.md, and the batch logs beside the model, `docs/studies/m2/queue*.log`; every cited run on the final model, whose 45 default fragments hash the same before and after the last batch of re-runs):
- **The pools against transcend.py,** on the model and as programs on seq.py through `routines.program` and `routines.run`: fp32 (the double word) 760 arguments, fp64 4,408, fp128 620, fp256 614, all 60 configurations: 0 wrong unmarked lanes, 0 lanes where seq.py and the model differ. The marks: the structured lanes, and at fp128 and fp256 the 282 to 293 lanes past 2^1024.
- **The specials,** nine rows of arguments a function at all four formats and five attributes: equal in bits and flag word. The flag word's values, by C4's walk on all 60 fragments: at most {0x0, 0x1, 0x10, 0x18, 0x90} (cos without 0x18).
- **The reduction against exact rationals,** with the audit: fp64 3,853 arguments and 1,844 binade edges, r's error at most 2^-7.90 of the bound; fp128 676 and 632, 2^-50.90 and 2^-56.43; fp256 434 and 302, 2^-189.59 and 2^-181.91; the quadrant never off, 0 audit failures.
- **The bound,** verifier-VM1b's first-order budget, ported, with three extensions (a negation by the sign word is continuous; the reduction's error-free phases frozen whole; a RECIP_SEED's source not frozen), over five regions: at most 0.096 Bv at fp64 (tan at the edge, its second-order residual at most 0.0125 beside it), 0.073 at fp128, 0.166 at fp256 (the box's larger budgets, below: 0.100, 0.0729 and 0.1663); at G = 46 fp64 would keep 0.26 for sin and cos and 0.36 for tan; fp32's double word at G = 18 0.33 to 0.39 for sin and cos and 0.53 to 0.61 for tan (residual up to 0.12).
- **Errors against mpmath at 4p + 200 bits** (6,000 arguments a function and format in five regions, and the pools' main lanes): largest 2^-4.35 Bv at fp64, 2^-3.91 at fp128, 2^-2.80 at fp256 and 2^-2.08 at fp32's double word; 0 wrong. Three of the 45 cells with a budget of their own pass the study's own bound: fp128 cos random, 0.0612 Bv against 0.0541; fp128 sin small, 0.0142 against 0.0036; fp256 tan near, 0.0954 against 0.0941 (the 400-lane budgets and the sparse "small" region missed lanes near |r| = pi/4). The box's larger budgets bound all 45, those three at 0.0724, 0.0679 and 0.1391.

**What was built** (six files changed, none added; this entry; docs/README.md recounted; a dated note in the study; VERIFICATION's golden row).
- `python/cft_golden/mathlib.py` (2,349 lines at the commit that carries this entry, 2,347 at 3f24cc9 before two comments were corrected; 1,778 at 1337a13): `NAMES = ("exp", "exp2", "expm1")`; `build(name, fmt, rnd, ...)` with `build_exp`, `build_exp2` and `build_expm1`; one double-word builder `_build_dw(fn, ...)` and one triple-word builder `_build_tw(fn, ...)`, the sections the three share (classify, the scale words, the fixed grid, the final rounding and the specials, the table, exp2's exact flag) written once as helpers, so that fp32's cannot drift from fp64's; `Build.two_diff` (TwoSum with the second operand given negated); `plan_exp(fmt, G, rel_z)` and `plan_exp32(fmt, G, rel_z)`; the scheduler (`schedule_order`, `permuted`) and `dag_digest`; `PLANTS`, 31 faults of the builder (E1's 18 and 13 more); `LIVE_CAP`; `check_constants(builder, formats, attrs, names)` and `--check`, generalised to the routine.
- `python/tests/test_mathlib.py` (835 tests, 49 test functions; E1's 38 functions are in it: 6 as they were, 26 generalised to a routine parameter with exp one of its cells, 6 replaced - the list is under the known limits), `mathlib_harness.py` (the lanes, the samplers, the edge pools and the checks, each routine through its own `fn`; the new checks `reorder` and `nofamily`), `mathlib_family.py` (the theory and the committed centres, `FAMILY` generated and now {routine: {format: {attribute: [centre]}}}), `mathlib_budget.py` (the true value per routine), `mathlib_runs.py` (`--fn` on every command; the new `sweep`; `live` is the reorder's).
- No file added or changed imports anything from `docs/studies/`; mathlib.py imports `hashlib`, `heapq` and `types` beside what it had.

**fp32's fit to the register file, and the reorder.**
- **In the design's order** (the study's, which both of E1's authors found a reorder of: their reports, READ) the triple-word routines keep 33 to 36 values live and the double word's 22 to 25 (MEASURED, `python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py live`, 119 s). `routines.program` places a fragment in seq.py's 32 registers by first free, so a count past 32 is refused: in the design's order it refuses all 15 fp32 fragments ("no register for the harness") and accepts all 45 others.
- **The scheduler** (`Build.fragment()`, `schedule_order`) takes the specialised body and emits the same instructions in the lower-peak of two topological orders: by phase (Kahn's algorithm, taking of the instructions ready the one of the earliest phase in `PHASE_ORDER`: the reduction first and whole, since it collapses many partial sums into a few words, then the polynomial, the table, the reconstruction, the scale words, the grid, the final rounding, the classification last) and by depth (E1-a's order: a depth-first walk from the flag word and the result, the larger subtree first). Neither is optimal and none is claimed to be. MEASURED (scratch, before it was built, on exp under rne at fp32 and fp64): the phase order keeps 19 live at fp32 and 14 at the double word, the depth-first 25 and 11, a list scheduler taking the fewest live after each step 30 and 22, an eager reduction then depth-first 23 and 11: the two orders are complementary, which is why both are tried. The instrumented `Build` keeps the design's order (the budget and the probes read it).
- **Scheduled**: exp 19 live at fp32 and 11 at fp64, fp128 and fp256; exp2 20 and 13; expm1 21 and 13 (MEASURED, `python -m cft_golden.mathlib`, and pinned per fragment in `SHAPE`). `LIVE_CAP` is 21 at fp32 and 13 at the others, the largest of each column, so that a growth is a change to look at (the comment above it says so); it leaves 11 and 19 of seq.py's 32 registers. BELIEVED, not shown: the triple word's state (three words each of y, Z and T and the reconstruction's running sums) is most of fp32's count; I did not look for a smaller one.
- **Nothing but the order moved**, shown five ways (the claim "change no value"):
  - the order-free digest of the dataflow graph (`dag_digest`: each instruction hashed from its opcode, attribute and what its operands hash to, words by their bits; the sorted hashes and the result and flag word's hashed again) of the scheduled fragment equals that of the design's order in all 60 fragments (`live`, and `test_the_scheduled_fragment_is_the_designs_reordered`);
  - exp's 20 digests equal the 20 that the same function gives the fragments of the exported 1337a13 tree (MEASURED, a scratch export of that commit; pinned in the tests as `EXP_DIGESTS`), so exp's instructions are E1's operand for operand and attribute for attribute;
  - exp's lanes: 3,390 arguments (the pools, E1's edge pool, 80 random and 80 weighted a format) through the 1337a13 tree's fragments and through this tree's, bits and flag word, five attributes: 16,950 lane-attribute pairs, 0 differ (MEASURED, scratch `compare_base.py`, 28 s); the shapes agree in instructions and words and differ in values live, 34 to 19 at fp32 and 23 to 11 at the others for rne;
  - each of the 60 scheduled fragments equals its design-order twin, in bits and flag word, on 269 to 392 pool lanes (fp256's pool at every second lane), and runs on seq.py through `routines.program` and `routines.run` equal to `evaluate` on the same lanes (MEASURED, `live`, 119 s: 60 of 60 on each of the three);
  - E1's own tests of exp, with E1's own support modules, pass against this tree's mathlib.py: 175 of its 252, every test of exp's values (the 77 that fail pin the design's live counts or fp32's refusal, or call an API this parcel generalised; the list is under the known limits).
