**The design as built** (READ: docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, sections 2.2, 2.5, 3.1, 4 and 5.1, and the model in docs/studies/m1/m1exp.py and m1exp32.py).
- **exp2** is the study's: the screens x >= emax + 1 and x <= emin - p, both integers and exact bank words; `t = fma(x, 8, M)`, n = t - M (n = round(8x), exact, since 8x is x with its exponent moved), r' = fma(n, -1/8, x) (exact: x and n/8 are multiples of x's ulp and |r'| <= 1/16), r_h = r' LN2H and r_l from two FMAs (TwoProd against ln 2's high word, the low word added once): 7 instructions with the negation, against exp's 14 (MEASURED, `Build.phase_of`, the "reduce" phase, fp64 rne). The table, the polynomial (K = 7, D = 12, 20 and 33 at fp64, fp128 and fp256: exp's plan, since |r| is exp's bound), Z, the reconstruction, the in-lane test and the fixed grid are exp's, one code path. An integer x is exact: r' = 0 and j = 0 (r' = 0 alone is every x = j/8: the study's defect 6, plant `exact_no_j`), the flag word zeroed, so such a lane is neither inexact nor marked, down to 2^(emin - man_w).
  - **The tie at emin - p** is the one thing not ported as the study has it. The screen `x <= emin - p` answers a quarter of the smallest subnormal, which rounds to +0 under rmm; but 2^(emin - p) is exactly half of it, the tie between +0 and the smallest subnormal, and roundTiesToAway gives the subnormal. transcend.exp2 has given the subnormal, flags 0x18, since parcel XT (profile 3). The builder answers that one lane apart, only under rmm: `bits = select(INT1, bits, x == XUNF)` (the smallest subnormal's encoding is the integer 1; two instructions, no new word). MEASURED: the routine equals transcend.exp2 at x = emin - p under all five attributes at all four formats (+0, +0, +0, the subnormal, the subnormal; flags 0x18), unmarked; the lane is in the pools at every format; plant `tie_screen` (the model's screen) is red in `pools` and `edges`.
- **expm1** is the study's: the reduction of exp (Cody-Waite in three words, ln2/8); K = 8, D = 13, 20 and 33 at fp64, fp128 and fp256 (the plan with one factor rho fewer, `plan_exp(rel_z=True)`: the n = 0 lanes are bounded relative to Z); V' = T (1 + Z) - 2^-k with T_h - 2^-k by TwoSum (`Build.two_diff`), 2^-k built from n's integer encoding and taken as 0 beyond k = p + G + 2, and the Fast2Sum of the sum with T_h Z_h ordered because |T_h - 2^-k| >= |T Z| for every n but 0 (the study's 2.2 says "in every case", READ; COMPUTED here from the table: the base is 0.0905 at n = 1 and -0.166 at n = -1 against |T Z| under 0.049 and 0.082, and larger beyond), while at n = 0 the base is exactly 0 and the Fast2Sum is exact in any order (the first version of the builder's comment said "|base| >= |P| in every case"; it is corrected in this parcel's last commit); Bv = 2^-(p+G) |V_h| (V_h is negative for x < 0); no fixed grid, since a result off the tiny path is never subnormal; the tiny path `fma(x, x, x)` for |x| < 2^-(p+2) with its underflow cases (|x| < 2^emin, and x = -2^emin under rtz and rup); the clamp to -1 for x <= RD(-(p+2) ln 2), -(1 - 2^-p) under rtz and rup; and question 12's one instruction, `ior(x, ZERO)` as the tiny path's first operand, so that no instruction reads only the input (`invariants` finds none).
- **fp32's exp2 and expm1 are new design** (the study models only exp there; its 2.5 estimates the others at about twice fp64's cost).
  - exp2: r' exact as above; r = r' ln 2 as three words from ln 2 in three words L0, L1, L2 (each the nearest to what the ones before leave): P0 + e0 = r' L0 and P1 + e1 = r' L1 by TwoProd, P2 = r' L2 rounded; e0 + P1 by TwoSum (u0 + u1), P2 + u1 + e1 by two rounded adds, then a Fast2Sum of P0 and u0 (ordered: |u0| < 2.5 2^-25 |P0| by COMPUTED) and a TwoSum for (r0, r1, r2): 26 instructions against exp's 42 (MEASURED, `Build.phase_of`, the "reduce" phase, fp32 rne). What the three words leave of r (COMPUTED from the constants and the term sizes, |r'| <= 1/16): the two rounded adds of the level-2 terms err by 2^-77 at most (u1 is 2^-53 at most), and the dropped r'(ln 2 - L0 - L1 - L2) and the rounding of P2 are 2^-82.1 and 2^-81.3 at most (ln 2 - L0 - L1 - L2 is 2^-78.1), against the bound's 2^-64; the measured bound below is the check. The rest is exp's triple-word body (K3, K2, D = 3, 4, 9: exp's plan).
  - expm1: exp's five-word reduction; the plan (K3, K2, D) = (4, 3, 9) (`plan_exp32(rel_z=True)`: one factor rho fewer); T_0 - 2^-k by TwoSum, its error joined by a TwoSum to the running sum at the level of the table's second word, and the Fast2Sum of the first word valid for the reason above; the rest exp's.
  - Fast2Sums and TwoSums (MEASURED, `Build.meta`), fp32: 21 and 15 (exp2), 22 and 23 (expm1), against exp's 20 and 18; the double word: 9 and 0 (exp2), 10 and 2 (expm1), against exp's 9 and 1. No augmented addition anywhere (an ALU body cannot hold one).

- **Item 5, the constants** (`python -m cft_golden.mathlib --check` from python/, 14 s): "mathlib --check: 3 routines, 4 formats, 0 differences". exp and exp2 hold 300, 245, 285 and 350 derived constants in five fragments each (fp32, fp64, fp128, fp256), expm1 307, 257, 292 and 357, and 315 lanes of the scale, fixed-grid, 2^-k and table words a format for exp and exp2, 535 for expm1. Each constant is checked as E1's were: whether the bits the BUILT fragment holds are what the rounding rule gives for every value of an enclosure of the true number (ln 2 by 2 atanh(1/3) in integers, 2^(j/8) by an integer 8th root, 1/(i+1)! exact), the rules through `softfloat.next_up` and `next_down` and exact fractions, never the generator's rounding. New: exp2's words (the negated low word of ln 2 as the rule rn gives it, in three words at fp32), expm1's clamp constants (M1B, the answer -1 or -(1 - 2^-p) under the attribute, and the clamp's K_CLAMP word), the tiny path's NMINN, and 2^-k and its clamp run through the fragment's own instructions at k = -(p + 3) to p + 1, the clamp - 2 to the clamp + 2 and the clamp + 4, with the scale words against 2^k exactly. It fails with the word named when a build has a wrong one: `table_entry` at TH3 (exp), `ln2_ulp` at LN2H (exp2) and `c1_ulp` at NC1 (expm1), `--check` as a program exiting 1.
  - The first run of this check found my slip: exp2's double-word builder holds only the NEGATED low word of ln 2 (NLN2L), and the check, which asks the BUILT fragment, answered "the fragment has no constant LN2L"; it now asks for NLN2L (rule rn, negated).

**The planted faults** (`python/tests/test_mathlib.py`, last section; each red check must return findings that all begin with its own name, and each green one nothing). 38 plants in 84 rows (exp 32, exp2 24, expm1 28; E1's were 25 plants in 29 rows): 31 faults of the builder (`mathlib.PLANTS`: E1's 18 and 13 new), one of the budget tool (`mathlib_budget.PLANTS`), two of an independent derivation (`TOOLS`) and four mutations of a fresh build or of its fragment (`MUTATIONS`). None touches a module-level cache, so every test passes alone, in any order and under pytest-xdist. The table's reds and greens are what the file's tests pin; the red sets below are what the table pins, and the "map" figures are fuller sets from the scratch measurement described next.
- **The checks.** E1's fifteen - `pools`, `edges`, `lanes`, `bound`, `budget`, `rate`, `family`, `census`, `census_counts`, `shape`, `sums`, `specialised`, `fixed_grid`, `spot`, `constants` - and two new. `reorder`: the scheduled fragment is the design's order's, reordered and nothing more - the same instruction and word counts, a topological order, the same order-free digest of the dataflow graph, and no more values live. `nofamily`, exp2's: the census, the deep arguments and the floats next to the integers 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16, 100, p and -emin (both signs, 1 to 8 ulps either side) are all unmarked and equal to transcend.exp2, and the theory agrees that none is within the bound of a boundary. Each routine has the checks its form has (`CHECKS_OF`): exp2 has `nofamily` where exp and expm1 have `family`, `census` and `census_counts`, and expm1 has no `fixed_grid`, since a result off its tiny path is never subnormal. The checks with plants of their own (`check_seq`, `check_r24`, `check_invariants`, `check_family_list`) are E1's tests: three unchanged, and the family-list test changed for the list's new nesting.

**Findings, for the lead** (none changes code outside this parcel).
- **expm1 has a second structured family, which the study's census did not hold: x near -n ln 2.**
  - **How I found it.** The first run of the new expm1 fragment over the transcend pools and E1's edge pool (MEASURED, scratch `smoke2.py`: 628, 665, 648 and 810 lanes at fp32, fp64, fp128 and fp256, all five attributes, against transcend.expm1) was right on every unmarked lane, and marked six lanes a cell under rne and rmm at fp64, fp128 and fp256 - none at fp32 and none under the directed three - every marked guess right. The study's family accounts for one: x = -2^-p, which the shared pools hold. The other five lay next to x = RN(-(p+1) ln 2), which E1's edge pool holds among exp's thresholds (n = p + 1, both signs, with neighbours at 1 and 2 ulps): -37.43 at fp64, -79.02 at fp128, -164.97 at fp256. There e^x = 2^-(p+1) (1 + eps), so expm1(x) = -1 + 2^-(p+1) (1 + eps) sits within the in-lane bound of the midpoint between -1 and its neighbour, the boundary of rne and rmm. The study's census (x = c 2^-e) is all next to 0 and cannot contain it.
  - **The theory** (`mathlib_family.py`, its docstring): for n <= p the value -1 + 2^-n (1 + eps) is next to a grid point, the directed attributes' boundary, and for n = p + 1 next to the midpoint; the bound is relative to |V|, about 1, so the true value is within it when 2^-n |eps| is under 2^-(p+G), from n about G + log2 n up to p + 1; x = RN(-n ln 2) is the centre of such a window, and the window's half-width in x is the bound over the derivative, about 2^(n - p - G), wider than an ulp of x only from that n on.
  - **How the committed lists hold it.** (1) `FAMILY["expm1"]` has two kinds of centre, `(c, e)` for c 2^-e and `("n", n)` for RN(-n ln 2), GENERATED from the theory alone (`F.generate`: n = 1 to p + 2, kept where the distance d to the nearest rounding boundary is under 0.7 of the bound) and held to a fresh generation by `test_the_committed_family_is_what_the_theory_generates`: fp64 7 centres under rne and rmm (the first family's 6 and n = 54) and 16 under the directed three (11 and n = 49 to 53); fp128 17 and 191 (n = 114; n = 49 and 51 to 113); fp256 17 and 314 (n = 238; n = 48 and 52 to 237). (2) The windows test runs every centre with its neighbours inside and outside the window (1, W/8, W/4 and 0.65 W ulps in; 1.35 W, 2 W, 8 W and 1024 W out) at every format and attribute, and the `family` run does the same with the census arguments that are not centres and the deep arguments. (3) `test_expm1_has_a_second_family_that_the_studys_census_did_not_hold` holds the second kind to the theory's shape at the three double-word formats and five attributes - n = p + 1 alone under rne and rmm, n up to p under the directed three, none of them in the census - and runs the fragment on the last centre of each list: marked, equal to the golden function in bits and flags without the mark, and a member of the edge pool. (4) The expm1 edge pool holds RN(-n ln 2) with neighbours at 1 and 2 ulps for up to 15 values of n from G/2 to p + 3, so `edges` meets them at every format and attribute. (5) The plants red in `family` on expm1 are `bound_loose`, `bound_wide`, `bound_half`, `bound_double`, `mark_silenced`, `mark_forced` and `reorder_misnumbered`; I have not shown a plant that only the second kind of centre catches.
- **expm1's margins are thin in two places, 2^-2.5 to 2^-3 of the bound at every format: the clamp and the cancelling cells n = +-1; the clamp's was the study's to leave to phase 2.** MEASURED: the placed points (the first clamped k's among them) give 2^-2.99, -2.93, -2.94 and -2.90 at fp32, fp64, fp128 and fp256 (the bound check); the budget's bounds are 0.1773 Bv at fp64 (2^-2.50; M 0.1310 + capacities 0.0463), 0.1316 at fp128 (M 0.1299 + 0.0018) and 0.1353 at fp256 (M 0.1335 + 0.0018), against exp's and exp2's 2^-6 at fp128 and fp256; and the stride-211 sweeps of fp32's n = +1 and n = -1 cells give 2^-2.67 (at x = 0.0578) and 2^-3.56 (at x = -0.0450). The study says the same of both (READ, M1-exp-log.md 3.2 and its margins table: "expm1's clamp term is 2^-2.9 of the bound at every format"; the cancelling cells' budget bounds 0.164 and 0.159 Bv, 2^-2.61 and 2^-2.65, at fp64 and G = 46), and that moving the clamp to k > p + G + 4 "costs nothing, since only a compare's constant changes, and takes the term to 2^-4.9. Phase 2's choice." The brief fixes p + G + 2, as the study's design has it, so the clamp is built so; moving it would thicken the clamp's part and leave the cancelling cells' at about 2^-2.6 (BELIEVED, from the two tables). `clamp = p + G + 2` is one expression in `_scale` (mathlib.py), with a copy in `check_constants` and the harness's placed points that follow it; the plant `clamp_low` (four k early) shows what the bound sees of the clamp: 25 of 478 lanes past it, the worst at 2^+1.06 Bv, at fp64. For the lead's decision; I did not take it.
- **The fp32 routines keep 19 to 21 values live, and C4's `routines.LIVE_MAX` is 16** (READ: python/cft_golden/routines.py line 107; 32 is seq.py's NREG). The double-word fragments keep 11, 13 and 13 (exp, exp2, expm1) and are under 16; fp32's 19, 20 and 21 are over it, so `routines.invariants` would refuse them as they are. `mathlib.invariants` takes the cap as a parameter (`LIVE_CAP`) and C4's is untouched; the cap for fp32 is the wiring step's to decide, which is not this parcel's.
- **exp2's tie at emin - p, as the brief says.** The study's section 4 paragraph on exp2 ("The screen at emin - p reproduces transcend.py's +0 under rmm for the exact tie") and its model give +0 under rmm; transcend.exp2 gives the smallest subnormal, flags 0x18, since parcel XT, and so does the routine: two instructions, under rmm only, at every format.

**Known limits, recorded rather than fixed** (Logan's rule).
- **Scratch comparisons are not reproducible from the tree.** The lanes of the exported 1337a13 against this tree (16,950 pairs) and the study's model against the port (30 cells) import files outside the tree. What the tree holds is `EXP_DIGESTS` (exp's 20 order-free digests at 1337a13, regenerated from the export by script), the pinned shapes, and checks that share nothing with the model.
- **The larger samples are the lead's, on amd-arc-box** (below). This entry's samples are the desktop's, at the study's scale, as E1's were. Every sample is a lower bound on the true worst, and the budget is first order (mathlib_budget's docstring; the study's 3.2). No second-order residue is computed for exp2 and expm1. In five of the six budget cells the largest error found is within 7% of the bound (exp2 0.1593 of 0.1643, 0.0147 of 0.0148 and 0.0180 of 0.0193; expm1 0.1299 of 0.1316 and 0.1336 of 0.1353), so a residue that the first-order bound omits would have to be smaller than that, and none showed an error past it (BELIEVED small, not shown); in the sixth, expm1 at fp64, it is 26% under (0.1312 of 0.1773: the bound adds the largest capacity of the cancelling cells to the clamp's method error, which no one lane has).
- **fp32 has no budget, only its measured bound**: over 30,000 random, 30,000 weighted and 30,000 uniform arguments and the placed points, 2^-4.73 (exp), 2^-4.91 (exp2) and 2^-2.99 (expm1). expm1's thinnest cells, n = +-1, are the strided sweeps of item 2 (2^-2.67 and 2^-3.56), 73,152 floats a sign of the 15.4 million between 0.04 and 0.14 (73,152 x 211 = 15,435,072); the full sweeps are the lead's.
- **`mathlib_runs.py sweep` walks every encoding of its range.** `H.range_encodings` yields each encoding in a Python generator and the command skips by `--stride` and `--shard`, so a pass over [-18, 89] iterates about 2.2 billion encodings per routine, whatever the stride or the number of shards (COMPUTED: fp32's encodings from +0 to 89 number 1.12 billion and from -0 to -18 1.10 billion). MEASURED, on the desktop, niced, one process: `sweep --fn exp,exp2,expm1 --format fp32 --lo -18 --hi 89 --stride 100003` printed nothing - not the first routine's line - in 13 min 47 s, and I stopped it by its PID; the thin-cell sweeps, ranges of 15 million encodings, ran as estimated (232 s and 241 s at stride 211). Each of the box's 108 main-path processes pays the walk once, on top of its evaluation (about 15 min or more by that measurement, where I estimated 12 min for everything); the lead judged 25 to 30 min a shard fine and left the O(lanes) form (the lanes of a shard are an arithmetic progression of keys) to a later parcel. The results of a sweep are right; only its cost is.
- **The scheduler is a heuristic, not an optimum**: two cheap orders, the lower peak taken. `LIVE_CAP` (21 at fp32, 13 at the others) is the measured maximum of each column, not a design argument, and a smaller state (fewer words in the triple word's tail) might need fewer; I did not look. `Fragment.live_max()` is exact for `routines.program`'s first-free allocation, and every fragment was placed on seq.py.
- **The quick tests were trimmed to keep the golden stage short**, and what each trim gives up: 60 random and 60 weighted lanes a cell at exp2 and expm1 (exp keeps E1's 120 and 120); the rate law at 1,000 lanes a cell for exp2 and expm1 (exp keeps E1's 2,000; at 22.6 expected the sigma is 4.7, and the plants that matter - `bound_loose`, `bound_wide`, `mark_silenced` - are far outside the 3-sigma band); at most three greens a row of the plant table; exp's edge pool on seq.py at the double-word formats only (all four formats and every routine in `mathlib_runs.py pools --edges --seq`, above); `nofamily`'s deep arguments under rne and rtz only; and a plant's `lanes`, `bound` and `budget` runs of 60 lanes, 100 random and the placed points, and 20 weighted and an eighth of the placed points. The windows test runs every centre (30 tests, 38 s at -n 4).
- **The theory decides which marks are allowed** at exp2 and expm1 (exp keeps E1's committed list): a mark is allowed where `F.classify` says "mark" or "either" (d under 1.3 of the bound), and the lists are generated from the same theory. That check is not independent of it; what is independent is the routine's own marks, which the tests compare to the theory both ways (every lane the theory says must be marked is, none that it says must not be), and the bound against mpmath.
- **Tests of E1's whose premises moved** (E1's 38 test functions, 252 tests: 6 unchanged in this file, 26 generalised to a routine parameter with exp one of its cells, 6 replaced). **The design as built** (READ: docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, sections 2.3, 2.4 to 2.6, 3 and 4, and the model docs/studies/m1/m1log.py; the comments in mathlib.py give each piece's argument).
- **The reduction is one for the three, at every format.** x = 2^E m with m in [1, 2) (a subnormal x scaled by 2^p, exactly; log1p's m is that of u = 1 + x). C = round(16 RECIP_SEED(m)) by the magic-number FMA, which takes the values 8 to 16 over the instruction's 512 cells (`--check`: all 512, below); C = 8 wraps (m' = m/2, c = 1, k = E + 1); c = C/16, exact; r = m' c - 1 is ONE FMA and EXACT, with the largest |r| of the 512 cells 0.05908203125 = 2^-4.081 (MEASURED, `--check`; RHO_LOG, 0.0592, is above it). The table is L_j = log(16/C), j = C mod 8, in two words (three at fp32) by the same SELECT tree as the exp family's, L_0 = 0.
- **The polynomial** is Y(r) = log1p(r)/r = sum (-1)^i r^i/(i+1): a single-word Horner tail from degree D down to K and K double-word steps (TwoProd by FMA, Fast2Sum), (K, D) = (11, 23) at fp64 (G = 44), (12, 38) at fp128 and (12, 68) at fp256 (G = 46) (COMPUTED by `plan_log`, an exact-rational search; equal to the model's float plan in the cells I compared, MEASURED in scratch `plan_check.py`: fp64 at G = 44 and 46, fp128 and fp256). The brief lists K = 12 for all three; it is 11 at fp64's decided G = 44.
- **The sum.** log: k ln 2 + L_j + r Y, with ln 2 in THREE words, the first two truncated to p - n_k bits (n_k the bits of the largest |k|: `_k_width`) so that k times either is exact (the study's defect 2: two words left k ln 2 short by up to 2^3 times the bound), A = k ln2_h + L_h by Fast2Sum, A + r Y_h by TwoSum, the rest in a few rounded adds, V = V_h + V_l by Fast2Sum. log2: F = L + r Y as a double word, times 1/ln 2 in two words, then k + it by Fast2Sum (|k| >= the product, or k = 0). log1p: u = 1 + x by TwoSum, the same core on u_h, and u_l folded in as r_l = u_l 2^-k c corrected by r_l/(1 + r) (1/(1 + r) by three Newton steps from 1 - r), 2^-k taken as 0 past k = p + G + 2 (defect 5); |x| < 15/256 skips the reduction (r = x, k = 0, L = 0), the end of that path being under the polynomial's rho (defect 8 had it at 2^-4).
- **The final rounding and the in-lane test** are the exp family's: R = rnd(V_h + V_l), Bv = 2^-(p+G) |V_h|, R1 = rnd(V_h + RD(V_l - Bv)) and R2 = rnd(V_h + RU(V_l + Bv)), mark = R1 xor R2, ORed into the flag word as bit 7 (the study's 3.1). The specials are section 4's rows in its order of priority, lowest first: the main path's inexact (and the mark), the exact cases (log(1) = +0 and log2(2^k) = k, no flag and no mark), log1p's tiny path fma(-x, x, x) for |x| < 2^-(p+2) with its underflow cases (|x| < 2^emin, and x = +2^emin under rtz and rdn), +inf, the negatives (NaN, invalid), zero (log, log2: -inf, divideByZero; log1p: the operand), x = -1 for log1p (-inf, divideByZero) and NaN. -x is `ixor(x, sign bit)`, one instruction, so that no instruction reads only the input (question 12); the result is always normal and the routine is not scaled (no scale words, no fixed grid).
- **fp32 is new design for the three** (the study models only exp there). r is exact in one word, so there is no reduction to carry; the table is three words per entry and ln 2 (or 1/ln 2) three words; Y(r) runs in (K3, K2, D) = (5, 6, 15) triple-word, double-word and single-word Horner steps (`plan_log32`; an exact-rational search); k ln 2 is TwoProd against ln 2's first two words and a rounded product with the third; V is the SUM OF ITS TERMS BY LEVELS, exactly (a TwoSum chain, the error terms of products by FMA held negated) down to 2^-48 of the scale and by rounded adds below it, then three Fast2Sums, then the final rounding through round-to-odd of V_1 + V_2 as exp's; log1p's low word is rho = r_l/(1 + r) as a double word with the square term of log1p(rho) = rho - rho^2/2 subtracted from it (rho^2/2 is 2^-49 at fp32, over the bound, and rho^3/3 is 2^-73, under it: COMPUTED from r_l <= 2^-24). (BELIEVED, not shown: another sum order would cost fewer instructions; I did not look.)

**Findings, for the lead** (none changes code outside this parcel).
- **log1p at fp32, just above 15/256, has a margin of 1.23 bits, thinner than any other cell and than the two bits the study asks of fp64.** MEASURED, `python python/tests/mathlib_runs.py sweep --fn log1p --format fp32 --lo 0.05859375 --hi 0.125 --stride 200` (116 s): every 200th float of [15/256, 1/8], 47,186 of the 9,437,185 in the range, all on the main path: the largest |V - log1p| / Bv is **2^-1.23 at 0x3d717ed0 = 0.05895882844924927**, in the binade just below 1/16, where u = 1 + x has bits below its ulp (u_l up to 2^-24). The 3,000 random arguments of item 2 found 2^-2.40 over the whole range and the placed points 2^-4.41: a random sample understates this cell by 1.2 bits, and a sweep of every float is the box's job. ## 2026-10-14 - M1's build, item 2: program.c parity - M1's six routines through libcft's sequencer, an eighth corpus in seq_check.py: 120 fragments in two shapes, 240 programs and 13,483 lanes at the gate's arguments, 0 mismatches, a planted fault for every check (parcel MP)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "M1's build after E1") makes item 2 "program.c parity: the fragments' programs in seq_check's corpora. No new C, since the routines are programs of existing instructions." Item 1 is merged (all six routines, 29f68fc), and until this parcel no program of them had been through program.c: the second wave's closing record says so (READ: "No routine's program is in its corpora yet; that is M1's build, item 2"). The fragments had run on seq.py alone.
- Logan on the round's models, verbatim as the brief gives it (READ): "Use Sonnet for M1's build parcels as you recommended, it performed well". The author is Sonnet and the verifier Sonnet. The project's discipline (READ: CLAUDE.md): the golden model, libcft, the simulator and the card agree bit for bit, and anything the hardware cannot do is refused by name.
- This parcel adds one corpus to `host/tests/seq_check.py` and restates what that makes false in two documents. It changes no code in host/src, python/ or rtl/, no fragment of mathlib.py, no name in routines.py or cftc, and it touches no card and no machine but the desktop (READ: the brief).
- Marks: MEASURED is a run of this parcel's, its command and time given, on the desktop, niced, one process at a time; READ is a file, named; COMPUTED is arithmetic on those; BELIEVED is mine and not shown. A run handed to the lead is marked so and its result is not claimed here. The brief is the lead's, outside the tree.

**What was built** (one file of code, three documents; the code's commits are b81fe11, 17a3fe7, d9c44b5 and 8920d95, in that order).
- `host/tests/seq_check.py` (2,689 lines at c918cb3, 3,593 at 8920d95): the eighth corpus, eighteen functions - `routine_modules`, `routine_programs`, `_routine_cached`, `routine_specials`, `routine_ln1p_marks`, `routine_struct_pool`, `routine_quotas`, `routine_lanes`, `run_in_c_routine`, `routine_top_const`, `routine_needs`, `routine_refuses`, `routine_rounds`, `routine_corpus`, `routine_caps`, `routine_limits`, `routine_expected_refusals`, `routine_remote_refusals` - its paragraph of the module's docstring and the `--device` paragraph's lines about it, `--math-rounds`, the counters, a summary, a reach check and the `--device` accounting in `main()`. `_Device` keeps three more capacities (max_insns, max_consts, max_deposits) and `_FakeServer` takes two (max_insns, max_consts), both with the defaults it had. Of the first seven corpora's code only these were restated: the fake server's constructor and its caps pack, the `bad +=` sum, `if not by:`, and the tuple the `--device` check walks; the `--device` paragraph of the docstring gained its sentences.
- docs/VERIFICATION.md's `--device` row, docs/HOSTAPI.md's paragraph on `seq_check.py --device`, docs/README.md's counts, and this entry.

**The two shapes.**
- READ (python/cft_golden/routines.py, `program`): `routines.program(f)`, the brief's stand-alone program, is the body, DEPOSIT of the result, DEPOSIT of the flag word, HALT, over a BANK_EXT bank; it has NO quiet region and NO raise, so a mark is a bit in a deposited word and STATUS[6] and the lane byte's bit 7 can never carry it. The brief's list of what is compared (STATUS with its mark, the lane bytes) and its plant "R24's RAISE not reaching STATUS's mark" need a RAISE in the program.
- So each fragment runs in two shapes. STAND-ALONE is `routines.program`'s. COMPILED is `python/tests/mathlib_harness.py`'s `r24_program` - QUIET, the body, ENDQUIET, RAISE of the flag word, DEPOSIT of the result, the shape cftc/inline.py gives a routine and the tests run on seq.py only (`check_r24`). Only the second reaches R24's mark and R23's byte; only the first lets the body's own flags reach FLAGS and carries the flag word as data.
- READ (seq_check.py): no corpus before this one ran a BANK_EXT program through libcft - every other `RunArgs` sets `bank = None` - so a bank went through `cft_program_run_ex` from this file for the first time here.

**The draw** (READ: the code; the figures MEASURED, below).
- A program's lanes come from five categories, shuffled, each lane tagged with its source: the special encodings (+-0, +-inf, quiet and signalling NaNs with payloads and of both signs, the extreme subnormals and normals, +-1 and the floats beside it); the routine's edge pool (`mathlib_harness.edge_pool`: thresholds with their signs, screens, the ends of every cell); the transcend pools (`mathlib_harness.pools`, the tests' own); the structured family - the committed windows' centres, which the routine marks, and at fp32 the five floats nearest ln(1 + t) that exp marks under the directed three (`routine_ln1p_marks`), as "centres", and as "beside them" the census a window would start at and the neighbours of a few centres, or for exp2 and log2, which have no family, the lanes next to their exact cases; and random encodings (the main path's samplers `random_main` and `weighted`, and raw bit patterns). Shares 15, 25, 15, 15 and 30 per cent, with at least 3, 3, 1, 1 and 1 lanes from nine lanes up (`routine_quotas`); a category short of lanes hands its remainder to the random one.
- 1, 2, 63, 64, 65, 65, 100 or 129 lanes a program (mean 61), each with a one in three chance of a mask, the per-lane block asked for on every compiled run and half the stand-alone ones. From a seed of the corpus's own per format - `args.seed * 2654435761 + width * 40503`, xor a constant - and a stream of its own per fragment, drawn from it in a fixed order; the seven corpora's generators are not touched, and their output at six sets of arguments has no line removed or changed (below). One round draws every fragment in both shapes; the default is one round for each 250 `--trials`, at least one, and `--math-rounds N` sets it.
- The lanes come from python/tests, which needs mpmath and pytest. A host without either prints one line, `SKIP  the routine corpus (the eighth): <package> is not installed here, ...`, which verify/run.sh's inner-skip regex matches, and runs the seven corpora as before; `--require-all` fails it, as for any inner skip.

**What is compared** (per program, both executors given the same lanes, bank, mask and block request).
- FLAGS; STATUS, the mark among it; every deposit (the result and the flag word in the stand-alone shape, the result in the compiled); every count; every lane byte where the block is asked for - and that the number of lanes compared is the number the run owns. The buffers are filled with the caller's pattern first (deposit bytes 0xA5, counts 0xA5A5A5A5, lane bytes 0xEE), so a masked lane's bytes, which libcft must leave alone, are told from ones written 0: for an owned lane the model's value must be there, for a masked lane the pattern.
- The model's own identity, beside it: on the first dozen owned lanes of each stand-alone program and on every lane whose flag word carries the mark, the (result, flag word) seq.py deposited is `mathlib.evaluate`'s - what `routines.run` returns, taken from the same seq.py run.
- A fragment the model runs and libcft refuses is a MISMATCH, named by format, routine, attribute and shape, with the library's sentence.
- Under `--device` a program needing a bit the device does not publish is refused by name (`device_refuses`, the other corpora's helper) and counted by CAPS place; one past a capacity the device publishes is refused naming `cft_caps.<field>` and counted on a line of its own; a device that takes either, or refuses it otherwise, is a mismatch.
- A remote leg (`routine_remote_refusals`) loads every program the run built on a remote handle to a fake server whose HELLO publishes a revision-7 tile's word (0x7f1f), that word without BANK_PTR, without WIDE_CONST and without REGS32, a revision-8 tile's word (R23 and R24 published), and that word at max_insns 300 and at max_consts 64: each load must be CFT_ERR_UNSUPPORTED naming a CAPS place or `cft_caps.<field>` where the program needs what the word lacks (asm.py's own account of an image's features, `_needs`) and must load where it does not; a run asking for the block on the revision-7 word is refused naming LANE_FLAGS before any frame; no load reaches the wire.
- The summary counts programs and lanes by format, the programs past the block, the runs under a mask and the ones that masked a lane, the lane block's runs and bytes, the marked lanes and the runs with STATUS[6] set, the lanes by class of argument and by source, the compiled runs by the flags they raised, and the identity's lanes; then one line of the programs' sizes against libcft's limits (`cft_get_caps`).
- A reach check fails the run, naming it, if any of twenty-five counters is zero (the programs past the block, runs under a mask, lane bytes, marked lanes, runs with STATUS[6], marked flag words, NaN, infinite, zero, subnormal and normal arguments, each of the five flags, the identity's lanes, the remote leg's refusals and loads, and the six sources of lanes), if the programs drawn are not the corpus's own arithmetic (every routine at every attribute in both shapes, a round at a time, at each format run), if the remote leg ran fewer than its seven servers, or if it never refused by a name the run's programs can be refused by.

**Held** (every command from the repository root, on the desktop, niced, one process at a time; "at 8920d95" is the code's last commit, the one the plants' last runs used; each run exits 0 and prints "libcft and the golden model agree on every program: deposits, counts, flags and status" or, under `--device`, its own last line).

**Known limits, recorded rather than fixed** (Logan's rule).
- **The draw is a sample.** 13,483 lanes in 240 programs at the gate's arguments, about 56 a program; the tests hold the fragments to the definition on far more lanes (the pools and edge pools whole, thousands of random lanes a cell, the lead's sweeps), and this corpus holds libcft to seq.py on this sample. A class of lane the sample does not reach is not compared. The classes of argument, the sources and the flags the compiled runs raised are counted and all non-zero, and a reach check fails the run if any is zero; but they are classes of argument and of flag word, not of path through a fragment.

STATUS[6] and bit 7 of the lane byte are therefore compared at fp32 for those three fragments (and the flag word's bit 7 in the stand-alone shape); the other fifteen routines' fp32 fragments mark nothing here. At fp64, fp128 and fp256 the marks come from the committed centres of exp, expm1, log and log1p.

## 2026-10-14 - the rate check's calibration: its centre and sigma are the sample's own, derived from the code and held to the fragment lane for lane, and a run of many cells is judged as the independent statistics it holds, by exact tails (parcel RC)

**Why.**
- The second wave's closing entry carries the rate check as a known limit (READ, "Known limits carried"): "its centre is the log-uniform mean, so use n at most 2000 for the log family, or the sample's own sum of 2w". The case was the lead's box batch at 85fe5e0: `mathlib_runs.py rate --fn log2 --format fp256 --n 20000 --seed 11` exited 1, rtz, rdn and rup marking 548 against 451.2 (+4.6 sigma), no lane wrong (READ, verifier-VMB2's ledger, the headings of 05:26:02 and 05:53:28).
- verifier-VMB2 measured the cause. The law's centre is the mean 1/ln 2 of a log-uniform significand of V; the log family's sampler draws the exponent field uniformly, so |V| is about the exponent and log2's significand is uniform (mean 1.4995), and the sample's own expectation is 468.6. Against that, 548 is +3.71 sigma of 21.4: VMB2 reads it as chance and marks that reading NOT SETTLED by measurement (30 further seeds gave +0.3 sigma). Its instrument computes the marks from the true values with no fragment run, and predicted the box's seeds 12 and 13 exactly (479 and 462; 517 and 458; READ).
- Logan, answering the lead's offer to make the check compute its expected count from the sample itself, verbatim: "Go ahead and queue the follow up" (READ, the brief).
- The brief (briefs/RC.md, sha256 c2320a73430660a94b370a5982df7f9a5a2a03b02e63ee0b5d5e5353fc012add): the centre and sigma from the sample, derived from the code; a rule for runs over many statistics, its false-alarm rate measured over many seeds, every rate plant kept red and no test weakened; the box commands; this entry. Nothing else moves: not mathlib.py, not the samplers.
- **Send-back 1** (the lead, after verifier-VRC, Haiku; briefs/RC-sendback-1.md, sha256 b5f32b71fed0847054e37ff15d25340745fa70d5f3eaaab6b1c0cc77039e4eec; READ): one (a) by the letter of Logan's rule and two minor (b)s. This entry was not pushed, so it is restated in place and says where a first figure was wrong. (a) Ten cells of the plant map that the plain line flagged at 1,000 lanes were not flagged by the rule: the plant rows' `rate` runs are now at 3,500 lanes (`PLANT_RATE_N`; the lead's first n was 3,000, which the geometry scan over the two bound plants' 96 cells showed to lose one more, then 3,500 at the lead's word; the plants, below). (b) 1 The log family's per-statistic mean of z, written -0.119 to +0.083, is -0.069 to +0.083 (the premise, below). (b) 2 `RateSample.pmf`'s table left more than 1e-20 above it at means below 0.88: its top is now `pmf_top`, the Chernoff top, which leaves under 1e-20 at every mean (kmax changed, not the docstring's range; What changed, below).
- Marks: MEASURED is a run of this parcel's, its command and time given, on the desktop, niced, a process at a time (or three, for the many-seed runs: `-n 4` at most); READ is a file, named; COMPUTED is arithmetic on those; BELIEVED is mine and not shown. A run handed to the lead is marked so and its result is not claimed. "Scratch" is a script of this parcel's outside the tree; the committed `mathlib_runs.py rategeom` gives the same numbers (MEASURED: 24 samples, counts, expectations and tails equal, below).

**What changed** (three code files, this entry, docs/README.md recounted, VERIFICATION's golden row; mathlib.py, the samplers and every other check are as they were):
- `python/tests/mathlib_harness.py` (1,667 lines at c918cb3): the derivation as a comment block above the rate section; `RATE_ALPHA` (0.1%), `rate_class`, `rate_statistics`, `rate_level`; `lane_cell` (a lane's true value: its binade, significand m_V and place u in its rounding cell); `poisson_binomial_pmf`; `pmf_top` (the top of its table, send-back 1: the least count above the mean at which the multiplicative Chernoff bound exp(-mean) (e mean / k)^k on the upper tail is under 1e-20, so what is past the table is under 1e-20 at every mean whatever the lanes' probabilities; the first version's top, mean + 14 sigma + 6, left more than that below a mean of 0.88); `RateSample` (a sample's lanes, each lane's probability 2^-G' m_V, the law's mean, variance, exact tails, exact probability of a flag, and the marks its geometry gives); `check_rate` rewritten (the centre and sigma are the sample's own, the verdict the exact two-sided tail against alpha / statistics; `sigmas` keeps the plain line; new `statistics` and `alpha`); the new check `check_rate_geometry`.
- `python/tests/mathlib_runs.py`: `rate` takes `--statistics` and `--alpha`, its `--sigmas` defaults to none (the exact rule) and a last line gives the run's smallest tail; the new command `rategeom` (the law over many seeds with no fragment: the rule's false-alarm rate and the mean and variance of z, measured).
- `python/tests/test_mathlib.py` (2,132 lines at c918cb3): `RATE_STATISTICS`; the committed rate test and `run_check`'s rate branch judge by the new rule; `PLANT_RATE_N` = 3,500, the lanes of the plant rows' `rate` runs (send-back 1: they ran at 1,000, and the committed 90-cell test stays at `RATE_N`); 57 new tests (the 48 cells of the geometry test, and 9 on the pmf and its table's top, the tails, the false-alarm arithmetic, the centre, the planted build, the geometry check's plants, the runs script and the plant rows' lanes); `check_rate_geometry` joins `ELSEWHERE`. The plant table's 143 rows are untouched.

**The derivation** (READ python/cft_golden/mathlib.py, unchanged by this parcel; the same text is the comment block in the harness).
- **The bound word.** `check_rate` builds the fragment with `bound_shift = G - G'` (G' = 6); the constants set `BREL = _pow2(fmt, -(p + G) + shift - _bound_plant(plant))` (lines 1177, 1690, 2002 and 2315), so BREL is exactly 2^-(p+6) for an unplanted build (the planted bounds are `bound_loose` 2^-40 narrower, `bound_wide` 2^16 wider, `bound_half` and `bound_double`), and `Bv = V_h BREL`, an exact product by a power of two (|V_h| for expm1 and the log family, V_h itself for exp and exp2, whose V is positive; V_0 at fp32): lines 1576, 1896, 2249 and 2550.
- **The mark.** R1 = rnd(V_h + RD(V_l - Bv)), R2 = rnd(V_h + RU(V_l + Bv)), `mk = ixor(R1, R2)`, ORed into the flag word as bit 7 (lines 1577-1581, 1897-1901, 2250-2254 and 2551-2555; at fp32 V_l is V1 + V2 and its two ends are the round-to-odd sums of V1 with RD(V2 - Bv) and RU(V2 + Bv)). The lane is marked exactly when [V - Bv, V + Bv], widened by the roundings of the low word (COMPUTED: by at most 2^-(p-6) of its width at each end, 2^-18 at fp32), holds a boundary of the attribute: a float under rtz, rdn and rup, a midpoint under rne and rmm.
- **The probability.** Boundaries of either kind are one ulp of V apart, and the window is 2 Bv = 2^-(p+5) |V_h| wide, at most 2^-5 of an ulp (COMPUTED), so at most one is inside. With V's place u in its rounding cell uniform, a lane is marked with probability 2 Bv / ulp(V) = 2^-G' m_V, where |V| = m_V 2^E, m_V in [1, 2) and ulp(V) = 2^(E-p+1): 1/64 to 1/32 at G' = 6, the same under the five attributes. The count of marks is then a sum of independent Bernoulli lanes, with mean 2^-G' sum(m_V) and variance sum p (1 - p): the sample's own centre and sigma.
- **The reduction to the law.** For a log-uniform significand (density 1/(m ln 2)) the mean of m_V is 1/ln 2, and n 2^-G' / ln 2 = n 2^(0.5288 - G'), the study's n 2^(0.53 - G') to 0.09% (COMPUTED: 0.99913).
- **A lane at a binade's edge.** An ulp is twice as long above a power of two as below it, but the window holds one boundary all the same and the lane's m_V is its own (just under 2 below the edge, 1 above it): the sum of 2 Bv / ulp is that of the smooth density, which is the sawtooth 2^-G' m_V. A lane whose window holds the edge itself is about one in 2^(p+4) (COMPUTED); MEASURED (scratch `edge_count.py`, exact integers on the `_mpf_` significand): none of 960,000 lanes (six routines, four formats, 20,000 lanes at seeds 7 and 11) has one.
- **The exp family's lanes with a subnormal result.** `_fixed_grid` (lines 1316-1353) leaves `mk` as the main test made it except where V_h is on the fixed grid's own boundary (a half-grid point under rne and rmm, a grid point under the directed three) with |V_l| <= Bv: the in-lane test runs in the scaled domain, so those lanes mark as any other. The directed three then mark exactly what the geometry says, and rne and rmm a few lanes more, the fixed grid's own. MEASURED (scratch `cmp_sub.py`, 20,000 lanes of a subnormal result each, seed 9, the inflated fragments): rtz 473, 452, 430 and 474 marked, equal to the geometry's lane for lane (exp and exp2 at fp32, then fp64); rne 463, 458, 471 and 468 against the geometry's 442, 439, 467 and 457 - 21, 19, 4 and 11 more (4.8%, 4.3%, 0.9% and 2.4%), none fewer. Those lanes are 8% (fp32) and 2.5% (fp64) of the exp family's sample, so the expectation is short by under 0.4% at fp32 and under 0.1% at fp64 under rne and rmm (COMPUTED), and less beyond.
- **What is not derived** is that u is uniform and independent from lane to lane. That is MEASURED, below.

**The rule for a run of many cells** (decided here; `check_rate`'s docstring states it).
- A cell's count is judged by its **exact two-sided tail** under the sample's own law, twice the smaller of P(count <= c) and P(count >= c), by the dynamic programme over the lanes (`poisson_binomial_pmf`, held to the enumeration of every subset of 12 lanes and to the binomial's closed form at 700 lanes, 1e-15 and 1e-13). A normal z misjudges the small counts: 0 marks of 16.4 expected is "-4.0 sigma" (a normal two-sided tail of 6e-5) and has an exact two-sided tail of 1.2e-7 to 3.5e-7 at the committed log cells (COMPUTED, all nine); a count 4 sigma over a mean of 16.4 has an upper tail of 2e-4 where the normal says 3e-5 (Poisson).
- The five attributes of a routine and format are **two statistics**, not five (the lane-for-lane run above): a run holds K = routines x formats x 2: 18 for the log family's 45 cells, 36 for the committed test's 90 (`rate_statistics`).
- A statistic is flagged when its tail is under **alpha / K** (Bonferroni), **alpha = RATE_ALPHA = 0.1%**: a run in which nothing is wrong is flagged with probability at most alpha. `mathlib_runs.py rate` takes K from its own cells, or `--statistics K` for a batch of processes that is one run (nine processes of one routine and format each, K = 18), and `--alpha`; the committed test passes K = 36. `--sigmas N` keeps the plain N-sigma line, about the sample's own mean.
- **The false-alarm rate per run, COMPUTED** (the law's own exact probability, the sum over a run's statistics of the exact probability that a count's tail is under the level, `RateSample.rejection`): **0.0589% for the committed run** (the 18 samples of seed 7, each statistic's 0.44 to 0.86 of the level: the counts are discrete; the 90 committed cells at seed 7 are all well inside the law: the smallest two-sided tail is 0.034, expm1 fp64 nearest, 13 marked against 22.9, and the largest |z| about the sample's own mean 2.10, so the old three-sigma line passes them too, COMPUTED, scratch `committed_cells.py`), 0.09% for the log family's 45 cells at 20,000 lanes and 0.09% for the exp family's (the exact flag probabilities summed over the seeds below, divided by their runs).

- **The sentence about 1,000 lanes, restated with its level.** The first version said that an exact family-wise rule cannot keep a twice-as-wide bound red in every cell at 1,000 lanes. It holds only for a false-alarm rate below about 27% (verifier-VRC; COMPUTED here as K = 36 times each cell's tail at 1,000 lanes, the alpha at which the cell would just be flagged, from the table's tails): expm1 fp64, the weakest, needs 36 x 7.5e-3 = 27%; then log fp128 7.6%, log fp64 1.4%, log1p fp32 1.05%, exp fp64 0.79%, the half exp2 fp64 0.75%, the half expm1 fp32 0.32%, expm1 fp32 0.21%, log2 fp32 0.14% and log2 fp64 0.12%. At alpha = 1% six of the ten are red (exp fp64, expm1 fp32, log2 fp32, log2 fp64 and the two halves) and four are not; at the committed 0.1% none is. So the sentence is true of a rule at 0.1% or 1% and false in general; what it comes to is that 0.1% needs more lanes than 1,000 against a bound twice or half as wide, and the next bullet says how many.

**Known limits, recorded rather than fixed** (Logan's rule).
- **The premise is measured, not proved, and its extreme tail is a little heavy at one place.** u uniform and independent from lane to lane: the central moments are the law's to 2% (above), the tails to the 1e-3 level; the log family at 20,000 lanes has five of 11,880 z past 4 sigma (about 1.2 expected), four of them log2, and log2 fp64 directed's variance of z is 1.172 (3.1 sd over 1). The three runs flagged at alpha 0.1% (against the law's 0.6) are those. 1,000,000 lanes of log2 at fp64 show no structure in u by binade. BELIEVED chance (about 0.5% for the five, though I looked at several cuts): a replication on 990 further seeds of log2 found none of them again (above); the box's third batch (command 3) is the larger measurement.
- **The family-wise rule sees less than the old line at small n, and a bound half as wide stays hard to see.** At 1,000 lanes it did not flag 13 cells that the old line flagged (above); the plant rows' `rate` runs are at 3,500 lanes, where none of the 275 cells of the map and none of the 96 cells of the two bound plants that the line flagged is lost, and the 36 listed verdicts are as they were. At the committed run's own `RATE_N` the rule flags a doubled bound in fewer cells than the line did (12 of 48 against 36 at 700 lanes, geometry), but no test judges a plant there: the plants are judged by the plant rows' runs and by the geometry check, which flags every one of the six bound and mark plants in every one of its 48 cells at 600 lanes. A bound half as wide is flagged in 43 of 48 cells at 3,500 lanes (the rule's power is 0.79 a cell there, so some misses are chance, and a different seed would move which); the five that stay green are cells the line did not flag at 1,000 lanes either, and all 48 are flagged at every n from 4,864 to 6,000 at seed 7, 5,000 among them (power 0.97 a cell there; first reached at 4,501). The n is the lead's: `PLANT_RATE_N`, 3,500 at the lead's word after 3,000 lost a cell the line flagged.
- **The exp family's lanes with a subnormal result** mark a few more under rne and rmm than the expectation says (the fixed grid's own test: 4.3% to 4.8% of them at fp32, 0.9% to 2.4% at fp64; under 0.4% of a sample's count at the most): the expectation is the p-bit geometry's for them, and `check_rate_geometry` leaves them out. Not modelled.
- **The geometry check runs rne and rtz at 600 lanes** and stands them for rmm and for rdn and rup (MEASURED equal at fp64 and fp256, 60 cells, not tested at the other formats beyond rne and rtz); at 600 lanes a bound off by under 10% shows in a lane or none. Its plants are powers of two.
- **K is the caller's.** A run's K is its own cells' unless `--statistics` says otherwise; a batch of processes without it is flagged more often than alpha (above). The committed test's 36 is `rate_statistics(FUNCS, DOUBLE)`; a new routine (M2's sin, cos, tan) adds six and lowers each level by 14%.
- **The law assumes the lanes independent;** the two classes of one sample have disjoint windows and so are slightly negatively correlated, and log and log2 at one format share their lanes (`uniform_m1rate` seeds by the format's width alone). Bonferroni needs no independence, so the bound holds; the exact false-alarm figures (0.059%, 0.091%) are the independent case's.
- **The exact tails cost O(lanes x top)**, the top being `pmf_top`'s: 0.75 to 0.78 s at 20,000 lanes (a mean of 450, top 669; MEASURED, three runs, scratch), and about 22 minutes at a million (a mean of 22,600, top 24,059: COMPUTED from the 20,000-lane rate, the cost being lanes times top; this entry said 50 minutes before send-back 1, which was wrong). `--sigmas` is the plain line for a sample that large.
- **`uniform_m1rate` at fp256 for the log family costs 0.4 to 1.6 ms a lane** (its Fractions are of 2^262,144): `rategeom` at 20,000 lanes spends 8 s (log, log2) to 32 s (log1p) a sample in the sampler. The samplers stay as they are.
- **Scratch.** The runs above are scratch scripts of this parcel's outside the tree (`cmp_lanes.py`, `cmp_sub.py`, `fa_fast.py`, `fa_analyze.py`, `plants_rate.py`, `power_scan.py`, `plant_counts_real.py`, `plants_geom_sweep.py`, `u_uniform.py`, `edge_count.py`, `mutate_tests.py`; and, for send-back 1, `plants_rate2.py`, `sb1_analyze_n.py`, `sb1_plant_counts_real.py`, `sb1_power.py`, `superset3000.py`, `superset_n.py`, `superset_every_n.py`, `sb1_residual.py`, `sb1_direct_check.py`, `sb1_guard_counts.py`, `sb1_mutate_tests.py`, `sb1_pmf_top_scan.py`, `sb1_origin_of_minus_0119.py`, `rate_calls_timing.py`), kept in the scratchpad; the tree holds `rategeom`, which gives `fa_fast.py`'s counts, means and tails (24 samples compared, 1e-9), and the tests.

## 2026-10-15 - M1's build, item 3: the language, golden-first - exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p and log2 as operations with transcend.py's golden functions, their folds and refusals, renderers and tangent rules, held by a central difference in high precision; cftc refuses them `math-library` until item 4; the language at 1.1, with cft.h and the certificate corpus; a planted fault for every check (parcel ML)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "M1's build after E1") makes item 3 "The language, golden-first: the six nodes and their interpreter; folds and refusals (question 8), and the renderers; the L3 rules (questions 6 and 7), with the central-difference check (question 10); LANGUAGE.md; the language at 1.1." Items 1 and 2 are merged: mathlib.py's six routines, and program.c parity. The design is docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, sections 6 and 7, with Logan's answers to its questions of 2026-10-12, "Approve all as recommended (Recommended)" (READ: ROADMAP, "Logan's answers").
- Logan on the models, 2026-10-13 (READ): "Use Sonnet for M1's build parcels as you recommended, it performed well", which put the language and cftc work on Opus. The author is Opus; the verifier is Sonnet.
- Marks: MEASURED is a run of this parcel's on the desktop, niced, one process at a time, with its command, time and load; READ is a file, named; COMPUTED is arithmetic on those; BELIEVED is mine and not shown. **No time here is a quiet figure**: from 05:38 to about 06:40 another session's mutation runs held the desktop at 74 to 100 per cent CPU, about twenty python processes, none of them mine, and after it the load was 1 to 17 per cent. Each run's load is given beside it.
- The brief is the lead's, outside the tree; the ledger is `ledger/ML.md` in the round's records.

**Four decisions made for me, by the lead, on 2026-10-15** (each asked with the cause; the ledger has the questions):
1. **expm1's rule is `(1 + r) * da`, not the study's `fma(r, da, da)`.** The fma reads da twice. The step graph gives an unlabelled node one use: graph.canonical asserts it, and the canonical form writes such a node where it is used, so a second use would read back as a second node. Where da is an unnamed expression it would have to be written again, which doubles the tangent at each nested expm1 (2^k nodes at k levels), with nothing to bound it short of a new refusal. The fma where da has a name was rejected too: "a let must never change the bits". So 1 + r is primal-only and shared across vectors, as log1p's 1 + a is, and the rule takes two roundings. It is a departure from section 7's table.
2. **All three logarithms take the select form**: `select(r == r, da / a, r)`, `select(r == r, da / (L * a), r)` and `select(r == r, da / (1 + a), r)`. Section 7's table gave log2 and log1p "as log" at their singular points, and question 7's own text names "log1p below -1", but the table's forms `da / (L * a)` and `da / (1 + a)` are finite below the domain. Below its domain each tangent is now the NaN r.
3. **cftc refuses every source that names one of the six, at run time or folded, under a new interim name, `math-library`.** The brief said "at run time"; but the folds let a source like `next x = x * exp(0)` compile, and python/cftc/outputs.py's rule steps the output version for "a source that compiles where it was refused", while the brief keeps VERSION 5. `runtime-routine` is false of a fold, so the name is new. Item 4 lifts it and steps VERSION to 6.
4. **The language at 1.1 reaches cft.h and the certificate corpus, and all of it is done here (option A).** lang/version.py is mirrored by cft.h's `CFT_LANGUAGE_MAJOR` and `_MINOR`: host/tests/audit_check.py holds them equal, and host/tests/segrun_check_v2.py holds the `language` line cft-segrun writes, from cft.h, to lang/version.py. At 1.1, cft-segrun writes `language 1.1` for a run naming a source. The corpus's writers-both sourced cases said `language 1`, corpus.py's recipe literal, and the corpus check holds that line byte for byte. The lead: "The language's version changes when the language does, and every pushed commit's record must be true." Parcel PS stepped CFT_PROFILE_MINOR and remade the corpus the same way for profile 3.1. Item 4 remakes the corpus again for VERSION 6.

The lead also accepted L computed by an integer series (below) rather than through transcend.log at check time.

**What was built** (one commit for the code, tests and documents, 740e6ac; a second for this entry and for what a sweep and a run without mpmath found after it).
- **The nodes** (python/cft_golden/lang/graph.py, check.py, interp.py). `exp(a)`, `expm1(a)`, `exp2(a)`, `log(a)`, `log1p(a)` and `log2(a)` with an operand that is not a constant are step-graph nodes named as transcend.py names the functions, in `OPS` after `sqrt` and among `ROUNDED`. Each is a built-in held to one argument, so the names stay reserved. The interpreter's operation table calls `transcend.compute(fmt, name, a, 0, rnd)` by the node's own name, under the program's attribute; the result is correctly rounded with its exact flags. `transcendental` still refuses the rest of the reserved list (sin, cos, pow, hypot, log10 and the rest), M2 to M4's.
- **Folds and refusals** (check.py, `_fold_math`; Logan's answer to question 8). A function of a constant folds exactly where the value is rational, and nowhere else: exp(0) = 1, expm1(0) = 0, exp2(n) = 2^n for an integer n, log(1) = 0, log1p(0) = 0, log2(2^k) = k. The folded value is a constant like any other, rounded once where it meets the run. Every other function of a constant is `irrational-constant`, its sentence saying why: Lindemann-Weierstrass for e to a nonzero rational power and for the logarithm of a positive rational other than 1; 2 to a power that is no integer; log2 rational only at a power of two; a logarithm below its domain no real value, as sqrt(-4) has none. log(0), log2(0) and log1p(-1) are `constant-division-by-zero`, the name's definition widened to the poles. A function of a constant that changes with h's size is `h-nonlinear`. exp2 of an integer past 2^20 is `constant-range`.
- **The renderers** (render.py). The canonical form writes each as the language does. The mathematical form writes exp(a), expm1(a), 2^(a), ln(a), log1p(a) and log₂(a), one operation each: the conventional notation where there is one, and the numerical libraries' names for expm1 and log1p, since e^a − 1 and ln(1 + a) would print two operations. L prints as the exact rational it is.
- **The exact evaluation** (graph.py, `exact_transcendental`). Exact where the value is rational, and otherwise mpmath's value at 1,024 bits, the argument rounded to nearest at 1,024 bits first; expm1(a) is exp(a) - 1 and log1p(a) is log(1 + a) of the same fixed exp and log. It is a fixed function of the exact argument, as L4's root is. A logarithm at its pole or below its domain is Undefined, and so is a value past 2^±1048576. The tests' reader (python/tests/lang_mathform.py) and the tangent stage (programs/tangent_check.py, `_trans`) compute it again themselves.
- **The tangent rules** (tangent.py): exp `r * da`; expm1 `(1 + r) * da`; exp2 `(L * r) * da`; log `select(r == r, da / a, r)`; log2 `select(r == r, da / (L * a), r)`; log1p `select(r == r, da / (1 + a), r)`. r is read by name or written again where it has none. L is ln 2 rounded once at the program's format under its attribute: `constants.ln2_bits`, an integer series, the sum of 1/(k 2^k), bracketed and rounded at both ends until they agree. Its exact value is a const like any other, made only where exp2's or log2's rule reads it, written in the canonical form as any constant is - its hexadecimal significand at fp64, fp128 and fp256 (`0x1.62e42fefa39efp-1` at fp64 under rne), a decimal at fp32, where it terminates within 24 significant digits (0.693147182464599609375 under rne) - which reads back to itself. No new name, so the step stays minor (Logan's answer to question 6).
- **mpmath** (interp.py, `need_mpmath`). `lang.run` of a graph holding one of the six needs it. Without it the run raises `transcend.ZivEscalation`, naming mpmath and the functions, before any lane runs. A graph without the six never imports it, and checking, rendering and cftc's refusal of a source with the six never need it. The exact evaluation of such a graph raises ImportError, never an ArithmeticError that a check would read as "this point decides nothing". `cert2.TRANSCEND_OPS` holds the six, so a definition holding one needs mpmath, and without it `_evaluate` refuses it undecided: the failure the audit names `definition-unavailable`.
- **cftc** (python/cftc/__init__.py, `refuse_math`; refusals.py). `math-library`, first, on every target, at the first source line holding a call of one of the six, at run time or folded. The lines are the checker's (`StepGraph.math_lines`, never in the bytes). A graph read from bytes carries no lines: its run-time nodes are refused with no line, and its folds, constants like any other, compile as the source that writes those values does. VERSION stays 5, and no committed compiled byte moves.
- **The language at 1.1** (lang/version.py, its docstring recording the step). host/include/cft.h's `CFT_LANGUAGE_MINOR` is 1, its comment saying the ABI stays 0.18; `bindings/arduino/sync.py` re-vendored it; docs/HOSTAPI.md's table. certificates/corpus.py's recipe states the language's own version text (`LANGUAGE_TEXT`, as `PROFILE_TEXT` states the profile's), and the corpus was made again (`make --keep-version-1`): 24 certificates and their 24 MANIFEST lines moved. docs/CERTIFICATES.md's version-2 example follows its case.

## 2026-10-15 - M1's build, item 4: cftc compiles exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p and log2 as routines - the eight in routines.py under one statement of the invariants, per routine; a marked lane through a compiled image; the call loop over them; VERSION 6 with its record's block and the certificate corpus remade; Lotka-Volterra and two more variational references holding the six's rules; `math-library` lifted, `routine-unavailable` for a host without mpmath; the golden auditor's misnamed refusal fixed before it was reachable; a planted fault for every check (parcel MC)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "M1's build after E1") makes item 4 "cftc: ROUTINES and the internal check's widened invariants (question 12); the targets' refusals, and the call loop over unary routines; VERSION 6, with the outputs record's block and the certificate corpus remade (question 9); the Lotka-Volterra reference." Items 1 to 3 are merged: mathlib.py's six routines, program.c parity, and the language at 1.1, whose compiler refused the six `math-library` until this item. The design is docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, sections 1.2, 6 and 7, with Logan's answers of 2026-10-12, "Approve all as recommended (Recommended)": question 9 (VERSION 5 to 6, the corpus remade), question 11 (the generator in mathlib.py, `routines.py` handing its fragments to cftc by name, both ROUTINES learning the six) and question 12 (a raised live cap and spills measured on a reference step; an IOR rule in `flag_words`; RDN, RUP and the program's attribute inside a routine; no instruction reading only the input). On M2's study Logan approved (2026-10-14) a live cap per function and format for M2's fragments, which the structure below is made to take.

The box's figures are the lead's, marked so.

**Five decisions made for me, by the lead, on 2026-10-15** (each asked with its cause; the ledger has the questions):
1. **`routine-unavailable`, a new compiler refusal,** for a run-time call of the six on a host without mpmath, through which mathlib.py derives every constant of their routines. It is the one compiler refusal that depends on the host: the same source and target on a host with mpmath compile, or are refused by another name such as `target-feature`. It is raised after the refusals of the arguments alone (`segment-steps`, `target-format`, a run value's) and before anything builds a fragment, so before `target-feature`, which reads the built image: on a revision-7 target without mpmath such a source is `routine-unavailable`, with mpmath `target-feature`. No line: the cause is the host. A fold of the six needs no fragment and compiles there. `math-library` could not serve (the brief: the name goes), nor `definition-unavailable`, the certificate auditor's name in another list.
2. **`StepGraph.math_lines` went with `math-library`,** as `routine_lines` went with `runtime-routine` at C4: nothing else read it, and it was never in the bytes.
3. **The eight's one order is the language's,** `OPS`: div, sqrt, exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p, log2. It orders the routines' words in the bank and the call loop's batches at a tie, and division and root keep their places, so no existing image moves.
4. **The invariants: one statement in routines.py, per routine,** the values unchanged - division's and root's C4's, the six's mathlib.py's - and mathlib.py keeping views of them, so that test_mathlib.py and docs/studies/m2/costs.py run as they were.
5. **The golden auditor's recompile maps `routine-unavailable` to `definition-unavailable`** (exit 78), not `compiler-differs` (the alternative I proposed first): the study's question 10 names `definition-unavailable` for an auditor without mpmath, whichever step meets the cause first, and one name for one cause gives a certificate audited without mpmath the same refusal whether its run was compiled from the source or defined by it. The widening is kept to that one case.

Why this shape: a statement shared by all eight would have loosened division's and root's to the six's, so each routine names its own; and the live cap is by routine and format because that is the finest any routine needs - M2's fragments, whose caps Logan approved per function and format (22, 26, 17, 16), extend the table without moving another's. `flag_words` has the IOR rule (the set of pairwise ORs), sound - each rule's set holds every value the instruction can give - and on division's and root's words, which no IOR reaches, it proves what C4's walk proved (MEASURED at all 40). `invariants(f, live_cap, contract)` is mathlib.py's clauses and messages: well-formedness, the flag word within its contract, the live cap, every instruction reading a word or an internal value (none reading only the inputs, inline.py's argument), nothing left to simplify, the attributes its own; a fragment of no routine is refused by name.
