## 2026-10-16 - the long-run stress driver for the U50 card (parcel ST, Sonnet): `hw/card-stress.sh`, its report, and a dry run that exercises each stated policy; **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**Why.** Logan asked on 2026-10-16 for a long stress test of the card, to start that evening and run to Monday 2026-10-19 08:00: cycling across the card's capabilities, keeping metrics, using the quad image as much as the others, and using the time for lengthy sweeps. No script did that: hw/run-soak.sh and hw/run-c5-soak.sh each drive one artifact, and the card legs are minutes each, one image at a time. This parcel writes the driver; the lead runs it, on amd-arc-box, first as a smoke and then for the weekend. The card's results are the lead's, later. Marks: MEASURED (a run of this parcel's, on the desktop or in WSL (cft2204), niced, nothing on the box), READ (a file, named), COMPUTED (arithmetic on those), BELIEVED (unverified). The parcel's ledger is the round's ST.md.

**What was built** (files; `wc -l` at the commit, MEASURED):
- `hw/card_stress.py` (1,998 lines): the driver. `hw/card-stress.sh` (43): the launcher that sources XRT's setup.sh and picks python3.
- `hw/card_stress_lib.py` (786): the verdict parsers, the sweep's items and coverage arithmetic, the metrics file's reading and writing, the telemetry reader, the weighted rotation. `hw/card_stress_report.py` (1,316): the report, written by a second agent (general-purpose) from a spec of this parcel's and integrated and held to figures counted from the records by this parcel's own test.
- `hw/card_stress_standin.py` (349): the dry run's stand-in for every command. `hw/test_card_stress.py` (1,509), `hw/test_card_stress_report.py` (1,872), `hw/test-card-stress.sh` (29): the tests. `hw/card_stress_fixtures/` (15 real logs and an index): the verdict parsers' real input.
- docs/CARDDAY.md, "The long run": how to start, stop and read it, the settings, and what it guarantees and does not. docs/README.md recounted.

**The decisions, each with its ground.**
- **Opening an image is switching to it** (READ: host/src/backend_xrt.cpp `cftx_open`, `xrt::device(index)` then `load_xclbin(*xb)` of the bytes it read and hashed, each compute unit `cu_access_mode::exclusive`). There is no program step to script. XRT treats loading the xclbin already there as a no-op (docs/HOSTAPI.md, "A tile a run was abandoned on"), so the cure for a tile left running is another image and then this one, and the failure policy does that.
- **On the quad the soaks are four processes, one a tile** (`CFT_XRT_TILES=1..4`; READ: docs/HOSTAPI.md, "One process per tile", which also records four processes on tiles 1-4 passing on the card on 2026-09-25 and a thousand small segmented sums at 431 ms on the quad against 91 ms on the single). A single process over four tiles cuts every 4,096-element call four ways. The battery legs open all tiles. The rate of a soak on a tile is **unmeasured**: run-soak.sh's header says only that every case crosses the bus.
- **The scripts are not run; their binaries are** (READ: hw/run-soak.sh:59-60 and hw/run-c5-soak.sh:86 wipe `$OUT/*.log` and the joblist; both run every job; both call `make -C host <tool>` without XRT=1). The driver generates the same job lines in the same order with the same seeds (hw/card_stress_lib.py `sweep_items`, 17 divsqrt and 51 clause-5 items) and slices them.
- **`nextup32` and `nextdown32` report 8 cases more than their range**, in every slice (READ: clause5_soak.c `drv_next32` runs `next_edges32` first, and counts eight; MEASURED on the real tool, `clause5-soak nextup32 0 1048576`: "1048584 cases"). A slice's case count is held exactly: `hi - lo` for the others, plus 8 for these two.
- **GNU `timeout -k` and `nice -n 10`, as measured** (MEASURED, WSL, coreutils 8.32): exit 124 at the limit when the leg dies on TERM; when it ignores TERM the group goes at the kill-after and Python sees -9 (a shell 137). `nice -n 10` adds to the caller's niceness (a test run under `nice -n 10` saw its legs at 19).
- **api-test neither ends nor extends the run of card failures** (it passes with a dead card). **The output directory stays outside the checkout** (READ: hw/card-segrun.sh:114-137 compares the build id the tools carry with the tree's now, and a tree with untracked files has another id): the default is `~/card-stress-out/...` and an `--out` inside the tree that git does not ignore is refused.
- **An unattended run survives its own defects and its tools' surprises**: an unexpected exception in a cycle is recorded (`driver_error`, with its traceback), what the run started is terminated, and the next cycle begins - the fifth in a row stops it; a sweep item whose slices keep giving logs no parser can read (more than `--quarantine-after` in a row) is disabled and recorded rather than starving every other item (it never counts as served, so it would be picked again at once, every wave); a metrics file whose last line a killed run left torn is repaired on `--resume` (the torn bytes kept beside it) instead of fusing the next record to it; and `cft-resident` and `cft-selftest`, which serve optional legs, disable only their own leg if not built or not XRT-linked.
- **Counts are read, not defaulted.** Every parser quotes the printf it matches and fails (a `parse_error` leg, its log kept whole) on a missing, doubled, damaged or exit-status-contradicted verdict line; hw/test_card_stress.py also finds each parser's wording in the tool's own source, so a reworded tool fails the test.

**What the tests showed** (MEASURED):
- **A first dry run** (17:25, this desktop, Miniconda's Python 3.12.9, fake images with their SHA256SUMS, `--dry-run --quick`): exit 0 in 28 s, 38 leg records (36 pass; 2 skipped by name: `acceptance-rev8` on the single, which has no entry, and on the deep, whose entry is a 40-minute compile with no cached image), 55 records in all. It found three defects before the harness existed (a KeyError for a single-tile sweep job; one failing telemetry report switching every report to text mode; the stand-in's header on the stdout the telemetry parser reads), all fixed.
- **The parsers on real logs** (group `parsers`, 117 checks): the software backend's own runs of the same tools, made in WSL from this tree's sources and kept verbatim in `hw/card_stress_fixtures/` (INDEX.txt: each command, exit status and time): api-test; device-test `sw` at -q -n 8 (2,516 checks), -n 256 (10,156), -r (2,322) and -b -n 256 (4,838); `divsqrt-soak sqrt32` over 2^20 encodings (5 s) and `div32`; `clause5-soak nextup32` ("1048584 cases": the +8 read above, seen on the tool), `rint32`, `conv32to64`; the two soaks' own sabotage controls (real failing runs: 65,536 and 32 value mismatches, operands printed); seq_check `--device sw` (741 programs, 259 refused by both, 47 s); acceptance.py `--device sw` (1 of 1, 16 checks, 12 s) and `--set rev8 --target u50-rev8-quad` (1 of 1, 27 checks, 87 s). The card's own quoted lines (docs/VALIDATION.md, 2026-10-06: "acceptance rev8: 9 of 9 PASS on ... as u50-rev8-quad (set); 115 checks ok, 0 failed, 353 s" and rev8a's "20 of 20, 174 checks") parse too. Each parser is also given its log with the verdict line removed, doubled, damaged or contradicted by the exit status, and must refuse it; and each wording a parser reads is found in the tool's own source, so a reworded tool fails the test.
- **The legs' commands** (group `commands`, 25 checks): read off a Driver without running it: the flags of each leg against the brief, the eight entries and the two left out, the single's skipped leg, the cache, every-third-visit selftest, the four tile-pinned jobs of a quad wave, the probe and the rate-sized slice, the 2^28 cap.
- **The driver as a process against the stand-ins**, groups normal (18 checks: the whole `--quick` dry run), fail (6), timeout (6), deaf (2, POSIX), nodevice (6: the ladder), cardlost (6: N consecutive failures stop it, exit 3, STOPPED.txt), stopfile (5: the leg running finishes, nothing starts after, a stale STOP refused), deadline (4), rotation (2: the visits are the weighted rotation, four of six on the quad), diskfloor (2), guard (8: a card user refuses the start, verify/run.sh is allowed and recorded, one appearing mid-run is waited out and nothing is killed), sweep (9: run A loses the device until it stops, run B resumes the same directory and starts at the slice that failed), disagree (6), telemetry (8), build (6: a wrong or missing SHA256SUMS, a wrong hash, an `--out` inside the checkout, each refused before any leg), buildreal (7, POSIX: the real `make` of the named targets in a scratch copy of the tree, the `ldd` assertions both ways, a make that cannot find XRT, and the real api-test through the driver), internal (2: an injected fault in a cycle is recorded and the run goes on), signal (4, POSIX), report (7: the report's figures against counts made here from the records).
- **The negative controls** (group `plants`): a CONTROL (an unmodified copy of the code passes the normal, fail, nodevice and parser checks) and then 20 plants, each a defect put back into a copy of the code - the timeout not classified, the stop file ignored, the guard blind, the disk floor unchecked, a failed slice counted covered, another image's SHA-256 unchecked, a soak that ran on software passing, nextup32's edge cases forgotten, the second failure not reloading, the run never stopping for a lost card, a log with no verdict passing, an `--out` in the tree accepted, the XRT-link assertion dropped, the exit status unchecked, a count defaulted to 0, an unexpected exception ending the run, SIGTERM unhandled, an unreadable sweep item never disabled, a torn metrics tail not repaired, an optional tool that is not XRT-linked stopping the whole run - and each must be caught **at the check written for it**. All 20 were caught at the check written for them (the log lists each, with its first failing checks), and the control passed all of its checks. One is caught by a crash rather than a failed check, by design: with the parser that lets a log with no verdict line through, the driver itself dies on an IndexError, which that plant's expected checks list among the detections.
- **Defects the harness found in its own plants** (fixed): the first draft's plants ran the driver from a copy whose default `--root` was the copy's parent, so the build step refused to start and every plant went red for that one reason; and two plants went uncaught at their check (a failed slice redone before the restart hid the defect; a scenario crashed before reaching its check).
- **Where it ran**: the whole suite, plants included, under WSL (cft2204: Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10.12, gcc 11.4, niced): **287 checks, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 800 s**; and everything but the plants on Windows (Git Bash, Miniconda's Python 3.12.9): **248 checks, 0 failed, 3 skipped by name** (deaf, buildreal and signal, which need POSIX), 327 s; nothing on amd-arc-box or the card. Two driver processes at once on one host see each other's stand-ins as foreign card users (the guard working), so the runs were made one at a time per host.
- **The report** (`hw/test_card_stress_report.py`, the second agent's, 4,196 checks, 0 failed, 2.5 s on Windows and under WSL): three views of each figure (an oracle in the test that calls nothing of the report, `summarize()`, the rendered text), ten record mutations, seventeen tamperings of the finished summary, truncated, corrupted, empty and missing files; and this parcel's own end-to-end check, above.

**Estimates** (marks as stated; none measured on the card):
- **The smoke**, `--quick`: **24 to 28 minutes** on the card (COMPUTED from the 2026-10-06 records: card-segrun 169-185 s an image, device-test's three matrices about 2, 11-14 and 2 s, the acceptance set 371-384 s for 20 entries so about 40 s for the two it runs, the revision-8 set 353 s for nine on the quad; BELIEVED for api-test, `dt-i`, seq-check (50-79 s on the software backend; 60-120 s assumed), the sweep's slices (at most 180 s an image by setting), an image load). If it runs past 30 minutes, the believed parts are the suspects. Outside it: the host build, and the revision-8 entry's 51 s compile on the quad if no cache is seeded.
- **A long-run cycle on the quad**: about 19 minutes of battery (COMPUTED from the same records plus cft-resident's 20-40 s) and 45 of sweep, so about 65 minutes; about 13 of battery and 20 of sweep on each single image; about 46 quad cycles and 11 or 12 each of single and deep in 63 hours (COMPUTED from the weights 4:1:1). With selftest every third visit (about 10 minutes an image, docs/VERIFICATION.md's card row) the cycles are longer.
- **Sweep coverage is a function of the unmeasured rate.** With exhaustive items at 43.75 per cent of sweep time (14 items of weight 3 against 54 random items of weight 1) and about 525,000 tile-seconds in 63 hours (four tiles for 45 minutes of each quad cycle, one tile for 20 of each other), COMPUTED: the exhaustive items get about 230,000 of those tile-seconds, and the 14 x 2^32 = 6.0 x 10^10 encodings need 60,000 of them at 10^6 cases a second a tile (a quarter: covered, with the rest of the time going to the random items), 600,000 at 10^5 (so about 38 per cent covered) and 6,000,000 at 10^4 (about 4 per cent). The smoke's `sweep` rates (status.txt) replace these.

**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge).
- **The driver has not run against the card.** The build step is exercised for real only as far as this host can: `make` of the named targets (XRT=0) in a scratch copy, a fake `ldd`, the build-id and clause-5 probes (the `buildreal` group); a make that cannot find XRT and tools `ldd` says are not linked both stop the run. That the XRT=1 build, the real device legs and the soaks behave on the card as their records say is the lead's smoke.
- **The telemetry JSON's shape is BELIEVED** (no card output was read): numbers are kept under their neighbours' labels; a sample with none is recorded as such. Which of `xrt-smi` and `xbutil` answers `examine -r electrical` on the card is not known; the driver tries both, the one that worked first. `mechanical` may not be a report this card has; it is recorded as an error each sample and the others still read.
- **The seq-check leg's time on a card, the soaks' rate and the first revision-8 compile on the box are unknown.** Timeouts are generous (seq-check 2,400 s, a soak job three times its slice plus 120 s).
- **The guard sees processes by command line and environment**: a card user with no name it knows is invisible to it, and so is one that starts mid-leg (it collides, and the leg fails by the policy).
- **A disagreement is recorded, not investigated**: the driver does not re-run a disagreeing slice on the software backend, which would tell a tile's fault from the oracle's or the library's.
- **The 40-minute and 2.2-hour revision-8 compiles are not run by the driver** (no background compile): the entries run only where `--rev8-images` holds their image and bank, else they are named as left out. Seeding that directory from the W8 images is the lead's.
- **Three parsers were held to less than real logs**: `selftest`'s (cft-selftest needs `vectors/out`, which the scratch copy lacked) and `resident`'s are held to their source's text alone, and `dt-b`'s command (`-b -n 4096`, docs/VERIFICATION.md's card row) was run only as `-b -n 256` on the software backend. A `parse_error` leg is a failure the driver cannot call a wrong answer or a lost card, and the report counts it apart.
- **The report agent's test file is large** (1,872 lines, 4,196 checks): I ran it on both Pythons and checked the report end to end from the records, and read its controls' list and the report's handling of damaged files, but did not read all of it.
- **The XRT=1 build and every real device leg are the lead's smoke**, as above; so is the first look at what `xrt-smi` and `xbutil` print.
- **There is no runner stage for this driver's tests** (adding one would move the stage counts CLAUDE.md and docs/VERIFICATION.md state, which are the lead's): `bash hw/test-card-stress.sh` runs them, about 5 minutes on Windows and 10 under WSL with the plants, and `--no-plants` is shorter.
- The POSIX-only checks (`nice`, `timeout`, a process that ignores SIGTERM, the real build) are skipped by name on Windows and run in WSL or on the box.

**Appended note, same day, after the runs above** (this entry's own correction, so it stays append-only): the guard's list of tools that open an xclbin had `hw/verify-image.sh` in it, which reads an image with `xclbinutil` and never opens the card, and which the gate's `images` stage runs; tonight's gate run could have made the driver refuse to start. It is out of the list (hw/card_stress.py `XCLBIN_TOOLS`), docs/CARDDAY.md's guard bullet says so, and the `commands` group gained five checks of the guard's matching rules on synthetic command lines (what is and is not a card user, `xbutil examine` among the latter), now 30 checks, with a plant that puts `verify-image.sh` back, caught at its check: 21 plants. The counts in this entry's results are the runs before that change; after it, WSL's `parsers,commands,normal,fail,guard,buildreal` gave 186 checks, 0 failed, 68 s, and Windows' `parsers,commands,normal,fail,guard,report` 184 checks, 0 failed, 72 s, and the new plant alone was caught. The full suite was not run again after it.

## 2026-10-19 - the card's long stress run, closed: 61 hours on the three revision-8 images, 4,086 legs and 0 failures, 3,287 sweep slices and 0 disagreements, the 14 exhaustive fp32 items complete; and which of the sweep's items reached the tile

**What Logan asked,** on 2026-10-16, quoted whole in the sixth wave's closing record: a long run on the card "cycling across all of its capabilities and keeping metrics on it", from that evening to Monday morning, "Ideally utilize the quad tile image as well, the more work on the card the better, we can also use the time for lengthy sweeps if it would prove useful as well".

**The sources** (READ):
- the run's report.txt, status.txt, settings.json and metrics.jsonl;
- each copied from amd-arc-box after the run ended, its SHA-256 equal to the box's;
- metrics.jsonl: 7,982,931 bytes, 5,108 records, sha256 e7989f88efded691ea7461e921840d8de5d449e069980f6ba92e6a8f87e007cc;
- report.txt: sha256 4a426b57d752a5b135714f6f4ef45f0844e58be2485e2c92ff7c923a9ffa1e04.

The figures marked COMPUTED are the lead's, from that metrics.jsonl.

**The run:**
- **The driver:** hw/card-stress.sh, parcel ST's (verifier-VST: 0, 0), from a clone at f0693b2, clean, out /data/card-stress-1016.
- **The images:** the quad (4 tiles, sha256 4f9921a25af6...), the single (0639248e9c66...) and the deep (bbf08fb3feb6...). The extended revision-8 entries ran because the run's revision-8 images directory was seeded from W8's compiles (the sixth wave's record).
- **Start and end:** started 2026-10-16 18:58:23; ended 2026-10-19 08:01:13, "reason deadline, exit 0, cycles 67". It ran 74 s past the 08:00 deadline because a leg running then finishes (card-segrun on the quad, 189.1 s). The wall span was 219,770 s (2 d 13 h 02 m 50 s).
- **The cycles:** 67 in all, the quad 45, the single 11 and the deep 11. In verifier-VSR's words: "each visit a battery and then sweep slices, except the last: the quad's 45th visit (cycle 67) ran 7 of its 12 battery legs, api-test to card-segrun, and no sweep slice, because the deadline passed while card-segrun ran."

**The legs** (READ): 4,086 recorded.
- **Pass:** 4,032; fail, timeout, no_device, parse_error and error 0 each.
- **Skipped:** 54.
  - The selftest runs every third visit of an image: 43 skips (29 on the quad, 7 each on the single and the deep).
  - acceptance-rev8 on the single: 11 skips. The revision-8 set has no entry for u50-rev8 by its rule.
- **What a visit's battery runs:**
  - api-test; device-test's legs i, q8, full, r and b;
  - card-segrun; seq-check;
  - the acceptance set: 20 of 20 entries, 174 checks;
  - the revision-8 set: 9 entries and 115 checks on the quad, 1 entry and 27 checks on the deep;
  - the resident tool; and the selftest: 1,072,415 cases a run, COMPUTED as 16,086,225 over the quad's 15 runs.
- **Every battery leg gave the same counts on every visit on which it ran:** 35 groups by image and leg, each one distinct set of counts once the reported seconds are left out (COMPUTED). The selftest ran on 15 of the quad's 44 visits that reached it and 4 each of the single's and the deep's 11; the single's acceptance-rev8 never ran (VSR, COMPUTED).
- **The battery's rates held:** the report's trends run from -4.0% (dt-q8 on the deep) to +3.5% (the selftest on the single). Two spreads sit inside them (VSR): dt-i on the quad ran at 2.4 or 9.0 checks a second, the 22 fast visits each following a quad visit and the 23 slow ones following another image or none (COMPUTED; the cause is the image's load, BELIEVED); and acceptance-rev8's first visit on the quad took 2,189 s, its compile.

**The sweep** (READ, the report; COMPUTED, the splits):
- **3,287 slices,** each passed, no disagreement in any. 1,356,316,228,303 cases, each tool counting in its own unit, in verifier-VSR's words: "checks (an operand and an exponent) for scaleb, in-range operand-and-target pairs for cvtto (four integer targets, about two an operand), and lanes a source type (four to an operand) for cvtfrom."
- **The 14 exhaustive fp32 items:** 60,129,542,144 of 60,129,542,144 encodings (100.000%), each item one interval.
- **54 random items:** banded samples, the n-th slice of an item seeded `base_seed + 7919 * n`.
- **Which items reached the tile.** host/include/cft.h, "The remaining clause-5 operations", READ: cft_rint, cft_scaleb and cft_cmp_sig are COMPOSED, "on a device it runs on the tile". Every other clause-5 operation is HOST, "results are bit-identical on every backend by construction". host/src/clause5.c has "remainder: host". Division and square root are the tile's.
  - **35 items ran on the tile:** their floating-point work is the tile's passes, with the host keeping integer bookkeeping. cft_scaleb takes a host path for exponents below the subnormal floor (clause5.c 461-501), which the soak's lists carry 2 of 17 at fp32 and 2 of 27 at fp64 (VSR, READ).
    - sqrt32 and rint32, five attributes each, exhaustive: 42,949,672,960 encodings in 175 slices;
    - div32, div64 and sqrt64 under four attributes, rint64 under five, scaleb32 and scaleb64 under four: 371,591,340,032 cases in 1,413 slices.
  - **33 items ran libcft's host code on the box's CPU,** with the card open:
    - nextup32, nextdown32, logb32 and class32, exhaustive: 17,179,869,480 cases in 74 slices, 4 x 2^32 and nextup's and nextdown's eight edge cases a slice;
    - the 64-bit next, logB and class, the format and integer conversions, and the remainder: 924,595,345,831 cases in 1,625 slices.
  - **So "on the card" holds for the 35.** The 33 test the library under a device's context, and the software backend on any CPU gives them the same assurance (BELIEVED, from cft.h's "bit-identical on every backend by construction"). Parcel EX found this, reading cft.h, on 2026-10-19.

**Telemetry** (READ, the report; COMPUTED, the extremes' times): 865 samples, none without values.
- **The FPGA:** 28 to 40 C, mean 34.65; 40 C last at 2026-10-18 18:12:55.
- **The card's power:** 15.40 to 34.38 W, mean 20.87.
  - The 34.38 W sample, at 2026-10-18 13:02:29, fell inside the quad's resident leg (13:02:27 to 13:02:31).
  - The next highest sample was 23.47 W.
- **The host:** load (one minute) 2.04 to 6.74; memory available 43,420 to 45,330 MB of 48,061.

**Uptime** (READ): in legs 219,550 s, 99.9% of the wall span. The longest gap between legs was 1.215 s, and no gap was over 300 s. That counts any leg: a leg using the tile ran in 71.6% of the wall span, host items' jobs filling the rest, and the quad's sweep phases averaged 2.98 of 4 jobs running (VSR, COMPUTED).

**Known limits:**
- **The HBM temperature reads 0** in 670 of 865 samples (mean 7.2 C, maximum 35), where the sixth wave's smoke saw it in 3 of 10 (VSR). Several of XRT's rails, the 12 V auxiliary among them, read 0 on this card.
- **The random samples do not accumulate.** A random item's seed number is rebuilt from the run's own metrics.jsonl (hw/card_stress.py, hw/card_stress_lib.py `seed_for`), so a new run in a new directory repeats these seeds, so the same streams, from their start (the lead's reading, 2026-10-19; VSR's words). A slice's length is set by the measured rate, so where two runs' lengths differ one slice is a prefix of the other. Parcel SC's study takes it up.
- **The units differ by item.** The sweep's case totals add items whose tools count different things (above); "1.36 trillion" is a count of the tools' cases, not of operands.

**Who ran it:** the lead, on amd-arc-box; no agent touched the card. verifier-VSR (Sonnet) checked this record at f539a2a: (a) 0, (b) 2, both restated here in its words, and eight of its nine other notes taken; the ninth, divsqrt_soak.c's header still saying it "cannot validate ... the tile itself" against its own main(), is a follow-up.

## 2026-10-19 - M1's build, item 6, the software side: the math library's six routine references join the revision-8 set, each with a structured lane a tile that marks (bit 7 of its byte, STATUS[6]); a version-1 certificate carries no per-lane block, so the driver reads it through libcft by ctypes; the record remade whole, its ten entries reproduced byte for byte and six added (parcel MA, Sonnet)

**Why.**
- docs/ROADMAP.md's plan of record for the math library, M1's build after E1, item 6: "The card, the lead's: STATUS[6] and the lane byte on a structured argument, and a routine case in the acceptance sets"; the study's section 8, item 8, says the same of revision 8's images. A routine needs flag control (FLAG_CONTROL, CAPS2[14]); no revision-7 target publishes it, so the case can enter the revision-8 set alone, not the acceptance set (READ: python/cftc/targets.py, the revision-7 targets' feature word has no FLAG_CONTROL and the revision-8 targets' do; MEASURED: `cftc.targets.get(t).features()` has neither FLAG_CONTROL nor LANE_FLAGS for u50-rev7 and u50-rev7-quad and both for u50-rev8, u50-rev8-quad and u50-rev8-deep; all six committed manifests' `accepted_by` is sw, u50-rev8, u50-rev8-quad, u50-rev8-deep; `asm.Image.features()` of each image reports FLAG_CONTROL among kx, REGS32, BANK_PTR, SCRATCH and SCRATCH_IO; and cftc compiles lotkavolterra-rk4-tangent-fp64.cftl for u50-rev7-quad to `Refusal: target-feature: the image needs FLAG_CONTROL (CAPS2[14]), which u50-rev7-quad does not publish`, and for u50-rev8-quad to 12,328 bytes, the committed image's size, in 0.8 s). The card's runs are the lead's. This entry is the software side: what the driver now holds, and what the lead's commands (docs/CARDDAY.md) expect.
- Marks: MEASURED by this parcel, on the Windows desktop, niced, one process at a time, the desktop shared with other sessions and no load added; READ in a named file; COMPUTED from figures here; BELIEVED, not checked. Nothing here touched amd-arc-box or the card.

**What was built** (files; MEASURED at 7fc03ab by `git show --stat` and `wc -l`: programs/acceptance.py 1,510 to 2,437 lines, programs/acceptance-rev8.json 474 to 1,332, python/tests/test_acceptance_marks.py 289 new, verify/run.sh 17 lines changed).
- `programs/acceptance.py`: `REV8_ROUTINES` (six: Lotka-Volterra in logarithmic variables - exp -, two diodes and a source - expm1, log1p - and a self-heating culture - exp2, log, log2 - each at fp64 and fp256, `programs/systems/compiled-tangent/`'s committed images and banks) and `STRUCTURED` (per entry, one lane a tile, the tile's fourth, one state component set to a centre of the function's structured family at rne); `reference_lanes(tiles=)`, `centre_bits` (softfloat alone, equal to `mathlib_family.argument`), `structured_lanes`; the mark probe (`LaneProbe`, ctypes mirrors of cft_run_args, cft_open_args, cft_caps and cft_image_id's prefix; `--lib`), `mark_probe`, `golden_mark_problems`, and the pure checks `block_problems`, `mark_problems`, `probe_device_problems`, `probe_run_problems`, `marked_record`; the record's keys `structured` (a parameter), `marked` and `lane_flags_sha256` (outcomes), for routine entries only; the controls `mark_controls` (17) and `reference_controls` (2); `rev8_controls` no longer assumes a workload first entry; the revision-8 oracle skips routine entries. `REV8`, the ten, is untouched byte for byte.
- `programs/acceptance-rev8.json`: remade by the driver, sixteen entries.
- `python/tests/test_acceptance_marks.py` (new, 17 tests): the set (the ten, the six, the quad by the rule), the acceptance set's references building the lanes they built (their init digests are `programs/acceptance.json`'s), the recipe's shape, each function one the entry's manifest holds, each centre in FAMILY at rne and demanded marked by the theory, the control's off-centre argument clear by the theory, and every mark check green on a block the recipe describes and red, by name, on a planted fault.
- `verify/run.sh`: `REV8_CENSUS` +6, the stage builds the shared library and passes `--lib`; `docs/VERIFICATION.md`, `docs/CARDDAY.md`, `docs/PROGRAMS.md`, `programs/README.md` and `README.md`: the sets' contents, the stage's row, the card commands; docs/README.md recounted.

**The decisions, each with its ground.**
- **A version-1 certificate carries no per-lane block** (READ: host/tools/segrun.c asks the library for R23's byte a lane only when FORMAT_VERSION == 2, `blk` stays NULL at version 1 and `--lane-flags` beside `--format-version 1` is `usage`; MEASURED: cft-segrun at version 1 on Lotka-Volterra fp64 with four structured lanes, the software backend at 4,096 slots, 2.15 s: `segment 0 ... flags 29 status 64`, segments 1 to 3 `status 0`, and the states directory holds c.cert and the boundary files only, no `.flags`; cft-audit in full accepted it, 2.29 s). Version 2 would write the block and refuse the marked segment (`replay-missing`: cftc writes no image that decides its own routine's mark). So the lane byte, which the item asks for, cannot be held through the certificate. The driver reads it itself: a *mark probe*, libcft through ctypes (host/tests/seq_check.py's pattern; the lead's answer, 2026-10-19: "yes"), re-runs each segment from its certified start on the same device and image at the same depth, asking for the block. Held to the certificate: the probe's backend, tiles, image (an xclbin's SHA-256, where the certificate names one) and depth; each end state the boundary file, bit for bit; each flag word and STATUS; and R23's identities on every block. The alternatives: a change to cft-segrun or positive-run in C (outside this parcel), version 2 (refused), or the golden model alone for the byte (which would hold nothing of a device).
- **All six references, both formats.** Each is a different image on the card (the routines' constants and tables differ by format); the three together hold all six rules; no compile and no mpmath are needed; the cost is about two minutes.
- **One structured lane a tile.** The quad cuts the lanes into a block a tile and reassembles the lane block, so a mark path that fails on tile 2 alone shows only if a lane on tile 2 marks. The lane is the tile's fourth (past the spot check's lanes 0 to 2, clear of the special lanes at the tiles' ends), one state component at a centre, the tangent the recipe's. The centres are FAMILY's at rne: exp (1,53) (3,53) (-1,54) (-3,54) at fp64, the same at 237 and 238 at fp256, alternating the two exp call sites (u and v); the diodes alternate log1p (3,51) (-1,52) with expm1 (1,52) (-1,53); the culture's log has three centres (1 + 6 eps, 1 - 2 (eps/2), 1 - 12 (eps/2)) and repeats the first on tile 3. log1p's anchors, clear themselves, are left out. The lane marks in segment 0 and nowhere else: its argument is the centre only at the first stage of the first step.
- **Which entries cannot mark: none.** Each holds a function with a family at rne: exp, expm1 and log1p, log. exp2 and log2 have no family (parcel VMP; FAMILY's lists are empty at every format and attribute): the culture's lanes mark through log alone, and the culture's eight exp2 and log2 calls never mark.
- **`REV8` stays the ten, the six in `REV8_ROUTINES`.** READ: hw/card_stress.py hard-codes `REV8_ENTRIES`, and hw/test_card_stress.py's `rev8_table_matches` reads acceptance.py's `REV8 = (...)` text with `[a-z0-9_]+` names and requires `len(pairs) == 10`; the brief's "your entries reach it at its next run" is not so. MEASURED: that file's parsers and commands groups, 147 checks, 0 failed, with the new acceptance.py (0.7 s). The stress driver's table and its test are the follow-up; hw/ is untouched (the lead's answer).
- **The golden audit is not in the default run** (`golden` is empty, as for the workloads): the spot check re-runs the last segment on seq.py for the 16 spot lanes, the structured ones among them, and the golden mark check re-runs segment 0 for the same lanes and holds the bytes to the probe's. `--golden all` is the option, and passes (below).
- **The record was remade whole**, by the driver, with the ten workloads' images read back from the lead's copy of the box's (the lead's option (a): no `--merge`): the stronger check, since every existing entry is reproduced.

**Known limits, recorded.**
- **The probe is a re-run** of each segment, not the certificate's own run; the end-state, flag-word and STATUS equality shows it is the same run, and a device that gave two answers would fail it visibly. The segments run twice on a card.
- **Marks occur in segment 0 only** (the centre is met at the first step), so marks from the second segment on are not exercised; an ordinary lane's chance mark (about 2^-43 a call at G = 44, READ from the rate law of docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md) never occurs.
- **The culture's exp2 and log2 call sites** are exercised unmarked, as no family exists to mark them; the diodes' log1p and expm1 and Lotka-Volterra's exp have two to four centres each, the culture's log three.
- **Quad only.** rev8a and rev8d have no routine entry: the rule gives the quad all six and an entry has one target (`--target u50-rev8-deep` selects none: "FAIL the set: no entry of --only on u50-rev8-deep", MEASURED). The stress driver does not run the six (above).
- **The XRT path of the probe is untested** (cft_open of an xclbin, cft_get_image_id, the lane block on a tile through ctypes); the structs are mirrors of cft.h held by the library's size handshake, and the remote handle's path passed. A third copy of those mirrors is in the tree (gathertime.py and seq_check.py have the others).
- **The record holds each segment's block hash, not the block**: a mismatch names the segment, and the explicit checks name the lanes. Segments 1 to 3 have the same block, so a device that returned one in place of another would not be seen by the hashes (the probe's end-state check would).
- **Fp32 and fp128 are not in the set** (the references are committed at fp64 and fp256).
- **Times are of a shared desktop**: 67 s and 113 s for the same six at different hours; the golden audit of LV fp256 32 s and 47 s.
- **Unmeasured here**: the Linux and Python 3.10 path of the new code (the box's), the card.

## 2026-10-19 - M1's build, item 5: the stages replay a marked lane - one rule for every comparison of an image with lang.run (the interpreter run lane by lane, an unmarked lane bit for bit with its byte's flags, a marked lane replayed by the definition and its guess counted, FLAGS and STATUS held to the bytes), its controls on a hand-written marking image, and the math library's six compiled and run in the `lang-routines` and `tangent` stages with the structured families in the lanes; a planted fault for every check (parcel MS)

**Why.**
- The math library round's plan of record (docs/ROADMAP.md, "M1's build after E1") makes item 5 "the stages' legs: lang-routines and tangent, marked lanes replayed (question 10), and VERIFICATION's rows". Items 1 to 4 are merged: mathlib.py's six routines, program.c parity, the language at 1.1, and cftc carrying the six as routines at output version 6. Three sentences in the record left this item's work open: ML's known limit ("the rounding order is held golden-only; ... the compiled legs, a marked lane's replay among them, are item 5's"), MC's ("the stages don't replay marked lanes yet; leg G fails one by name") and VERIFICATION's tangent row ("its compiled legs with generated sources, a marked lane replayed, are item 5's"). The design is docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md, section 6's last paragraph and section 8's item 7, with Logan's answers of 2026-10-12 ("as recommended"): question 4 (the structured families keep their marks, the centres are listed in the tests, LANGUAGE.md states the rule) and question 10 (mpmath accepted in the language's checks, a stage without it skipping the six's legs by name).
- Logan on the models, 2026-10-13 (READ, the brief): "Use Sonnet for M1's build parcels as you recommended, it performed well". The author is Sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5); the verifier is Sonnet.
- Marks: MEASURED is a run of this parcel's on the desktop, niced, one process at a time, with its command; READ is a file, named; COMPUTED is arithmetic on those; BELIEVED is mine and not shown. **Wall-clock time on this desktop is no measure** (the same d3fef4b group took 174 s in one run and 354 s in another; a niced process there ran at about a quarter of a core, 87.8 CPU seconds in 366 s), and **CPU time is not steady either** (the parent's CPU for nearly the same group was 87.8 s and 55.7 s), so every cost below is given with its run and as a proportion inside one run where it can be; the box's figures are the lead's, marked so.
- The brief is the lead's, outside the tree; the ledger is `ledger/MS.md` in the round's records; the scratch tools (the plant driver, the CPU wrapper, the A/B of leg K, the comparison of two runs' check lines, the full-centre scan, the probes) are in the round's scratchpad for the verifier and not committed.

**The rule** (programs/lang_check.py: `Ref`, `judge`, `rule_compare`; the comment above them states it, and so does docs/LANGUAGE.md, "A marked lane"). `compare`, `compare_routine` and the tangent stage's `compare` all call it, so nothing else in either stage compares an image with lang.run. The interpreter is run lane by lane (`Ref`: lang.run of each lane alone, which is the lane as it is in the lockstep run, since the interpreter's lanes are independent), because a lang.run `Run` carries only the OR of the lanes' flags. At each checkpoint - the image's REPEAT patched to 1, 2, 5 and its own steps, each a run from the initial states:
1. **R1** an unmarked lane equals the definition bit for bit: its state, its tangents, its lane params (`lane-value`);
2. **R2** its byte is exactly the definition's flags for that lane, [7:5] clear (`lane-byte`);
3. **R3** a marked lane (byte [7]) is replayed: the definition's values and flags stand in for its own, as `cert2.replay_segment` makes a certified segment's. Its guess is counted, and reported where it is wrong in its values (its tangents among them) or its flags, and never required; its byte may carry nothing in [6:5];
4. **R4** FLAGS after the replay - the OR of the corrected bytes' [4:0] - equals lang.run's (`flags-replayed`);
5. **R5** STATUS is zero but for STATUS[6] (`status-other`);
6. **R6** STATUS[6] is set exactly when some byte is marked (`status-mark`);
7. **R7** FLAGS as the run reports it is the OR of the raw bytes' [4:0], seq.py's own statement of R23 (`flags-word`);
8. **R8** a mark is never lost between checkpoints (`marks-vanish`); and a block that is not a byte a lane is `block-length`.
- **A lane marked at one checkpoint and the next.** Each checkpoint is its own run from the initial states, judged against the definition of that many steps from the same states: nothing is carried from one checkpoint's replay to the next, as cert2 carries a segment's corrected end state into the next segment's start (READ: cert2.py `replay_segment` and `run_chain`; here there is no chain, each checkpoint is one segment whose start is the initial state). That is the definition's own rule: a lane's value after s steps is lang.run of that lane for s steps, a function of its initial state alone. The runs are one deterministic computation of which each shorter is the prefix, so a lane marked at s is marked at every later checkpoint (R8), its replay at the later one is the definition again from the initial state and never the earlier replay's end, and a lane marked only at the later one (its mark came after step s) is judged unmarked, bit for bit, at s.
- **What I had to ask of seq.py's run: nothing** (READ: python/cft_golden/seq.py, `Result.lane_flags`, "computed for every run, as the counts are"; MEASURED, a scratch probe: it holds one byte a lane, 40 for 40 lanes at every format). What I had to ask of lang.run is each lane's own FLAGS, which a Run does not carry: one call a lane with `at=` the checkpoints, the interpreter untouched.
- **For an image that marks no lane** the rule is the one before it - states, tangents, lane params, FLAGS, STATUS - with R2's per-lane bytes and R7 beside it. The evidence is under "What the runs showed".

**What was built** (the branch m1-stages, cut at d3fef4b; the code in 536bb12, 48a6be2, 7c6c2ae, dd9fc0b and 938f7ad, a comment in 391b1be, the records in the commit after; not pushed; `wc -l`, MEASURED):
- **programs/lang_check.py** (2,966 lines at d3fef4b, 4,375 now). The rule: `Ref`, `judge` (a pure function of the run's values, bytes, FLAGS and STATUS and the definition's, so that a control can plant a fault in a copy of a real run), `rule_compare` (which runs the image at the checkpoints and judges each), the thin `compare` and `compare_routine`, and the tally of what the rule saw (`MARKS`) and the six's (`SCOVER`). **Leg O**, the rule's 16 controls on markstep (`markstep_subject`, `Fixture`, `leg_rule`). **Leg N**: N1 `leg_six_alone`, N2 `g_six` and `leg_six_generated`, N3 `leg_six_loops`, joined as `leg_six`; the I2 tally's six part (`six_coverage`); `--six N` and `--six-all`. The module docstring restated. The routines group is now `routines, pools, loops, rule, six`.
- **programs/tangent_check.py** (2,316 lines at d3fef4b, 2,523 now). `compare` calls the rule. **Leg N** (`leg_six`, `six_controls`), `--six N` and `--six-all`; leg G's docstring and failure text say what a certificate does not do; the module docstring restated.
- **verify/run.sh** (+21 lines). The comments above the `lang-routines` and `tangent` stages and their one-line descriptions name the six and the rule. No logic.
- **docs/LANGUAGE.md.** "A marked lane" says what the stages do (the rule, the checkpoints, the certificates' limits), and the stage paragraph names the legs. **docs/VERIFICATION.md.** The top paragraph, the `lang`, `lang-routines` and `tangent` rows and the gate paragraph. **docs/studies/M1-exp-log.md.** A dated note. **docs/README.md.** Recounted.
- **Not changed, and said so:** mathlib.py, transcend.py, cftc, the language and its interpreter, cert2.py, the C tools, python/tests (so the golden suite's count, 5,222, does not move), the committed references and the certificate corpus, the card and the RTL. docs/ROADMAP.md and CLAUDE.md are the lead's and were not edited.

**The decisions, each with its ground.**
- **One interpreter run a lane.** The definition costs N calls where the lockstep run cost one, and that is not where the time goes (MEASURED, a profile of leg K at 8 sources: `rule_compare` 13.0 s in all, 12.4 s of it the image's runs on seq.py, so the rule's own part about 0.5 s; MEASURED, interleaved against d3fef4b's leg K, three rounds: the new code took 1.040 of the old at the least and 1.028 at the median).
- **The fixture for the rule's controls is a hand-written image that marks lanes on purpose,** the golden corpus's `markstep-fp64.cfta` (READ: certificates/corpus.py, which calls it the corpus's version-2 example, and certificates/programs/markstep-fp64.cftl and .cfta): lane k = 7 has a wrong last bit and k = 106 a right one, each raising the mark with invalid (0x81) where the definition raises inexact (0x10). The rule's 16 controls (leg O) run on it and need no mpmath, so the rule is tested on every host; the six's legs, whose golden functions need mpmath, are skipped by name without it.
- **The structured families decide which lanes the legs demand marked.** READ: python/tests/mathlib_family.py, `classify` says "mark" where the true value is within 0.7 of a rounding boundary in units of 2^-(p+G) |f(x)| (the bound of the routine's double-word value), "clear" past 1.3 of it, "either" between, and "gated" where the routine decides by other means. The legs put the committed centres in lanes and assert the first class marked, every lane of it; the other classes are counted and not asserted (over-marking costs a replay, never an answer).
- **A gate-sized draw, the larger behind a flag.** N1 samples each family's committed list (the anchor whose guess is wrong under round-to-nearest if the list holds it, the first three, the last and two spread between; the neighbours a unit in the last place above and, for the first three, below), N2 draws 12 sources (leg K draws 40, the tangent stage's corpus 24), and `--six N` / `--six-all` take every centre of each family, both neighbours, twelve ordinary lanes and the edges whole (and N2 up to twelve structured lanes a direct call, where the gate's has two).
- **Under Stormer-Verlet a structured argument marks a different call than under the other integrators** (MEASURED, scratch probe_sv.py): the language drifts q by h/2 times the position equation's right side before the force is called (READ: `let Q1.q = fma(h/2, p, q)` in the expansion), so a momentum equation's call reads the drifted position and a position equation's reads the initial momenta. `g_six` records as direct only the calls that read a component at the first step, and N1's Stormer-Verlet lanes hold p = 0, where the drift leaves q alone. The template is LANGUAGE.md's; the generator had to know it.
- **A refusal costs a compile.** `target-feature` is raised after the lowering, so four targets cost four compiles (MEASURED, scratch probe_refusal2.py, the gate's 12 generated sources of 378 to 5,226 instructions: one compile for sw 0.16 to 1.97 s, the four refusals 0.38 to 8.01 s, about four compiles). N1 asks all four of revision 7's targets of each function at one format (the format its place among the six decides), N2 asks every source of u50-rev7 and the first two of all four, and compiles the first two also for sw:4096 and sw:32768 to one image.
- **The tangent stage's marked lane is replayed whole.** lang.run of the lane alone gives its states and its tangents together (`Ref.vector`), so a marked primal lane's tangent is the definition's too, and a guess wrong in a tangent is counted apart (`wrong_tangents`). The structured arguments are put in the primal; a tangent comes from the primal's value through the rules of LANGUAGE.md's table.
- **Leg G's guard stays, and says why** (READ: docs/CERTIFICATES.md 2058-2090 and host/tools/segrun.c): leg G writes version-1 certificates, which hold the machine's guess and STATUS[6], and fails a segment that marks a lane, by name. cft-segrun's refusals `replay-missing` and `replay-undecided` are its version-2 writer's: with a source and no `--replay-image` it answers the former, and with an image that marks the lane too the latter, which no image of the six is. - **The lockstep comparison could not see a lane's own byte.** It compared lang.run's FLAGS, the OR of the lanes', with the image's; four of the `lang` stage's twelve plants leave every value right and move only flags, and were counted "0 of 8 lanes ... FLAGS differ". Under the rule each lane whose byte lacks a flag is counted: "8 of 8", "4 of 4". Verdicts unchanged (red), numbers printed not.
- **No defect in the compiled six, and no unmarked lane wrong anywhere.** Not in the full-centre scan (11,982 lanes), not in the larger draws (16,534 lanes in N1, 246 and 233 demanded lanes in the generated sources and systems), not in the gate's. Every lane the theory demands marked was marked (642, 23, 44, 21 at the gate's draw; 11,274, 246, 233 in the larger). The guesses wrong are six arguments (above), always marked.
- **Under Stormer-Verlet a structured argument marks a different call than under the other integrators** (above): nothing wrong, the generator had to know the template.
- **cft-segrun's `replay-missing` and `replay-undecided` are its version-2 writer's** (above): the brief and MC's known limit gave them as what leg G meets, and it meets neither. Leg G's text now says both.
- **A refusal costs a compile,** so the legs ask all four of revision 7's targets of a few sources only (above).
- **My first control for "a lane marked that did not need to be" planted a mark at one checkpoint only, and R8 turned it red**: a mark planted must persist as a real one does. The control was wrong, the rule right; O5 plants it from a step onward.
- **A plant that crashes is not a red check.** R9's first plant removed the early return as well and raised a traceback; the harness counted rc 1 as red, and I read the output and redid it (above). The harness reports a count of traceback lines beside the FAIL lines, which is how this one showed.
- **Timing on this desktop is noise at the factor of two,** in the clock and, less, in CPU time (above). It is why the costs here are proportions inside one run, and why the leg K A/B is interleaved.

**Known limits, recorded rather than fixed** (Logan's rule).
- **The rule is the stages'; a certificate still cannot replay.** cft-segrun and cft-audit are unchanged. Leg G writes version-1 certificates, which hold the machine's guess and STATUS[6], and fails a segment that marks a lane, by name; the twelve references mark none in any run (MEASURED, leg G's 12 "no segment marks a lane"). Version 2's writer replays only by an image of the source that decides the lane, and no image of the six does.
- **A wrong guess is rare and anchored; the stages do not require one.** 6 lanes of the 11,982 of the full scan, all at the rne anchors; the gate's N2 and the tangent stage's N hold none (23 and 21 marked lanes, all right), so the tolerance of a wrong guess is shown on real lanes by N1's and N3's anchors and on a planted one by leg O and the tangent controls. If mathlib.py's routines come to guess right there, those lanes stay in the draw and the count of wrong guesses is 0; nothing fails, and the controls still hold the tolerance. P6's proof is the controls (above) for the same reason.
- **The theory's "must mark" is asserted, its "must not mark" is not.** `mathlib_family.classify` says "mark", "clear" or "either"; the legs assert the first and do not look at the others (over-marking costs a replay, not an answer; test_mathlib.py holds the rate, and the legs report marked beside demanded: 664 marked against 642 demanded in N1, the surplus being "either" lanes and neighbours).
- **fp32, exp2 and log2 mark nothing by the families:** fp32's windows are empty at G = 40 and exp2 and log2 have none, so the legs run them on ordinary, special and edge lanes and report 0 marked, 0 demanded.
- **Under Stormer-Verlet the momentum equations' calls get no structured lane,** since they read the drifted position: they are compared under the rule like every other lane, but no mark is demanded of them.
- **The draws are gate-sized.** Beyond the sample of each family's list (above) the lanes are the generators' own; a mark that appears in a lane the theory did not demand ("either" lanes, neighbours, a second step's value) is replayed and counted, not asserted.
- **Without mpmath the six's legs are skipped, shown by simulation** (`sys.modules["mpmath"] = None`), not on a host without it; leg O needs none.
- **R7 is seq.py's own contract.** FLAGS as the run reports it is the OR of the bytes' [4:0] "over the lanes the run owns", except where ACTALL wakes a lane past `n_active` (READ: seq.py's docstring; tb/test_seq_core.py's `actall_over_a_ragged_block`); no compiled image does that, none failed R7 here, and one that came to would be red by name (`flags-word`).
- **The stages whole through the runner are the lead's.** I ran the routines group whole on the desktop (the lead's reply to my message, about 06:00), the `lang` core group whole, and the tangent stage in two pieces (197 checks and E with F); I did not run them through `verify/run.sh`, nor on amd-arc-box or the card, which agents do not touch. The runner's own environment (the tools it builds, its logs) is the lead's to confirm.

Each plant is described above by file and change, and the harness with its anchors and the unplanted runs is in the round's scratchpad.

## 2026-10-19 - the project's figures: fifteen, made by script from committed data and held to the numbers the record states, checked on every gate run; restated after verifier-VFG's four (b)s and its re-check's two (parcel FG, Sonnet 5.5)

**What Logan asked,** verbatim, on 2026-10-19: "As a 'standalone' parcel, I'd like to create some more visualizations of the data collected and progress made across the project, dispatch a Sonnet agent with the task of simply creating visualizations/charts/graphs/etc from data sourced from the project, created via script (Point them at the StoryDocs repo for examples on how figures were generated, or the ones already present in this projects readme as well) to ensure they stay accurate like the rest of the project. The main 'goal' of this parcel is just to have more visual content about the project, not any specific portion. The stress data will likely be useful for it, but as its not finished yet, either give an early snapshot of the results to use or simply instruct it to wait until the sweep finishes." The parcel used the long run's final files (card-stress-1016, ended 2026-10-19 08:01:13) and none of its partial data. Nothing here ran on the card or on amd-arc-box.

**What verifier-VFG found, and what changed.** The first version (dfeb249) went to verifier-VFG (Sonnet 5.5): 0 (a) and 4 (b), so under Logan's rule it came back; the fixes are the commits after dfeb249 on branch figures (the code and figures, then these records), and this entry is restated in place, before any push, to say what is true after them. VFG recomputed all fifteen figures with its own code and viewed all thirty renderings; thirteen were true as drawn and captioned in their numbers, and the two that were not are (b1) and (b2) below ((b3) is a reading of numbers it found right). Its re-check of the fixes (3f59da3) found 0 (a) and 2 (b) more, **(b1') and (b2')** after the first four, with small notes; they, and verifier-VEX's (a) from a trial merge with soak-exhaustive, are the later commits on the branch, and this entry is restated again. Its four (b)s, each with its evidence (READ in VFG's ledger) and what changed:
- **(b1) hw-clock's "every" was false.** The ledger states a kernel slack for seven U50 builds that were not drawn: 2 Sep, the case-ROM single (+0.433), the tip quad (+0.143) and the tip single (+0.618); 14 Sep, the narrow fp64/fp128 single (+0.253), the first revision-5 image (+0.308), the R14 image (+0.191) and the seq6 image (+0.140). With them there were 43 builds, 5 missed, and the quad closed 135 MHz 10 times, with slack up to +0.143. I re-read the ledger's U50 timing statements myself (a scan of every line that pairs a slack with a WNS) and agree on the seven, and found a third whole-design miss VFG did not list. Fixed: the seven are drawn (the patterns capture the numbers; the identification of each image is mine), and the caption, the alt text, the figure's subtitle and its bottom text said what was drawn and what was not and rested "every" on a scan of entries - which the re-check (b1') found still too strong, so that claim is gone too.
- **(b2) stress-timeline's "Every other leg ran on every visit and passed"** was contradicted by its own table: the quad's 45th visit, cycle 67 (07:57:36 to 08:01:13), was cut by the deadline after 7 of its 12 battery legs (api-test to card-segrun) and ran no sweep slice, so seq-check, acceptance, acceptance-rev8, resident and selftest read 44 against 45 visits. I checked the raw records (cycle_end: 7 legs, 216.8 s) and agree. Fixed: "but the last", with the cut visit named, computed from the cycles, and a claim that the per-leg counts agree with it (selftest counts 15 passes and 29 skips, 44 in all).
- **(b3) the ledger note's reading** ("only those 3 lines belonged to an entry that was no longer the newest, which is the case the rule rules out; the rest restate the entry being written") counted by position, not by push state: by origin/main's reflog only 28 of the 518 deleted lines were text that had been pushed, in 7 commits (d9b5ac4, bb448e0, 3b27a7a, 1678747, 71eb3f1, f0156c9, ef6d9f5), and of my 3 older-entry lines only d9b5ac4's was pushed text (the other two, e3fe2ca and 3947c44, restated unpushed entries); so 490 of 518 (94.6%) were unpushed work restated in place. That is VFG's MEASUREMENT from a local reflog, which this parcel did not reproduce and which `figure_extracts.py --verify` could not. Fixed: the position counts stay (518, 515 and 3, which VFG recomputed and found equal), the two interpretive clauses are gone from the gallery, the SVG's text and this entry, and the figure says the counts are positions in the file and that whether a line had been pushed is not in the history.
- **(b4) this entry said "the one conflict is docs/README.md's counts" at a merge.** There are two: docs/README.md's counts and the tail of docs/VALIDATION.md (keep both entries, main's first). Fixed in Known limits below.
- **Small, asked for and done:** math-cost's last legend row was drawn over its source line, math-marks' source line (about 220 characters on a 900 px canvas) was clipped, and stress-telemetry's last note line touched its footer: footers now wrap and the three canvases are sized to their content; a layout rule in the SVG lint (a text the canvas clips, a mark drawn over the footer) now fails by name, and when run over the committed SVGs it also flagged three that were not on VFG's list (history-size, stress-timeline, verify-growth: texts that a renderer with a wider font than Windows' would clip), fixed too. Two control gaps VFG found by breaking the check (the lint's call site in check_tree, and the tolerance branch of a claim) each have a plant now. The runner's remedy line for this generator says `--write`. "79 numbers" was 59 numbers and 20 phrase, presence or consistency checks: it is 83 statements, 58 numbers and 25 of the others, and says so. history-size's caption now names the areas in the order of their lines (it left out programs and certificates, more than the golden model); and the clause5.c claim named "(rint and scaleb)" for two cft_run sites of which one, :159, is the shared step() helper that cft_rint and cft_cmp_sig call, and the other, :441, is cft_scaleb's multiply chain: the claim now names the functions and the callers.
- **(b1') hw-clock still claimed a completeness it could not have (the re-check).** After (b1) the figure and its caption said that the builds drawn were every U50 build the ledger states a kernel slack for, and the check's scan, which matched by entry (an entry that pairs "kernel" with a slack needed some build drawn or listed from it), held that. VFG read the ledger statement by statement and found builds stated in running text, in entries the scan counted as covered: the 130 MHz control single of 31 Aug (line 50, +0.450); a revision-7 probe single (line 15943, +0.065); the first clock sweep's builds, left on the box (line 13836: 115 MHz +0.409, 145 MHz +0.084, 175 MHz -0.562); build-seq135s (line 11104, -0.286); a sibling repository's f128x6 design built on the same box (lines 13876 to 13878); the single's +0.045 in two other places (lines 1034 and 18895); and, BELIEVED by VFG, the diet quad's -0.113 (line 13865) (READ in VFG's report; I re-read each line and agree). Fixed: the first is drawn, a 44th build; the rest are listed in the extract with a reason each, the nine that no pattern reads marked as found by hand; and the figure no longer says "every": its subtitle, its panel title, its bottom text and its caption say what is drawn and what is not, name the builds that exist only in running text, and say that the page does not claim there are no others. The scan is by statement now: each of the 67 statements the two patterns find in the pinned prefix (50 of kernel slack, 17 of negative WNS) must carry the number of a build drawn from its entry or of an item listed from it, matched by number within its entry, so that a second number in a drawn entry is not covered by the first (39 are a drawn build's, 28 are listed); the extract records its rules and its rows, and `--check` compares both with a fresh scan. "The timing record", below, says what that proves and what it does not.
- **(b2') the timing figure's clause that five legs "show one pass fewer" on the cut visit was false for selftest.** Selftest is skipped by design on most visits (its cell is 15 passes and 29 skips, 44 in all), so on the cut 45th visit it was one visit fewer, not one pass fewer; the other four read 44 against 45 in passes as well. Fixed: the clause says the five were reached, run or skipped by design, on 44 of the 45 visits, and gives selftest's split; it is computed from the cycles.
- **The re-check's small notes, done:** the extract's recorded rule strings are compared with the script's constants (a plant edits the record and makes the extract's own digest agree); the layout lint has a text-on-text rule (two texts whose estimated boxes overlap by more than 2 px across and 3 px down; a box is the full em, so lines 9 or 10 px apart touch by a pixel without their ink), with a sample that must trip it, a sample for the footer's text rule (a label written over the source line) and a sample that must not trip it (lines 9 px apart, labels touching end to end); and hw-area and stress-sweep, which VFG found overlapping labels in a wide font (Verdana), no longer do: hw-area's two column heads sit a row higher, the first reading "share" where it read "of the part", and stress-sweep's left panel title is shorter. The new rule, run over the committed SVGs, found one more by the same estimate, fixed too: stress-timeline's KPI row (the label "failed, timed out or lost" ran into the next, so the row is now spaced by the width of what it holds). A scratch run with every width 10% over the estimate found a near miss the gate does not see, perf-speedup's bold row label "fused multiply-add" within 2 px of the first cell's value, and the grid starts 40 px further right (a margin, not a defect). MEASURED with real text boxes, not the estimate (getBBox in the desktop's browser, with Verdana set for the sans stack and Courier New for the mono one): the previous version's SVGs overlapped in hw-area ("85% routing limit" over "of the part", 7.2 x 9.5 px) and in stress-sweep (23.8 x 11.5 px) and nowhere else; the new ones overlap nowhere in Verdana, Tahoma, Arial, Segoe UI, Trebuchet MS, Georgia or Calibri. That is one pair in each where VFG saw two; the estimate finds two in the old hw-area (its two column heads also touch) and one in stress-sweep.

**What was built,** on branch `figures`, cut from main at 0b77387 (marks: READ a file, COMPUTED arithmetic on what was read, MEASURED a run of mine, BELIEVED mine and unverified):

**The timing record: what is drawn, what is listed, and what the check can say** (READ the ledger prefix, COMPUTED the scan; this replaces a section headed "every", which claimed more):
- **Drawn:** 44 U50 builds whose kernel slack the ledger states in a form the extract's patterns read, each slack a capture group of a pattern that names its entry: 39 closed and 5 missed (the 260 MHz long shot, the 145 and 150 MHz brackets, round 2's first quad at 135 MHz, the sweep's 175 MHz build with the standard recipe). The quad closed 135 MHz 10 times (+0.003 to +0.143) and missed it once with a kernel slack stated (-0.363); one tile closed 175 MHz (+0.001, with the second recipe). The 130 MHz control single of 31 Aug (+0.450) is the build the re-check added.
- **Listed, not drawn,** 42 other figures of slack, each in the extract with its reason and counted in the caption, 33 found by the scan's patterns and 9 by a reader: 8 repeats of a drawn build's number (round 2's single stated a day before its table, the sweep's six per-point entries, rev8a's part one); 3 mentions of one; 6 other numbers of drawn builds (round 2's quad on the system clock, two routed WNS before post-route phys_opt, revision 8's whole-design WNS and the first negative steps of its routes); 3 misses at 135 MHz for which the ledger states only the whole design's slack, with the worst paths in the kernel (a single tile on 1 Sep, -0.577; two quads on 2 Sep, -0.141 retimed and -0.113 not, no xclbin); 9 out-of-context probes (probes S and K, the RETIMING toys); 5 figures of other designs and parts (7-series, the Kintex-7 325T flows, a sibling repository's f128x6); and 8 builds named only in running text (the revision-7 probe single, +0.065; the first clock sweep's three, +0.409, +0.084 and -0.562; build-seq135s, -0.286; the single's +0.045, twice; the diet quad, -0.113).
- **The scan:** over the pinned prefix the two patterns (in the extract and the sidecar) find 67 statements, 50 of a kernel slack and 17 of a negative WNS; each is carried by a build drawn from its entry or by an item listed from it (39 and 28), by its number within its entry, and a repeat's number must equal the attempt it repeats.
- **What that proves, and not more:** that every statement in the two forms the patterns read is drawn or listed, today and on every run, so a new one in an edited entry fails by name. It does not prove that no build is stated in other words: the re-check found nine, which the patterns do not read and which are listed by hand. So the figure, its caption and this entry say what is drawn and what is listed, and do not say that there are no others.

**The sweep's tile items and host items** (the lead's fact, checked in the code before anything was counted):
- host/src/clause5.c's header lists COMPOSED = cft_rint, cft_scaleb, cft_cmp_sig, whose floating-point work is cft_run() passes, and HOST = cft_convert, the integer conversions, cft_logb, cft_next_*, cft_class, cft_total_order*, cft_rem (READ). The file has two cft_run call sites: the shared step() helper at line 159, which cft_rint and cft_cmp_sig call, and cft_scaleb's multiply chain at line 441; line 1229 reads "remainder: host" (READ; the check names the two functions and step()'s callers). host/tools/divsqrt_soak.c's lib_call calls cft_div and cft_sqrt (READ).
- So the tile items are sqrt32 and rint32 (exhaustive, five attributes each) and div32, div64, sqrt64, rint64, scaleb32 and scaleb64 (random): 10 of the 14 exhaustive items and 25 of the 54 random. The host items are nextup32, nextdown32, logb32 and class32 (exhaustive) and 29 random ones over class64, logb64, nextup64, nextdown64, conv32to64, conv64to32, cvtto32, cvtto64, cvtfrom32, cvtfrom64, rem32 and rem64 (COMPUTED from hw/card_stress_lib.py's item list).
- Of the run's 1,356,316,228,303 sweep cases, 414,541,012,992 (30.6%) are tile items' (42,949,672,960 exhaustive and 371,591,340,032 random) and 941,775,215,311 (69.4%) host items'. All 14 exhaustive items covered their 2^32 encodings, the last by hour 9.9: 10 x 2^32 through the tile and 4 x 2^32 in host code; 0 cases disagreed (COMPUTED from the final metrics.jsonl; each total also agrees with the run's own report.txt, with hw/card_stress_report.py's summary and with VFG's own recount).
- No figure or caption calls the sum "on the card". `--check` reads clause5.c and divsqrt_soak.c on every run and fails by name if the header stops saying it, if a swept host operation is not in the HOST list, or if the file gains a third cft_run site.
- The telemetry is consistent with the split and was not asked to prove it: on the quad image the median power was 22.1 W between legs, 22.1 W during sweep slices of host items only and 22.5 W with tile items running (a 0.3 W difference; that it is the tile's work is BELIEVED, nothing here isolates it); the image sets the board's power (22.2 W on the quad, 15.7 W on the single, 16.1 W on the deep, medians of 673, 94 and 98 samples by whole-second spans; VFG's exact-epoch spans give 671, 94 and 99 and the same rounded medians), and the one sample near the README's 35 W, 34.4 W, fell in cft-resident's leg of about 4 s (COMPUTED from the run's samples).

**How the figures stay accurate,** and how the check was made to fail:
1. `--check` regenerates every SVG, sidecar and the gallery in memory and compares byte for byte with the committed files. It fails by name on a difference ("STALE figure NAME: FILE differs from a fresh generation", which the runner's STALE pattern recognises), a missing output, an output no figure makes, an extract whose data no longer matches its own digest, an extract whose recorded source digest no longer matches a source that is present, an extract no figure reads, a number or sentence the README or another document states that a figure disagrees with (or a sentence that has stopped being there), a personal path in anything written, an SVG outside the small element and attribute set GitHub's sanitiser keeps, a text its canvas clips, a text drawn over another text and a mark or a text drawn over its own source line (by the kit's conservative estimate of text widths, 0.58 em).
2. It reads no git history, network, card or other machine, and proves it: the whole check runs under a tripwire that raises if a process is started or a connection opened. CI's checkout is shallow.
3. It scans the ledger prefix statement by statement (above) and repeats the scan on every run: a statement of the two forms that is neither a drawn build's nor a listed item's fails by name, the rules the extract records must be the script's, and its record of the statements must equal a fresh scan of the prefix.
4. It plants 32 faults in a scratch copy and requires each to be named: the brief's four (an SVG changed by one byte; an extract's data changed; a sidecar changed; an extract's recorded source digest no longer matching the source, which is present - done twice, by editing the source and by editing the digest with the extract's own digest made to agree), a deleted output, a stray one, the gallery edited, an extract no figure reads, a build the ledger states a slack for which the extract no longer draws or lists, a second build's slack stated inside an entry that is drawn (the ledger prefix edited and the extract's digest of it made to agree, so that only a scan by statement can notice), the scan rules the extract records no longer the script's, the extract's record of the statements edited, a left-out entry whose number no longer equals the attempt it repeats, a bench file edited by one digit, a stated number changed, a stated sentence removed, a number the record quotes from another run moved beyond its tolerance, a stage added to the runner's list, a drawer that emits a style element with its committed files remade to match (so that only the lint can notice), a personal path an extract would feed to a sidecar, nine bad SVGs (a script, a style attribute, a CSS variable, an external font, an image, a text running off its canvas, a legend swatch over the footer, a label written over the footer, one label written over another), and the two the tripwire exists for (a call to git, a connection). It also makes three controls that must change nothing: a comment added to verify/run.sh, which the stage figure reads only in part (its stage names and its two budget lists, digested as that, not as the file), so a check that failed on it would fail for nothing on every round; a catalog item the stress run never served, which the stress reduction must leave out; and lines set 9 px apart with labels that touch end to end, which the layout lint must not flag.
5. 83 statements the README and other documents make are held to the figures' data by patterns that name the sentence, each at the document's own precision or, where the document quotes another run of the same thing, within a tolerance the sidecar states with the reason: 58 are numbers and 25 are phrase, presence or consistency checks (for example "written by an OpenAI model", "all found, with the same dates", a function named by a pattern, a sum that must add up). All 83 agree: 31 against README.md, 20 against docs/DETERMINISM.md's table, 6 against docs/studies/M2-trig.md, 4 against host/src/clause5.c, 3 against CLAUDE.md, 2 each against docs/BENCHMARKS.md, docs/CARDDAY.md and programs/workloads/README.md, 1 each against host/tools/divsqrt_soak.c, docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, docs/LAYOUTS.md and bindings/arduino/sync.py, and 9 internal to extracts and captured outputs (sums that must add up, the ledger scan, the cut visit).
6. A figure of the current state fails the moment what it reads moves; a figure of history is dated and lags until its extract is remade, and `--check` then prints a note instead of failing (verify-growth does this when the runner's counts have moved), so a stage added later does not turn CI red for a figure of the past.
7. Beyond the controls, fourteen runs of mutations of the check itself were made in scratch (a comparison, a check, the lint's call site, the lint's layout rules, the tolerance branch, the ledger scan or the tripwire broken in a copy of the script, one at a time): every one was noticed by the control meant to notice it, including the two VFG found unnoticed.

**What the figures found,** the data against the prose, reported and none silently picked:
- **The ledger's append-only rule.** The file's header says "An entry never edits history; a correction is a new entry naming the old one." Git says 518 of the 21,561 lines ever added to it were later deleted, by 82 commits (54 of whose subjects say restated, corrected, fixed or a verifier's finding: a count of those words, not a reading of each): 515 (99.4%) from the newest entry at the time and 3 from older entries (1 line 19 entries back, d9b5ac4, 2026-09-04; 1 line 1 entry back in each of e3fe2ca and 3947c44, 2026-10-06) (COMPUTED by position; VFG recomputed all of it by patch counting and found it equal). By push state VFG measured 28 of the 518 as pushed text (see above, not reproduced here). Reported on history-size and in the gallery; nothing here edits the ledger.
- **The README's 812 against 107 million elements a second** is docs/BENCHMARKS.md's cft-resident table of 2026-09-16 (1M, one tile: 812, 417, 212, 107), not the committed sweep, which gives 787.9 and 106.8 at the same million elements (3.0% and 0.2% apart: another run) (READ, COMPUTED). Held to 5% with the reason in the sidecar. Likewise the README's "3.76 against 1.74 million a second, one thread" is BENCHMARKS.md's fma table; the sweep's software fma gives 3.754 and 1.766 (READ, not held by a claim).
- **"Exactly eight times"** (README, one binary256 element against one binary32, on the beat): the arithmetic is exact at the top of the ladder - 8.02, 4.01 and 2.01 at each format's largest size - and not at a million elements, where one tile's binary32 is 7.4 times its binary256 in the sweep and 7.6 in BENCHMARKS.md's table (the README's own "about seven and a half times" is the table's) (COMPUTED).
- **The README's "about 35 watts"** is four tiles streaming: the stress run sampled that once (34.4 W) in cft-resident's leg; its sweeps' tile work drew 22.5 W on the quad (MEASURED by the run, COMPUTED here). The README's table and the run agree; the figure says what the 35 W is.
- **The test counts.** docs/VERIFICATION.md counts pytest's 5,222 golden tests; python/tests defines 1,027 test functions at 0b77387 (READ, COMPUTED). Different quantities (parametrisation); verify-growth says "functions defined".
