**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge).
- **L2 is PLAUSIBLE.** It excludes a defect keyed by a combination of dropped bits beyond the walking set, and a pattern-dependent timing fault; it says nothing of values between the classes' representatives (the value level, L1).
- **Nothing here has touched the card or the box.** The XRT=1 build, a card run of rint64-class and scaleb64-class, and the real times of the lane-exact calls on a tile (BELIEVED above) are the lead's.
- **The lane count (4) is read from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the lane an element takes from the staging order (BELIEVED);** a build with another count takes `-DCLS_LANES`. A defect that needs a particular (lane, attribute, pattern) triple is covered only for the attributes run.
- **The exponent witnesses are this parcel's extension of the study's 281**, and a repeated cell is counted, not removed (the distinct counts); `cvtfrom64-class` has the lowest distinct share (11,557 of 50,923: every position below 54 bits is exact, so its four classes repeat).
- **scaleb64's subnormal operands use one leading-bit position** (route 2) and the three routes are three of many (operand exponent, n) pairs a strip has; the assumption is that the exponent enters only through a rebias and range checks. In-range results are exact and are not enumerated. cvtfrom64-class covers the i64 and u64 sources; the i32 and u32 sources are `cvtfrom64-all`'s.
- **The oracle for a scaleB exponent past int's range is asked at the clamped exponent** (INT32_MAX or INT32_MIN), the library at the true int64: the same correctly rounded value, argued in the source; a first run without the clamp found 12 mismatches, all in the driver (cast to int gave -1 and 0).
- **The dropped-class plant's "wrong selector" form is hidden at scaleb e4m3's half class** (reached a second way), so the test runs it on four other instances; the "no case of the class" form fails every instance.
- **Values are compared per lane and flags per call; a class case is a call of its own, so its flags are its own** - the batched knob build and the random modes keep the OR, and a flag one operand drops among others that raise it goes unseen there (measured above).
- **The size**: the Python reference is 841 lines and the C section 467 with its comments (the file grew by 554 with the header, usage and the conversion kernel), over the brief's few hundred and 150 to 350; the coverage check, the stand-in and the independent skip count are in the Python file.
- **docs/README.md and docs/VALIDATION.md will conflict with main at the merge** (the counts are recounted against 881bbcb): `python python/check_docs_index.py` states the right numbers after the merge.

**Records.** docs/README.md recounted (82,888 lines in all, 2,674 of operations, 45,220 of record; CARDDAY 1,530, VALIDATION 21,888). `python python/check_docs_index.py`: rc 0 (47 documents, 50 links, every count true; 69 tracked documents, 128 relative links, 1,342 quoted paths exist; 47 negative controls each caught by name). `git diff --check` clean; no personal path in any added line.

## 2026-10-20 - the divsqrt soak's hard-case modes (parcel HC, Sonnet): `div32-hard`, `div64-hard` and `sqrt64-hard`, over a deterministic index space of constructed operands that `python/hardcases.py` reproduces and verifies in exact integers; the closest-approach, exact-quotient, strip-tie and sqrt(1 + k ulp) cases a sampler cannot reach at fp64; thirteen proposed stress-driver items; and the outside generators, listed and not downloaded; **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**Why.** Logan, 2026-10-20, on the sweep study's questions: "The more independent generators the better" (Q3, hard cases); "Class level and hard case to begin, others are long term goals" (Q7; the class level is parcel CL's, beside this one); the oracle stays the host FPU and libm ("Yes", Q8: the golden model and the software backend are for re-checks and arbitration); coverage counted "Per tree" with the three images reported separately (Q4) (READ, the brief). The study (docs/studies/SWP-A-coverage.md, section 4.2, rank 4 of its plan) built the closest-approach cases of division in a prototype (docs/studies/swp-a/hardcase_div.py) and found that a stress-run item of 1.45 x 10^10 draws expects 2.2 x 10^-6 of them at fp64; this parcel turns the prototype into an index space the soak tool runs. Marks: PROVED (an exact-integer check run over the cases named), MEASURED (a run of this parcel's, with its command), READ (a file or page, named), COMPUTED (arithmetic on those), BELIEVED (this parcel's, unverified).

**What was built** (files; `wc -l` at the commit, MEASURED):
- `python/hardcases.py` (new, 583 lines): the reference generator. `space`, `dump`, `count`, `verify` and `stats` commands; the builders for nine families; `verify`, which decodes the operand bits and classifies each case with Fractions and `isqrt`: the classification's own arithmetic (decode, div_class, sqrt_class) shares none with the builders; its skipped-F0 check (independent_dividends) uses the builders' modular inverse; verify takes its operands from them and, for a skipped F0 index, its divisor from f0_divisor.
- `host/tools/divsqrt_soak.c` (484 before, 1,068 now; 590 lines added and 6 changed): the three modes, the sub-modes `hard-space`, `hard-dump` and `hard-count` (none opens a device), the builders ported from the generator, the exact checks of every F0 and S0 case as it is built, and a refusal by name where the compiler has no 128-bit integer. The random modes' code is unchanged, and the usage text gained its lines after the old ones.
- `hw/test_divsqrt_hard.py` (new, 764 lines) and `python/tests/test_hardcases.py` (new, 19 tests: the whole of python/tests collects 5,258 against the 5,239 docs/VERIFICATION.md states for the golden stage, so +19).
- docs/CARDDAY.md (1,400, 1,532): the section "The hard-case division and square-root items"; docs/README.md recounted; this entry.
- Not changed: hw/card_stress_lib.py and hw/card_stress.py (the driver parcels'; their items are below), hw/run-soak.sh, host/tools/clause5_soak.c (parcel CL's), `python/cft_golden`, any runner stage.

**The modes** (what the doc section tells a reader to run; the families are in `python/hardcases.py`'s docstring). Each takes `<lo> <hi> <attribute>` over an index space, calls `run_batch` as the random modes do, and prints the exhaustive modes' line, `..., E encodings, S skipped`, with E counting indices and cases + S = k x E, k = 4, 4 and 1 (the four sign combinations of one operand pair; one operand). A skip is an index whose construction yields no operand pair, all k slots with it. Spaces: div32-hard 21,235,788 indices, div64-hard 289,685,696, sqrt64-hard 4,456,448, in segments smallest first (F3a ties in the subnormal strip, F3b powers of two over the whole quotient-exponent range, F2 b = 1 +- k ulp with the repository's failing a = 1, b = 1 - ulp at j = 0, F1 exact quotients, F0 closest approach to a midpoint or a representable number over odd divisors from the bottom of the binade, the top and, at fp64, keyed; S1 sqrt(1 + k ulp) and kin, S0 the inputs nearest the squares of midpoints from the 2-adic roots of rho = 8m + 1). Attributes: rne, rtz, rdn, rup, and rmm for square root only (it rides the RNE oracle: an inexact root is never on a tie); rmm for division is refused by name, as in the random modes. Refused by name, exit 2: a range that is empty, reversed, past the space or not a number; an attribute that does not exist; rmm for division; a build with no 128-bit integer; and **a slice of 64 or more indices in which every index skipped**.

**Where this departs from the brief, and why.** (1) The brief says an all-skipped slice is "refused, as EX's all-skipped rule does". EX's rule is the opposite: a slice that compared nothing because every pair was skipped "is not" refused (the docstring of `parse_soak`; hw/test_c5_exhaustive.py checks that 4,096 quiet NaNs give 0 cases, 16,384 skipped and a pass; hw/test_card_stress.py line 422), and the cover rule alone accepts it. These modes refuse it, from 64 indices up (a run of skips that long is a broken construction here: a case is built for most indices everywhere), and the test also holds the tool's S to the generator's count, so a mode that skipped everything is caught both ways (plants below). A smaller slice, which can be all skip legitimately, is a pass. (2) The brief's "roughly 61%" of odd divisors with no dividend at a target and sign is the prototype's single window (mx >= my); these modes use the sampler's convention (the dividend doubled when it is below the divisor), reach both quotient binades and skip 30.7 per cent (1 - ln 2, COMPUTED; MEASURED 30.68 per cent (30.6849) of F0K's 1,073,741,824 slots). (3) The brief puts the C modes at about 150 to 300 lines, the generator at a few hundred and the tool test at a few hundred; the C file gained 590 lines (114 comment, 30 blank, 446 code), of which the modes proper - the nine builders, the batch driver, the range check and the dispatch - are about 290, the three sub-modes about 95 and the no-128-bit stubs about 45; the generator is 583 lines because it carries `verify`, and the test 764 because it carries eight groups and fifteen plants. (4) The existing random `sqrt64` mode refuses rmm (only `sqrt32` accepts it, though the file's header says the tool checks RMM square root against the RNE oracle); `sqrt64-hard` accepts it, as the brief says, and the random mode is untouched.

**What is PROVED** (exact integers, by program, for the cases named; not a claim about the tile). `python hardcases.py verify` over **every index** of div32-hard (21,235,788; 305 s) and of sqrt64-hard (4,456,448; 367 s), and over a sample of div64-hard (the two small segments whole and 150,000 indices of each of the five large ones, 766,576 indices): 0 failures. Each case is held to its family's claim by a classification written from the definitions (the decoded bits, Fractions, `isqrt`): F0 - |N| = 1 exactly, the designed sign, the divisor the reduced denominator, and every skip genuine by a second construction (the two-binade congruences); S0 - the nearest input is rho 2^-2p from the square of a midpoint (D = -rho), and every skip genuine by a bit-by-bit search over all residues; S1 - |D| = k^2; F1 - the quotient is exactly representable, the odd parts below 2^((p-1)/2), subnormal in variant 3 only; F2 - the operands are exactly 1.0 or 2 - ulp over 1 + k ulp or 1 - k ulp; F3a - the quotient is a half-integer of the subnormal grid, s places below the smallest normal (so an exact tie, RNE and RMM differing where the kept bit is even); F3b - one operand a power of two, the other all ones or 1.5, the operand exponents differing by the designed quotient exponent, the quotient's binade exact. F2 and F3b are structural: their distance to a boundary is computed and not claimed small. The tool re-checks every F0 case (|N| = 1 and its sign) and every S0 case (u^2 = rho mod 2^s) in 128-bit integers as it builds it, so the whole-space `hard-count` runs below are also exact checks of every F0 construction of the three spaces (fp64: 186,066,361 + 8,388,607 + 4,194,304 built indices of F0K, F0A and F0D; fp32: 6,801,339 + 4,826,737) and of all 1,483,608 S0 cases. The Python and the C builders agree on the whole of div32-hard and sqrt64-hard (the built and skipped counts of every segment equal the tool's whole-space counts) and on 53,104 operand lines of the three modes over 132 ranges (the agree group).

F0D at fp64 skips exactly half, F0A at fp64 4 slots of 33.5 million.

- **The plants**, each in a copy, red at the check written for it, a CONTROL passing the same slice first: generator, six (F0's dividend two too high; F0's doubled quotient never built, a real construction reported as a skip; F2's divisor one ulp off; F3a's quotient shifted one place; F3b's dividend exponent one too high; S0's nearest input off by one: `verify` exits 1 naming `F0 closest approach`, `F0 skip is genuine`, `F2 divisor`, `F3a tie in the subnormal strip`, `F3b the operand exponents differ`, `S0 odd-square input`); the brief's three on the tool - (1) a construction off by one is refused by the tool's own exact check by name (exit 2, no verdict), and with that check blinded it runs and PASSES the soak (a case that is not hard still tests the library) and only the agreement with the generator's dump sees it; (2) a slice one encoding short fails `encodings for a slice of`, skipped slots one short an index fail `cases + skipped is not 4 x E`; (3) a mode that skips every index: a 4,096-index slice is refused by name (exit 2, no verdict), an 8-index slice prints 0 cases and 32 skipped and is caught by the independent count, and with the refusal removed the 4,096-index slice prints 0 cases, 16,384 skipped, no mismatch, exit 0 - everything `parse_soak` can check passes - and is caught only by the independent count; and (4) the prototype's division that computes 40 extra bits and rounds ties-to-even on them fails on 25,063 of 100,000 closest-approach-to-a-midpoint pairs of div64-hard's F0K (25.1 per cent) and on 0 of 100,000 of the soak's own random draws (`docs/studies/swp-a/seed_audit.py`'s port of the sampler, held there to the real tool); with 80 extra bits it is correct on all of 20,000 constructed pairs. Two more: (5) **a library defect found through the tool**, which the Python plant of (4) is only a model of: a copy of host/src/divsqrt.c whose `div_chunk` takes the guard test's discriminant for zero (an exact tie) when it is below 2^-(p-1) of the remainder, built; on the F0K slice [21,250,240, 21,950,240) (700,000 indices, about 1.9 million cases) under rne the real library passes and the planted one FAILS with 485,236 value mismatches (exit 1, operands named); under rtz the planted one passes (the defect is in the tie only); and the soak's random mode on the planted library, `div64 2000000 1 rne`, passes (2,000,000 cases, 0 and 0); (6) a build with no 128-bit integer refuses the modes and sub-modes by name and still runs the random ones. Every `parse_soak` claim above is the driver's own: the test imports hw/card_stress_lib.py and holds each slice's line to its cover rule (the 173 special slices are accepted; the encoding-short and skip-short plants are refused by name; the skip-everything plant with its refusal removed is ACCEPTED, as an all-NaN slice of cvtto32-all is).
- **The golden model and an exact arbiter** (`python/tests/test_hardcases.py`, written here from the definitions, sharing no code with softfloat.py or the builders): on a sample of every family of both formats, all four sign slots and all five attributes, bits and flags (inexact, underflow by tininess after rounding, the overflow landings), the golden model equals the arbiter in all 36,980 (div32-hard) and 9,900 (div64-hard) comparisons and in the square root's; and CPython's own float division and `math.sqrt` (the host FPU) equal its round-to-nearest answers. The arbiter goes red at once on two planted mutations of itself (a scratch run; the script is not in the repository).
- **The parts the prototype only argued, by exhaustion at small precision** (`python/tests/test_hardcases.py`, 19 tests in 2.5 s): F0 at p = 9 and 10, over every odd divisor (the A and D streams together are all of them) and every dividend: the Fractions classification lists the dividends at |N| = 1 from a midpoint and from a representable number, above and below; the builder returns exactly that dividend when it exists (never more than one per target and sign) and a skip exactly when there is none, 0 differences; S0 at p = 10, 12 and 14, over every input of [1, 4): the distances |D| from the squares of midpoints are all congruent to 1 mod 8 up to sign, the least are 1, 7, 9, 15, 17, 23 (the study's fp32 list), the inputs at |D| = 1 are exactly two, sqrt(1 + ulp) and the predecessor of 4, and for rho = 1, -7, 9, ... up to the 64th the set the builder lists equals the set of inputs at D = -rho. F2's index 1 (j = 0, v = 1) is exactly a = 1.0, b = 1 - ulp at both formats, with |N| = 1 from a midpoint (H4, the prototype's check label in docs/studies/swp-a/hardcase_div.py).

So libcft's software backend and the host's division and square root agree on every constructed case run - 127,758,344 of them in these runs - the overflow strip, the whole subnormal strip, the underflow-to-zero region, the exact ties and the exact quotients among them, flags included.
- **Sanitizers**: the tool built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=undefined` (the library the plain one), niced: `hard-count` over sqrt64-hard and div32-hard whole, div64-hard's first 22,298,816 indices and two stretches of a million, the soak over slices of every segment under every attribute of each mode (100,000 indices of div32-hard's F0A, F0D and div64-hard's F0A, F0K under rne, rtz, rdn and rup; 300,000 of sqrt64-hard under all five), `hard-space`, `hard-dump` and the two refusals: 33 invocations, no `runtime error`, no AddressSanitizer report, the two refusals exit 2.

**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge). Nothing here has touched the card or the box: the XRT=1 build of the modes, a card run and the real rates on a tile are the lead's. Flags are compared per batch, as in every mode here (a flag dropped on one lane among others that raise it is not seen; F1's batches are all exact, so a spurious inexact there is). Operands are positive normal magnitudes in four sign combinations; zeros, infinities, NaNs and subnormal operands stay with the random bands. F0 is built at one exponent pair and F1 and F3 at others with their own significands: the product of structure and exponent is not swept (the scale lemma of the study, argued at p = 24 and 53), and a closest approach to a midpoint of the subnormal grid that is not a tie is not built. The fp64 keyed stream is 2^26 of 2^51 odd divisors, and its divisors can repeat (their low 40 bits come from a hash): 2 values repeat among the 67,108,864 (MEASURED by the lead, a numpy port of `f0_divisor` checked against it on 20,003 indices), each repeat a wasted index, not a wrong answer. BELIEVED at fp64, MEASURED by exhaustion at small precision (the bullet above): that S0 lists every input at a given distance (the roots of u^2 = rho mod 2^s are four, which the builder takes whole), that F0 builds every dividend at |N| = 1 and only those, and that sqrt(1 + ulp) and the predecessor of 4 are the only inputs at distance 1 (the congruence u^2 = 1 mod 2^s has the four roots +-1 and +-1 + 2^(s-1), which leaves u = 2^p + 1 and 2^(p+1) - 1 in range); the step from p = 10 to 14 to p = 53 is that lemma about squares modulo a power of two, ARGUED here and not machine-checked. The rates and times above are the stress run's, not these operands'. The software backend's rate is 0.20 to 0.25 M cases a second, so the whole div64-hard item would take 54 to 68 minutes a process (COMPUTED from its slices); its slices are the evidence, not a whole run.

## 2026-10-20 - signed sweep records (parcel SG, Sonnet 5.5): `hw/sweep_record.py` makes the stress driver's finished sweep slices into canonical records, signs them with a key in `python/cft_sign.py`'s format and verifies them; `docs/SWEEP-RECORDS.md`; **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box, and no real key was made, read or used**

**What Logan said,** on 2026-10-20, answering the sweep study's question 6 (who contributes), verbatim: "At the moment only my device, though built to support a signing key would be good". Then, of the math round: "Math round may be slightly delayed to handle 6 and 9, as well as the task chips"; the lead confirmed that "6" there is question 6, which is this parcel. Marks as everywhere here: MEASURED (a run of this parcel's, named), READ (a file, named), COMPUTED (arithmetic on those), BELIEVED (mine, unverified).

**What was built.** Three new files and two recounted ones. `hw/card_stress.py`, `hw/card_stress_lib.py`, `python/cft_sign.py` and `python/cft_golden/ed25519.py` are unchanged and were only read or imported.
- `hw/sweep_record.py` (735 lines), in hw/ because it consumes the driver's records and its item table and counting rules (`card_stress_lib.sweep_items`, `read_records`, the rules of `parse_soak`) and DR2 will import it from the driver's own directory; it reaches into python/ for the shared Ed25519 and key format. `export RUN --out FILE (--key KEY | --device-key HEX)`, `sign FILE --key KEY --out FILE2`, `verify FILE... [--keyring RING] [--allow-unsigned]`, and for the driver `Exporter(Signer(load_seed(KEY)))` with `.run_start`, `.build` and `.leg`. Twenty refusals, each by name.
- `hw/test_sweep_record.py` (941 lines), run by hand: `python hw/test_sweep_record.py [--metrics RUN_OR_FILE]`.
- `docs/SWEEP-RECORDS.md` (426 lines): the record field by field, the keys, the commands, the refusals, a finding told from coverage, what a signature proves and does not, what the driver calls and what it costs.
- `docs/README.md` recounted (forty-eight files; the new row under "The tools") and `docs/VERIFICATION.md`'s "indexes the forty-seven documents" made forty-eight, which the checker reads.

**The record, version 1** (READ in `hw/card_stress.py` `finish_leg` and the `run_start` record; the document has the table). A slice (an exhaustive item's `[lo, hi)`), a stream (a random item's `seed` and `count`, which the study's 5.8 keeps apart from enumerations) and a campaign. Canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, ASCII, integers only and none above 2^53 - 1); `id` the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes without `id` and `sig`, stored in the record so that a changed byte is seen without a key; the signature Ed25519 over `cft-sweep-record 1`, a NUL and the 32-byte id. Carried: `cid`, the interval or the seed and count, `cases`, `vm`, `fm`, `skipped` (only where the tool's verdict line has the clause), `subject` (image name and SHA-256, the image's tiles, the tile where recorded), `tool` (the driver's commit and whether tracked files differed), `run` (id, device pseudonym, the epochs in ms, the rate rounded, the log's relative path), `disagreements` on a finding. **Absent, because the run does not record them:** `digest`, `control`, the oracle's libm, CPU and probes, `stratum`, `enumeration`, `subject.rtl`, `subject.abi`, the soak tools' build id, compiler and flags. **The run does not record an RTL tree hash**; what it would take is in the document (the driver reading each image's manifest, which `hw/rebuild-2022.sh` writes with a `commit:` line, and `git rev-parse <commit>:rtl` on a full clone; or a table in the repository), and none was computed here. The campaign carries the operation, the attribute (absent for a job without one), `sweep`, the tool, the argument form, the oracle's kind, `reach`, and for an exhaustive item `space`, `exact`, `extra_cases` and `per_encoding`; its SHA-256 is the cid. The device pseudonym is 16 hex of SHA-256(`cft-sweep-device 1`, NUL, the key): made from the key, so that nothing is stored and the verifier can recompute it, which also makes it name a key and not a machine.

**What ran** (the desktop, niced, one heavy process at a time; the copy of the 2026-10-19 run's `metrics.jsonl` the lead made, 751 records, SHA-256 cd0aec75c8fa...):
- **The real run, exported.** 378 finished sweep slices, all `pass`, 22 campaigns, 0 findings: 364 slices on the quad (91 on each tile), 7 on the single and 7 on the deep (MEASURED, a separate script). Their cases sum to 978,480,791,566 (902,016,532,494 + 37,934,333,952 + 38,529,925,120), the sum of the raw legs' `counts.cases` computed apart from the exporter (MEASURED). The test reads every record back against its raw leg, field by field, with code that does not share the exporter's. The other 373 records of the file (165 battery legs, 176 telemetry, 14 cycle_start, 14 cycle_end, build, event, run_end, and the one run_start is used) are of kinds the exporter ignores or reads for the run's facts, without error (MEASURED).
- **Commands and costs** (desktop, MEASURED, the lead's copy, as commands with their 0.4 s of start-up): `export --device-key` 0.46 s; `export --key` 1.5 to 1.7 s; `verify --keyring` 1.6 to 2.0 s. Per call, for DR2: `Exporter.leg` 3.0 ms median signed (3.2 mean, 5.3 worst, 756 calls over two passes; 2.5 ms a record in WSL), 0.06 ms unsigned; `Signer(seed)` once, 1.5 ms; `verify` 3.3 ms a slice; a signed slice line is 853 bytes on average (837 to 860), 619 unsigned, a campaign line 299, the signature 234, so a 60-hour run's 3,287 slices would be about 2.8 MB (COMPUTED). The timings move with the desktop's load (signing took 2.5 to 3.8 ms a record in the runs below).
- **The test.** Windows Python 3.12: 239 checks, 0 failed, 5 skipped by name, 24 s with the real copy, and 196 checks, 2 skipped, 10 s without (forms 50, rules 6, export 73, keys 18, domain 10, plants 38, real 43, and the check that every refusal was seen firing); Python 3.13.14 the same 239 in 23 s. WSL cft2204, Python 3.10.12: 240 checks, 0 failed, 4 skipped, 22 s; there the POSIX check of a key file others may read ran and drew `key-file`. The 5 skips: that POSIX check on Windows, and four plants the real run has no record for (nextup32, sqrt32, rem64, a random campaign; the synthetic run has them).
- **The driver's rule, held to the driver.** The verifier's counting rule against `card_stress_lib.parse_soak` itself, on 1,233 (item, interval, cases, skipped) points of the catalog's 90 items: 0 disagreements. The rate rule accepts 20,000 driver-rounded runs (durations 10 ms to 4,000 s) and refuses 2,000 runs with a rate 2% too high. MEASURED.
- **Plants, each red by name** (on a synthetic run, and on 44 lines of real records, the first slice of each campaign): a count changed after signing, the id left (`id`); the interval moved and the id recomputed (`signature`); another key's valid signature (`key` with a keyring that names only the first, `device` without one or with one naming both); another key's name on the first key's signature (`signature`); a validly signed slice of another run, with and without its campaign (`splice`), and of a run of the same name on another device (`splice`); the domain string swapped to the certificate's, a certificate-domain signature over the record's own id (`signature-domain`); a key file inside a working tree (a `.git` directory above it, a `.git` file, and this repository's own path: `key-in-tree`, exit 64, nothing written); and `version`, `canonical` (spaces, order, CRLF, non-ASCII, no final LF), `form`, `signature` (missing), `signer`, `counts` (seven kinds, each validly signed afresh, so that a signature does not launder a count), `campaign`, `run`, `signed`, `device` at `sign`, `empty`, `usage`, `output` (exit 73), `key-file`, and `metrics` (twenty-five runs altered in one way each, a dry run and the three of VSG's (b)3 among them).
- **The two domains, on the committed certificate** `certificates/signed-fp64/signed-fp64.cert` and a throwaway key (the test's key A): the certificate's own signature, written as the `sig` of a record line with that record's own id, gives `signature` from `verify` (it signs the certificate's body hash, not that id); a signature made under the certificate's domain over the record's own id gives `signature-domain` in a file, and the same key's record-domain signature over that id verifies; the key's record-domain signature over the certificate's body hash, written into a signature file for the certificate, is refused `signature` by `cert2.check_signature_file`; and, as a function call only (`check_signature` given the certificate's body hash as the id, which no file can have since a record's id is the SHA-256 of its own bytes), the committed signature gives `signature-domain`, which shows the two domains separating the same 32 bytes under one key and no more. Each control (a certificate's signature as a certificate's, a record's as a record's) passes. Only the test's own throwaway key signs. MEASURED. *Restated 2026-10-20 after verifier VSG's (b)1: this bullet, bc962f4's commit message and the report said that the certificate's own signature "taken for a record's" is refused `signature-domain` and that both directions were shown; that is true of the function call alone, and a file gives `signature`.*
- **A finding is a record, never coverage:** a synthetic failing slice exports with its disagreement lines, verifies, is listed as `FINDING ... never coverage`, is not among the cases in clean records, and `verify` exits 3. A record dropped from a signed file is not seen (nothing in version 1 signs the set); the test runs that as a known limit.
- **Records an unknown type could break.** At the lead's word (DR1 adds an event `sweep_empty`): a synthetic event of that name, a record of an unknown type, telemetry, cycle_start, a leg of an unknown kind and run_end, put among the legs, give the same lines as without them; so do legs without the keys later parcels added (`reach`, `expected_cases`, `expected_encodings`, `jobs`). MEASURED.
- **The verifier, taken apart** (one-off, a scratch copy of the module, not committed): 29 single-line mutations (splice, device, keyring, domain diagnosis, id, canonical, version, signature-required, key-in-tree, the cover rule, expected_cases' extra cases, the space bound, the small-order key, the dry-run refusal, `sign` verifying first, the exporter's catalog and build checks, the domain tag, the rate rule and others), and every one turned the test red, 27 at a named check and 2 by a crash; a thirtieth, which changed only a message string, correctly changed nothing. The test itself also takes out `check_signature`, `counts_problem` and `run_problem` in turn and shows the plant for each get through. MEASURED.
- **Byte for byte across interpreters.** The signed export of the lead's copy by the test's key A (its seed the SHA-256 of a label in the test, so nobody's) is identical under Windows Python 3.12 and WSL Python 3.10.12 (`cmp`): 328,894 bytes, SHA-256 2b16ee144deb35927d07f65286d56e1e9a6ef99ce30589577fe19d5526cc07e1; the unsigned export for key A's device, 240,442 bytes, 2897183b9f30128296e68edc232237adf58f4bc67206b271a2cd45cc1dbe58b9 (key A's public key b93a34db38a13f7261a5ddcdec500ebc681f244a8cf11edf37b3e022d1b0c4b9). MEASURED, at this tree; Ed25519 here is deterministic.

**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge):
- **Over the brief's ceiling.** The module is 735 lines and the test 941 against "a few hundred" each; every piece asked for (three commands, the forms, twenty refusals, two kinds of slice, the key rules, a plant for each refusal) needed its lines, and I cut none. The document is 426.
- **A stream has not been run on a driver-written random leg.** The 2026-10-19 run is all exhaustive; the stream form is held to synthetic legs built from `plan_wave`'s and `finish_leg`'s own fields (READ). The driver's dry run (`--dry-run --quick`) would give real ones; I did not run it, because DR1 and DR2 beside me were very likely running theirs, and its guard counts another driver's stand-ins as card users.
- **The 2026-10-16 run was not to hand.** That its legs lack `reach`, `expected_cases` and `expected_encodings` (which later parcels added) is BELIEVED; an exporter that tolerates their absence is shown on legs with them taken out, and a key that is there must agree with the catalog. Export reads the item table of the tree it runs from and refuses a leg that table disagrees with, so a run is exported from the tree it ran at.
- **Nothing signs the set**, so a record dropped from a file is not seen; `splice` and `device` are the only protection of a file's membership, and a second run of the same name made by the same key is not told from the first. **Copying is not seen:** another key can re-sign the same content under its own device, a new record with a new id, which a fold counting owners would count; independence is the study's rank 10 (replay, quorum).
- **A signature carries no time and there is no key revocation**; a stolen key's records cannot be told from earlier ones. Ed25519 here is not constant-time (its module says so). On Windows a key file's mode is not checked, as in `cft_sign.py`; `python/cft_sign.py keygen` itself will write a key inside the repository when told to (the refusal is at `export --key` and `sign`, and it is any `.git` ancestor, so a home directory that is itself a repository would refuse too).
- **What a signed record cannot prove** is section 6.6's list: that the slice ran, on the card, on a given device; what the oracle was; that the tool is the commit's build; the RTL tree (not recorded). The honest statement of a coverage is "covered by K owners, each replayed", and version 1 has one, not replayed.
- **No runner stage runs the test.** One could, for the groups that need only Python and the repository (196 checks, 10 s); the stage counts are the lead's and none was added. Parcel DR2 wires the signing into the driver; the document gives its calls, its failure policy (log an event and go on, never stop a run) and the resume's repeated campaign lines.
- **Merging:** the README's file count and totals and VERIFICATION's "forty-eight documents" are recounted for this branch alone; another parcel's document makes each of them wrong again.

**Records.** `python python/check_docs_index.py`: rc 0, forty-eight documents, every count true, 47 negative controls planted and caught by name (MEASURED, 34 to 49 s on the shared desktop, at each of the three commits after bc962f4); `git diff --check` clean.

**Restated after verifier VSG on bc962f4** ((a) 0, (b) 3; the entry is unpushed, so it is restated in place, in the commits 1f4625b, 42caf81 and the one that carries this paragraph):
- **(b)1, wording.** This entry's bullet on the two domains, bc962f4's commit message and the report said that the certificate's own signature, taken for a record's, is refused `signature-domain`, and that both directions were shown. In a file it is `signature`; `signature-domain` is a certificate-domain signature over the record's own id; the first claim holds as a function call only, with the certificate's body hash given as the id, which no file can have. The bullet, the document ("The signature"), the test's header and its messages say so, and the test has both file-level cases (VSG's cases 11 and 12).
- **(b)2, the header** of `hw/sweep_record.py` now gives the exit codes of all three commands: 2 for a refusal, 64 for usage, key-file and key-in-tree, 73 for output.
- **(b)3, the contract.** A pass or fail sweep leg with null counts and a sweep-kind leg with no sweep block were dropped with exit 0; Infinity for `rate.value` or a time was an uncaught `OverflowError` (exit 1), where NaN was refused. All are now `metrics` refusals, `OverflowError` is caught beside `TypeError` and `ValueError` in `leg`, `run_start` and `_ms`, and an unfinished sweep leg is still counted by status. The new test, run against bc962f4's module, fails 14 checks, one for each of these (MEASURED), and passes on the new one; the export of the lead's copy is byte for byte what it was (signed 328,894 B, sha256 2b16ee144deb...; unsigned 240,442 B, 2897183b9f30...).
- **Taken with them:** the test says "cases in clean records" where it said "cases covered", and the document says the total is a sum, that overlapping slices count twice and that nothing refuses an overlap (a known limit; no refusal was added); the document's "does not prove" list has section 6.6's second clause (a contributor who runs the golden model in software and reports the card's identity) and says version 1 checks no maximum rate; the header names the imports it left out, and the `splice` refusal says "or another device".

**Conduct.** No real key was made, read or used: the keys are the test's, derived from labels or made by `cft_sign.py keygen` in a temporary directory, and one `keygen` into my scratch for the first run; no key store and no `~/.ssh` was opened. WSL cft2204 (this desktop's Linux layer) was used for the Python 3.10 runs, with one key copy in its own /tmp, removed by that exact path; the box and the card were not touched. Files made in my scratch directory were removed by their exact paths; no process was stopped. ## 2026-10-20 - the CRLF hazard in project_figures.py's `--check` and `--write`, closed (parcel FX): a text file of the tree is read and digested as git's blob holds it

**What Logan asked,** verbatim, on 2026-10-20: "Math round may be slightly delayed to handle 6 and 9, as well as the task chips once the stress test is finished". The chip is the follow-up of the side parcels' closing record (2026-10-19): "the CRLF hazard in project_figures.py's `--check`".

**The hazard, shown** (MEASURED; 881bbcb's own scripts, run on scratch trees of the 80 files the check reads; the LF tree passes, rc 0):
- **One source saved CRLF** (python/cft_golden/formats.py, as on 2026-10-19): `--check` rc 1, three STALE lines (formats-dark.svg, formats-light.svg, formats.json).
  - **The check's remedy records the CRLF digest:** `--write` on a copy gives formats.py as sha256 47ee0ad7934f... and 1,863 bytes, where the committed sidecar has 3a4d02f54aa9... and 1,798. Every LF checkout would then fail the check.
- **docs/VALIDATION.md saved CRLF** (the ledger extract reads a byte prefix of it): `--check` rc 1, "extract ledger: its recorded source digest no longer matches: the first 1891030 bytes of docs/VALIDATION.md hashes to d3267b0e4d2c..., the extract says 300660c895da...", and the closing line says STALE and "remake with --write", which does not apply.
  - `figure_extracts.py ledger` refuses, "the clock sweep's table has 0 rows ... (want 8)", because its patterns are LF-bound, and writes nothing.
  - So figure_extracts.py's exposure was a misleading refusal and a misleading line; project_figures.py's was a recorded CRLF digest.
- **Which file is likelier to bite** (BELIEVED): docs/VALIDATION.md, not formats.py. Agents write it on Windows all the time, and a CRLF save followed by `git add` leaves an LF blob, a CRLF file and a clean status.
- **No tracked text file is legitimately CRLF** (MEASURED, `git ls-files --eol` at 881bbcb): the 16 tree files that sidecars or extracts digest are all `i/lf w/lf`; of 1,781 tracked files none is `i/crlf`, `i/mixed` or `w/crlf`; the 398 that are `-text` are binary (320 by attribute, 78 by git's own sniff).

**The choice** is (a), read a text file as git's blob holds it, with a note naming each file so read:
- **Not (b), git's blob:** `--check` runs under a tripwire that forbids a process, because "reads no git" is its stated design and CI's checkout is shallow; and the controls' scratch copy is not a git tree.
- **Not (c) alone:** the check would go red for a condition git itself calls clean, and its only cure would be restoring files from the index. (a) removes the hazard where the file is read, so `--write` cannot record a CRLF digest; the note keeps it from being silent.
- **The rule,** `figure_extracts.lf_form`, the one definition:
  - a file with a NUL byte, or that is not UTF-8, is not text and is read as it is; so is a lone CR, since only a CRLF pair is a line ending;
  - any other file has each CRLF read as LF.
  - This is how a binary file is told from a text one without git. A legitimately CRLF text file cannot be told from a CRLF copy of an LF blob by its bytes; none exists today (above), and if one did, its digest would be of its LF form on every platform, so the sidecars would still agree across platforms, though not with `sha256sum`.

**What changed** (two files; the sidecars, SVGs, gallery and extracts are byte-identical, below):
- **python/figure_extracts.py:**
  - `lf_form`, `tree_bytes` and `crlf_note` are new, and `sha256_file`, whose one caller was `Src.extract`, is gone;
  - `source_problems` and `make_ledger` read through `tree_bytes`, so the recorded byte count of the ledger prefix means the same prefix on every checkout;
  - `source_problems` returns the note, and `make_ledger` prints it to stderr.
- **python/project_figures.py:**
  - `Src._read`, the one place a tree file is read, returns the LF form and remembers the file (`Src.crlf`); `Src.extract` digests through it;
  - `--check` and `--write` print one `note:` line per file read as LF;
  - a committed output (an SVG, a sidecar, the gallery) is still held to its bytes, because the check cannot tell a CRLF blob from a CRLF working copy without git. It is STALE with CRLF, and the line now says "only in its line endings (CRLF on disk, LF made; --write writes LF)";
  - the controls' scratch copy is the tree in its LF form, so a CRLF checkout runs the same controls, whose plants cut files at byte offsets.
- **Three new faults (32 to 35) and five new controls (3 to 8),** eight new checks in all:
  - a unit check of `lf_form` on six byte strings (CRLF, mixed, LF, a lone CR, a NUL, not UTF-8);
  - four copies saved CRLF that must give no problem and a note naming the file: a source a figure reads whole (the first one), verify/run.sh (read in part by two figures), docs/VALIDATION.md (the ledger's byte prefix) and an extract's own file;
  - three faults that must fail by name: a one-digit edit of a bench CSV saved CRLF (STALE), the same inside the ledger's prefix in a CRLF copy ("its recorded source digest no longer matches"), and a CRLF SVG (STALE, "only in its line endings").
- The packager, project_packager.py, is not changed (below).

**Evidence** (MEASURED, the desktop, niced; scratch trees and copies in a scratch directory):
- **The check:** `python -B python/project_figures.py --check` rc 0 in 14.0 s, against 12.6 s at 881bbcb: "35 faults planted, each caught by name, and 8 controls that must change nothing, which changed nothing".
- **Nothing committed changes on LF:**
  - `--write` in a scratch copy: 46 files (45 under docs/img/figures and docs/FIGURES.md), `cmp` identical to the committed ones;
  - `figure_extracts.py ledger` into a copy whose ledger.json had first been made different: it writes the committed docs/figures/ledger.json byte for byte (38,806 bytes), as 881bbcb's script does;
  - history, tree and stress are not rewritten by either command.
- **On CRLF:**
  - only formats.py CRLF: `--check` rc 0 with one note; `--write` on the copy that 881bbcb's `--write` had poisoned gives 46 files identical to the committed ones;
  - only docs/VALIDATION.md CRLF: `--check` rc 0 with one note; `figure_extracts.py ledger` writes the committed extract byte for byte, with the note on stderr (the same `bytes` and sha256 300660c895da... as committed);
  - every input CRLF (34 of the 80 files): `--check` rc 0 with a note a file; `--write` 46 identical;
  - every file CRLF, outputs too (80): `--check` rc 1, 46 STALE lines, each "only in its line endings"; `--write` 46 identical, no CR in the sidecars or the gallery.
- **`figure_extracts.py --verify`** with the lead's copy of the stress run (its SHA256SUMS checked: metrics.jsonl 7,982,931 bytes, e7989f88efde..., and report.txt, 4a426b57d752...): rc 0, five ok (history, tree, ledger, stress, and stress unchanged by the three decoy catalog items), 32 s.
- **The gate** (run A): `bash verify/run.sh --only docs,generated` under Git Bash, run 20261020-091305-881bbcb, 09:13:04 to 09:14:56 (112 s), on the two script changes before the records were written: docs 35 s ok, generated 72 s ok, "VERDICT: PASS, nothing skipped", 0 inner skips. The packager's `--check` inside `generated` names one plant "not run on this platform" on Windows (the backslash entry name), and the stage prints only "ok" for it, so the runner does not count it as an inner skip (verifier-VFX's note; the runner's, before this parcel). The runner used `python`, which it prefers on Windows: Python 3.12.9 (Miniconda), first on PATH. The same command on the final commit is in the parcel's report, not here: an entry cannot name its own commit.
- **The controls can fail:** five one-off breakages in a scratch copy of the scripts, none committed, each made the check fail by name.
  - `lf_form` returning its input: six controls fail (the unit check, four copies, the CRLF SVG's wording);
  - `lf_form` stripping every CR: the unit check fails (the lone CR);
  - `source_problems` skipping the digest when the file had CRLF: the in-prefix edit in a CRLF copy "failed to fail";
  - no note: the four copies "wanted a note";
  - the outputs' wording removed: the CRLF SVG "failed to fail".

**Known limits:**
- **project_packager.py, report only, not changed** (the lead's word).
  - MEASURED: its `check_sidecar`, called unchanged on the CRLF-formats tree, gives one refusal, `sidecar-mismatch`: "figure formats: docs/img/figures/formats.json records python/cft_golden/formats.py with digest 3a4d02f54aa9..., and the tree's file is 47ee0ad7934f...". It gives none on the LF tree.
  - It re-hashes each sidecar source from its raw bytes. On a CRLF checkout it is now the first thing to refuse, since `--check` passes. docs/EXPORT.md's `sidecar-mismatch` row ("or whose digest is not the tree's file") describes it.
  - READ, not run: an archive made from a CRLF checkout would hold CRLF bytes of any CRLF document or output.
  - READ by verifier-VFX, not run: `check_sidecar` (project_packager.py lines 333-339) also compares each extract file's raw bytes, so a CRLF docs/figures/*.json would be refused too.
  - The fix is the same helper in `check_sidecar`, about four lines, and the lead's to order.
- **Outputs are held to their bytes** (above): a CRLF output is STALE, by design.
- **`figure_extracts.py ledger --verify` on a CRLF-saved extract** prints "ok ... remakes byte for byte" with no note, while `--check` names the file (MEASURED by verifier-VFX; the code is 881bbcb's, so not this parcel's): true of the LF form, not of the bytes on disk. Its fix is reading the file through `tree_bytes` and printing the note.
- **The text rule is simpler than git's,** which also weighs a lone CR and the share of unprintable bytes: a file git would sniff as binary on those grounds, that is UTF-8 with CRLF pairs, would be read as LF. None of the 16 sources is that (MEASURED, above). Verifier-VFX showed the difference in a throwaway repository (MEASURED): a file with a lone CR and CRLF pairs is `i/-text`, and its blob keeps the CRLF pairs, which `lf_form` reads as LF. No tracked text file has a CR in its index blob (its census: 1,781 files, 0 `i/crlf`, 0 `i/mixed`).
- **A source that is not in the tree** keeps the digest of its own bytes: the stress run's metrics.jsonl and report.txt.
- **`figure_extracts.py ledger --extend` is refused on the current file,** in 881bbcb and here alike (MEASURED): the ledger states a kernel slack the extract does not list - the statement at line 21472, in the entry headed at line 21429 (MEASURED by verifier-VFX; its -0.363 is round 2's first quad, whose build the extract draws from line 12748). The default remake is unaffected, because its prefix ends before it (at line 21,037). It is VFG's note, and not touched here.
- **Other raw digests of tree files** (the vendoring check in bindings/arduino/sync.py, the image digests in hw/card_stress.py) were not looked at: the brief named three files (READ, `git grep sha256_file`).

**Conduct** (MEASURED):
- A command of mine started `python3 -` with no input and hung. I stopped that background task by its id and listed the python processes read-only: one of 10/15 that is not mine, none of mine.
- I started a job with `&` inside a background task, which makes the task's "completed" mean only that its wrapper shell exited (PK's ledger has the same lesson). The job was a 32 s `--verify`; I waited for its own output file.
- Scratch trees were deleted by their exact paths.

## 2026-10-20 - the stress driver's three fixes: the telemetry sampler serialised, the six routine entries in the revision-8 leg, `--quick` with `--sweep-items`, and an empty wave that says why (parcel DR1, Sonnet 5.5); **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**What Logan asked,** verbatim, on 2026-10-20: "Math round may be slightly delayed to handle 6 and 9, as well as the task chips once the stress test is finished".
- **The chips** are "The follow-ups" of the entry "2026-10-19 - the side parcels of 2026-10-19, closed". Three are the stress driver's, and they are this parcel: the telemetry check's race, the six routine entries in hw/card_stress.py's `REV8_ENTRIES`, and (from the smoke of 2026-10-19) `--quick` with `--sweep-items`. The fourth, the CRLF hazard in python/project_figures.py, is parcel FX's.
- **The lead added two checks** while this parcel ran: the lock's worst case, and the new event read by the report and by the figure reduction (below).

**Fix 1: the telemetry check's race** (hw/card_stress.py, hw/test_card_stress.py).
- **The cause (READ, hw/card_stress.py, hw/card_stress_lib.py's `append_record`, hw/card_stress_standin.py):**
  - the timer's thread and the run's own calls (before a cycle, after its battery, at the end) both ran `telemetry()`;
  - the stand-in's thermal temperature is `30 + 0.5 n` for the n a file counter gives each examine call, and `append_record` stamps `ts` and `epoch` as it writes;
  - so two overlapping calls could take n in one order and write in the other.
  - COMPUTED from the stand-in: a telemetry call in the test makes four examine calls (electrical; thermal; mechanical as JSON and as text, which the stand-in does not know and fails both ways), so consecutive samples step by 2.0. EX's sequence steps 37.0 to 40.0 (six counter values: another sample's calls between) and then to 39.5.
- **The decision: the driver, not the test.** A sample holds one lock from its first examine call to its append, so records are in the order the readings were taken.
  - **Why not the record's two suggestions:** "take the stand-in's temperature from the call's own sample" needs a stand-in that knows the sample, which it does not. "Compare in counter order" is sorting by temperature, since the temperature is a function of the counter: `ts == sorted(ts)` would be true by construction, a check that cannot fail.
  - Two samples of one card at once are also two questions at once to the vendor tool.
- **MEASURED, the race forced, not waited for** (`telemetry_order_checks`, in hw/test_card_stress.py; no load): a sample A takes its reading and is held inside its examine call, a second sample B starts, A is released.
  - **881bbcb's driver** (hw/card_stress.py and hw/card_stress_lib.py from `git show 881bbcb:...`): RED, `readings taken ['A', 'B'], records appended ['B', 'A'], temperatures [31.0, 30.5]`. EX's pair, made on demand.
  - **The final driver:** green.
- **The lock's worst case** (the lead's first added check).
  - **READ:** `examine` is `subprocess.run(..., timeout=--telemetry-timeout)`, which kills the child at the timeout. A sample is at most 3 reports x 2 tools x 2 modes = 12 calls.
  - **COMPUTED:** at the default 60 s a sample is at most 720 s, and only if every call hangs. A per-leg `telemetry()` that arrives behind the timer's sample waits at most that, then takes its own (at 881bbcb: its own alone). The wait is bounded by each call's timeout, not by the hung process.
  - **The finding that mattered:** with the lock alone, a stopping run waited for a whole NEW timer sample: the timer's thread, blocked on the lock, takes it the moment the run's own sample lets go, and the run's `end` sample queues behind it. So a timer sample now drops itself at its next examine call once the run's stop is set (3 lines). The worst alignment is one sample plus one examine timeout longer to stop than at 881bbcb, only if every call hangs.
  - **MEASURED, Windows (Miniconda 3.12.9), dry run** (`scn_telemetry_hang`, `measure_hang.py`, two runs each, no added load): every examine call hangs, `--telemetry-timeout 2`, one report (a sample is two calls), STOP touched when the first hung call began.

    | driver | STOP to end | records | gaps between records | hung calls, alive after |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 881bbcb, no lock | 8.3, 8.4 s | before-cycle, timer, end | 0.5, 4.0 s (the first two samples overlapped) | 6, 0 |
    | the lock alone | 11.9, 11.9 s | before-cycle, timer, end | 4.0, 4.0 s | 6, 0 |
    | the lock and the stop rule (final) | 9.8, 9.8 s | before-cycle, end | 6.1 s | 5, 0 |

  - Each hung call was killed at its 2 s and the run obeyed STOP (exit 0, `stop_file`) in every run. The deadline shares the path (READ: `should_stop()` returns Stop for the stop file, a signal and the deadline in one function, checked between legs).
- **The suite:** `scn_telemetry_hang` (three checks) in group `telemetry`, and a second phase of the forced check for the stop rule. **Plants,** each MEASURED red at the check written for it:
  - the lock removed: the forced check, and the hang scenario's "no two samples ran at once";
  - the stop rule removed: its own check;
  - records appended in swapped pairs: scn_telemetry's own `ts == sorted(ts)` check, by name.
- **Not seen:** a swapped pair at natural load, in the ten runs under "What I ran" (EX's came at load 2.15). **Not measured:** how long a sample takes on the card (BELIEVED about a second).

**Fix 2: the six routine entries in the revision-8 leg** (hw/card_stress.py, hw/test_card_stress.py).
- **The premise holds (READ):** the leg's `--only` named the ten workloads' entries alone, and acceptance.py runs `selected` entries only, so the six never ran in the leg; docs/CARDDAY.md said so twice.
- **What the leg must pass for them (READ, programs/acceptance.py's `prepare`, `probe_library`, `main`):**
  - `--only` with their names;
  - `--lib host/libcft.so`: the mark probe loads libcft by ctypes, and acceptance.py's default is `$CFT_LIB` first. The leg names this tree's library, the one the build step ldd-checks, rather than trust the environment;
  - nothing for `--images`: `prepare` reads `--images` for `workload` entries only, and the six read `programs/systems/compiled-tangent/<name>.cftp` and `.bank`, committed files.
- **The trap:** the leg's `missing` list (entries whose files are not in `--rev8-images`) adds the 14,400 s first-compile allowance to the leg's timeout. The six are never in `--rev8-images`, so counted as missing they would add it to every quad leg for ever. They are exempt, and a check holds that.
- **The decision: a table in the driver, held by the test to both tuples** (the must-have's own words), not derived at run time. The driver is standard-library only, and a parse failure at the start of a 60-hour run is a new way to lose it. **How the drift happened:** MA added `REV8_ROUTINES`, a second tuple in the same file, and the test read `REV8` alone and counted its ten. **How it is shut:** the test reads both tuples, entry for entry and target for target, and refuses any other module-level `REV8` name in acceptance.py that it has not been shown.
- **MEASURED,** the old table check does notice a changed table: with only the driver's table edited, 3 of the 54 `commands` checks went red, the three that encode the old counts. It never read the second tuple.
- **Timeout and estimates (COMPUTED, two figures read from the records):** 353 s for the nine workloads on the quad (2026-10-12) and 57 s for the six on the card (the lead's, 2026-10-19, in docs/CARDDAY.md) make 410 s for the quad's fifteen; the leg's 2400 s is 5.9 times that and is unchanged. `estimate()` is the timeout over three, 800 s, used only against the deadline, also unchanged.
- **`--quick`:** its revision-8 leg runs `phi4_extended_fp64` (a 51 s compile) alone. Routine entries have no compile, so the smoke now also runs one, `lotkavolterra-rk4-tangent-fp64`, on the quad: the routine path (the `--lib` probe, the structured lanes, cft-audit) on the card in the smoke instead of in the long run's first cycle. About 10 s (COMPUTED: 57 s over six, not a measure of that entry), inside the smoke's 24 to 28 minute estimate.
- **What the box needs before the next stress run: nothing beyond a checkout that has this commit and the build the driver already does.**
  - The six's files and programs/acceptance-rev8.json are in git.
  - `host/libcft.so` (XRT=1), `cft-segrun` and `cft-audit` are in `make -C host all`, and the driver's build step ldd-checks them.
  - The lead's by-hand run of the same acceptance.py on rev8q needed no more.
  - `$CFT_LIB` is no longer consulted by the leg.
  - `--rev8-images` stays as it was: only the two long compiles want it, and the six do not use it.
- **The suite:** the table check over both tuples; the quad's leg has 14 entries (eight workloads and the six) and names `--lib`; with the workloads cached it has 15 and its timeout is the leg's own (the routine entries never make it uncached); the deep has no `--lib`; the quick leg is `phi4_extended_fp64,lotkavolterra-rk4-tangent-fp64` with `--lib`; and `scn_normal` reads the stand-in's echo of the command the quick run gave. **Plants,** each MEASURED red at the check written for it: the table drops `culture-rk4-tangent-fp256`; a routine entry counted as uncached; `--lib` not named.

**Fix 3: `--quick` with `--sweep-items`** (hw/card_stress.py, hw/test_card_stress.py).
- **The cause (READ, as the brief says):** `--quick`'s sweep was a fixed list (four items on the quad, `sqrt32-rne` then `rint32-rne` on a single). `plan_wave` passed each to `pick_item` as `only=`, which skips an item that is not in `--sweep-items`. The EX items the lead named were none of quick's four, so every wave was empty; `sweep_phase` then printed "sweep: nothing left to run in this campaign", the words for a finished campaign. The long run was not affected.
- **The decision: (a), and why not (b).**
  - Under `--sweep-items`, quick takes the named items, in the order named, the least served first; the quad takes the first four, a single image one a wave; an item that cannot run is passed over.
  - **Against (b), refusing the pair:** it would send the operator to the long run's whole battery for a smoke of a few items, which is what 2026-10-19's command wanted to avoid. The refusal stays the fallback if the lead prefers it.
  - **A deliberate reading of "the first two on a single image":** the rotation means the single and then the deep take the NEXT items, not the first two again. On a fresh run the quad's four are the first four named, as the brief says. With `--resume` a second smoke should go on again (READ: `load_state` rebuilds the served counts from the records; not run), so 22 items are reached in about three smokes (COMPUTED: eight a smoke) instead of the first four being served again and again.
- **An empty wave says why** (`why_no_wave`; a log line and a `sweep_empty` event in metrics.jsonl). Each item is classed as covered, disabled, outside `--sweep-items`, moved past by the quarantine, or not in this run's catalog (a probe ruled it out).

The harness has two deadlines, `wait_for` 60 s for the first hung call to appear and `r.finish` 120 s for the driver to end (the run takes about 12 s, so 5 and 10 times); a driver that overran 120 s would be killed and its hung stand-ins left alive, which the check would call a failure. It has one more assumption that is not a deadline and that load can break: that a pid `tasklist` reports is the stand-in the test recorded.
  - **Pid reuse is the likely cause: BELIEVED, not reproduced.** `pid_alive` was a `tasklist` substring match, and Windows hands a freed pid out again at once, to the very `tasklist` that asks or to another session's process, so a stand-in the driver had killed could look alive; five killed stand-ins and a desktop whose sessions start processes all the time make it plausible. Nothing I measured reproduces it, and the failing run's detail (cut, with no per-condition values) cannot say.
  - **Could it be the race the serialised sampler closes? No.** The first check never reads the order of records: it asks that each sample is an error record naming a timeout and that no stand-in remains. The order is asked by `telemetry_order_checks`, by scn_telemetry's `ts == sorted(ts)` and by the hang scenario's second check (the gaps). The one way the sampler could make the first check fail is a deadlock that held the driver past the harness's 120 s. READ: `telemetry()` is the only taker of `tel_lock`, and `say` and `write_status`, which take `self.lock`, are never called inside it, so there is no lock order to cycle. BELIEVED, not exercised under load.
  - **ab92598:** `standin_alive(pid)` counts a pid only while its command line is a card_stress_standin.py process (CIM on Windows, /proc elsewhere; unreadable counts as alive), and the check's detail prints each condition (began; each sample's timed-out and ok flags; the hung calls; the stand-ins still alive). MEASURED: a live process carrying the stand-in's name, True; a live python without it, `pid_alive` True and `standin_alive` False; both killed, False and False.

The scenario now kills, by pid, the stand-ins it finds alive (its own); afterwards no python.exe naming the plant's directory remained.
  - **No deadline was widened:** nothing measured implicates either, and widening one on a guess would only let a hang last longer. Both observations stand as a known limit with the load cause BELIEVED; a recurrence now prints which condition failed.

## 2026-10-20 - the random draws made in one order on every compiler (the lead's fix, 1db9592): seven expressions in three host tools that drew two values inside one unsequenced expression, each now two statements in the order every gcc at hand already used, so no draw changes; ten more of the kind remain in a fuzzer and two tests

**Why.** C leaves unspecified the order in which a sum's, a shift's or a call's operands are evaluated (BELIEVED: C99 6.5p3 and 6.5.2.2p10, from the lead's and verifier-VLD's knowledge; the standard is not in the repository). An expression such as `bands[rng() % 7] + (rng() % 3)` therefore drew the band and the offset in the order the compiler chose, and the soak tools' operand streams could depend on the build.

**What changed** (1db9592; `git diff --stat c9741e0 1db9592`: the three files, 25 insertions, 8 deletions):
- host/tools/divsqrt_soak.c: `banded32` and `banded64`;
- host/tools/clause5_soak.c: `banded32`, `banded64` and `cvtfrom_int`;
- host/tools/mpfr_check.c: `rand_enc`'s band, and `check_cvt_from`'s `rng() >> (rng() & 63)`.
- Each of the seven is two statements, the left operand's draw first.

**The evidence** (MEASURED, but for the amd-arc-box results, which are READ: they are the lead's runs, whose logs are transcriptions from the ssh sessions (`replicas-box.log`, `objcmp-box.log`) or their captured output (`c5draws-box.log`, `d5draws-box.log`); the scripts and logs are in the round's records, `briefs/lead-draw/` with a SHA256SUMS file, not committed):
- **Replicas** of the three expression shapes, 3 seeds x 10^6 draws: every compiler at hand calls the left operand's rng() first, at -O0 and -O2. The compilers are MSYS2 gcc 16.1.0 on the desktop (i686-w64-mingw32), gcc 11.4.0 in cft2204 and gcc 13.3.0 on amd-arc-box. clang is on none of the three; verifier-VLD checked the desktop and cft2204.
- **Objects**, old (c9741e0) against new, with the Makefile's flags, with and without `-DCFT_SOAK_HAVE_ROUNDEVEN=1`:
  - divsqrt_soak's are byte-identical under gcc 11.4 and 13.3, and mpfr_check's under 13.3 and 16.1 (16.1 measured by VLD);
  - clause5_soak's code differs under 11.4 and 13.3; under 16.1 (VLD) divsqrt_soak's differs, and clause5_soak's differs without the define (with it, clause5_soak does not build there: `roundeven` and `roundevenf` are undeclared).
  - cft2204's MPFR 4.1 is below mpfr_check's 4.2 floor, so mpfr_check was not built there.
- **The draw functions from the real sources.** The tool's file is included whole in a harness, with `main` renamed, and each function is hashed over 3 seeds x 10^6 draws.
  - divsqrt_soak's `banded32` and `banded64`, and clause5_soak's `banded32`, `banded64`, `cvtfrom_int(32)` and `cvtfrom_int(64)`, give the same hashes old and new, at -O2 and -O0: clause5_soak's under gcc 11.4 and 13.3 with and without the define, and under 16.1 without it; divsqrt_soak's under 11.4 (VLD), 13.3 and 16.1, with and without the define (16.1 with it by VLD).
  - The hashes are the same on all three compilers.

## 2026-10-20 - three outside test sources against libcft: Berkeley TestFloat 3e with SoftFloat 3e, UCBTEST and IBM's FPgen vectors, with their drivers, the arbitration and the tests (parcel XG, Sonnet 5.5); **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**Why.** Logan, 2026-10-20, on the sweep study's question 3: "The more independent generators the better"; on these three: "Go with all three outside generators if possible, more coverage isn't a bad thing even to have". His "Yes" to question 8 stands: the host FPU and libm stay the only *sweep* oracle; these suites bring expected results of their own and are independent checks beside the sweep, and every disagreement is arbitrated by `python/cft_golden`. The manual and the results are `docs/EXTERNAL-GENERATORS.md`. No byte of an outside file is in the repository (the IBM vectors have no licence; UCBTEST's and Berkeley's notices ask to travel with every copy), and every driver takes `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` as the soak tools do, so the lead can run them on the card; this parcel never did. MEASURED: with a nonexistent artifact named, the TestFloat subject and a UCBTEST program built with the hooks each refuse with "no such device" and exit 2, and neither falls back to the software backend.

**What was built** (the tests are of our own code, on cases we wrote; none comes from an outside source):

- `python/external_tf.py` (the pipelines, their counts, the arbitration of every reported case by the golden model with the classes named and the fused multiply-add row recognised from the operands), `python/external_ibm.py` (the `.fptest` reader and runner), `python/external_ucblib.py` (UCBTEST's ten arithmetic vector files), `python/fetch_external.py` (the fetch-and-verify script), `host/tools/ucb_hooks.c` and `host/tools/ucb_run.sh` (UCBTEST's own programs with libcft as the arithmetic under test).
- `python/tests/test_external_gens.py`, 48 tests, in the `golden` stage's `pytest python/tests` (MEASURED: 48 passed under Windows Python 3.12 and, on the committed tree's export, under WSL's 3.10; the whole suite collects 5,287 tests on the desktop, 5,239 at the base and the 48); `docs/EXTERNAL-GENERATORS.md`; a block in `host/Makefile` and one `.gitignore` line. No runner stage was added. **The code is 2,163 lines with its comments** (tf_subject.c 560, ucb_hooks.c 270, ucb_run.sh 118, external_tf.py 472, external_ibm.py 382, external_ucblib.py 168, fetch_external.py 193), **the tests 879** (tf_subject_check.py 281, test_external_gens.py 598), **against the brief's "a few hundred lines in all"; the document is 189 lines against "a page or two"**. **What the instruments measured** (WSL cft2204, niced, one pipeline at a time, the software backend; tininess after rounding, which is libcft's and TestFloat's own default):
- **TestFloat 3e and SoftFloat 3e** built from their own makefiles (3.8 s, specialization 8086-SSE, no edit). **Level 1**, binary32 and binary64: 212 pipelines (every function, every rounding mode both libraries share, exact and not exact where TestFloat has it), 63,940,800 cases, 360 reported cases, all one row (below). **Level 2**: the same 212 pipelines, 2,635,770,880 cases, 2,920 reported, all the same row: 202 pipelines and 1,293,593,600 cases but for mulAdd with 0 reported, and the mulAdd prefix (below) with 10 pipelines, 1,342,177,280 cases and all 2,920. Through `testfloat_ver` with libcft as the subject, levels 1 and 2 and binary128 together: 2,731,696,912 cases (COMPUTED).
- **Level 2 is not complete for mulAdd**: its stream is 14,512,627,712 cases a mode at binary32 and 180,795,884,544 at binary64 (COMPUTED from the generators' loop bounds); what ran is the first 134,217,728 lines of the stream per mode and format (0.92% and 0.074%). Half of them are random triples; the other half are structured with a outer, b middle and c inner, so they hold only the first values of a (MEASURED from the generator's output): at binary32 0 and the powers of two 0x1 to 0x8000 against every b and c pair, and 3,391,232 pairs of 0x10000; at binary64 0x0, 0x1 and 0x2 against every pair, and 6,682,432 pairs of 0x4. The prefixes ran at 1.7 M cases a second at binary32 (399 s for its five) and 1.2 M at binary64 (549 s), MEASURED; at those rates the five modes of the whole stream would take about 12 hours at binary32 and 8.6 days at binary64 (COMPUTED).
- **Division runs 65 K cases a second at binary32 and 52 K at binary64 at one case a call** (MEASURED): 105.9 to 115.9 s for each binary32 mode (7,496,192 cases) and 762.6 to 886.0 s for each of the five binary64 modes (40,284,288 cases, 4,144 s in all). The binary32 rate had predicted 10 minutes a binary64 mode, five times my first guess of 2.

- **Binary128** (beyond the brief's fp32 and fp64, under Logan's "more coverage"; TestFloat's `f128_` functions against libcft's fp128, level 1): 103 pipelines, 31,985,232 cases, 190 reported (38 a mode in five modes), all the same row.
- **The host CPU as the subject** (the brief's "host oracle where it applies"), level 1, add sub mul mulAdd div sqrt at binary32 and binary64 in the four modes x86 has: 48 pipelines, 50,558,304 cases, 288 errors, every one the fma row; it agrees with SoftFloat, bits and flags, on all of add, sub, mul, div and sqrt.
- **Strict probes**, level 1, `--max-errors 0`, every error line arbitrated, all libcft = golden: `-checkInvInts` on the 80 float-to-integer pipelines, 54,720 cases, 13,412 differ (libcft delivers the contract's RISC-V values with invalid, SoftFloat's 8086-SSE the x86 indefinite integer; READ, docs/DETERMINISM.md convertToInteger); `-tininessbefore` on all 212 pipelines, 63,940,800 cases, 8,471 differ (360 the fma row, 8,111 the underflow flag alone, in mul, mulAdd and f64_to_f32); `-checkNaNs` on 202 pipelines, 2,608,320 cases, 138,962 differ, and on the first 600,000 lines of each mulAdd mode and format, 6,000,000 cases, 531,685 differ (the NaN's sign and payload, which the contract canonicalises). My first arbitration of the NaN probes sampled 2,000 a file and left 50,854 and 511,685 counted only; rerun in full.
- **`testsoftfloat`** (SoftFloat against TestFloat's own slowfloat, level 1, the 46 functions the pipelines use): 281 combinations of function, rounding mode (the five and round to odd) and tininess setting, 150,759,744 tests, 0 errors, 2 min 38 s: the oracle of `testfloat_ver` is itself sound in this build.
- **UCBTEST**, `ucb_run.sh` at NTESTS 5,000,000: `ucbdivtest` 8,467,262 cases (single) and 8,465,347 (double), `ucbsqrtest` 1,768,546 and 1,768,269, `ucbmultest` 82,796,202 and 83,000,539 calls (the halfway cases 2,796,202 and 3,000,539, the nearly-halfway cases 5,000,000 each): all six UCBPASS, and the host CPU's own division, root and product, computed beside every call, agree on bits and flags (0 and 0). The same operands through `testfloat_ver`: the same counts, 0 errors. With `CFT_UCB_SABOTAGE=1` all three double programs fail by their own UCBFAIL line. UCBTEST's ten arithmetic vector files, 11,687 vectors (libcft and the host CPU): 0 disagreements, 28 of them cases on which the two detections of tininess differ, and in all 28 the vector's flags equal both predictions. Round to nearest only for division and root, and for the multiplication run (its dumps show no other attribute).
- **IBM**, seven files, 6,798 case lines, all binary32: 5,293 comparable cases run, 1,505 "trap taken" (IEEE 754-1985 trapped overflow and underflow results, which libcft does not model; each has its untrapped twin in the same file among the 5,293), 20 disagreements, the same 20 for the host CPU. IBM's binary64 leg is **empty**: the lead counted the six other binary-model files at the mirror, and every case line of each is b32.
- **Negative controls** (a sabotaged subject itself exits 0; the pipe's gate is `testfloat_ver`, which reports and exits 1): with the TestFloat subject sabotaged, `testfloat_ver` reported 40 and 45 errors in 46,464 cases at period 1,024 and exited 1; the two vector runners, which exit 1 on a defect class, with the subject sabotaged every 7th case: IBM 763 disagreements (743 filed as libcft defects), UCB vectors 1,357 and 1,656 (all so filed; that runner reuses the IBM runner's judge, so its class names read "IBM"), rc 1; the UCBTEST replay with the subject sabotaged every 7th case: 4,849, 4,842, 48,571, 48,571, 1,019 and 1,021 errors found by `testfloat_ver` in its six streams (one case in seven), the replay script's rc 1, and the plain subject on the same dumps none, rc 0. The first attempt on the vector runners, at the default period, changed nothing, because the runners send short streams; that was the control's fault, not the runners', and `CFT_SOAK_SABOTAGE_EVERY` is the fix.

**Every disagreement, classified** (golden arbitrates each; 0 libcft defects):
- **Fused multiply-add, product 0 x infinity, quiet-NaN addend**: level 1, 39 a mode at binary32 (195) and 33 a mode at binary64 (165); the level-2 prefix, 176 a mode (880) and 408 a mode (2,040); binary128, 38 a mode (190); the modes near_even, near_maxMag, minMag, min and max alike. libcft returns the canonical qNaN with no invalid flag; SoftFloat raises invalid and TestFloat expects it. Every case was read back from the error line and checked three ways: libcft equals golden in bits and flags (all 3,280 at binary32 and binary64), SoftFloat's value is the default NaN with its sign set (0xFFC00000, 0xFFF8000000000000) and its flags differ in invalid only, and the operands are the row (one factor zero, the other infinite, the addend a quiet NaN). A **convention difference**: RISC-V requires invalid here and its note says 754-2008 allows but does not demand it (READ by the lead in riscv-isa-manual, `f-st-ext.adoc` lines 319-326; 754 itself not read here); the contract's NaN-in rule is the same in `host/src/softfloat.c`, `rtl/cft_fpfma.sv` and `rtl/cft_fpfma_pipe.sv` (READ by the lead), so the tile cannot disagree with golden on this row; and the host's libm fma (glibc's `fmaf` and `fma` on an i5-12400F, called through the PLT: a library routine, not shown to be the FMA instruction) returns the addend and raises no invalid either, so the sweep's own oracle gives libcft's flags here and not SoftFloat's. `docs/DETERMINISM.md`'s NaN section does not say which of its two sentences wins here: an unstated precedence, the lead's wording. Logan decides.
- **IBM, underflow flag**: 20 of 5,293 (10 `*`, 10 `*+`). IBM's flags equal what tininess detected before rounding gives; libcft and the host CPU detect it after rounding. Each was checked, not assumed: the value agrees, only the underflow bit differs, the before-rounding prediction (exact rational arithmetic and golden's inexact) equals IBM's flags, the result is the smallest normal number; and these are all the cases on which the two detections differ (IBM sides with "before" in 20 and with "after" in 0). The `-tininessbefore` probe finds the same difference at scale (8,111 cases).
- **IBM, trap taken**: 1,505, not compared (above).
- **The three strict probes' classes**, each a convention the contract pins and TestFloat's default does not look at: the integer delivered with invalid raised (13,412), tininess before rounding (8,111) and the NaN's sign and payload (670,647).
