## 2026-10-20 - the `generated` stage counts the checks its passing tools skip, and a CRLF checkout and a CRLF extract are named for what they are (parcel GS, Sonnet 5.5)

**What Logan asked,** verbatim, on 2026-10-20: "Math round may be slightly delayed to handle 6 and 9, as well as the task chips once the stress test is finished". This is the chip that follows parcel FX's entry (above): verifier-VFX found four things while checking FX, and this closes them. Two are known limits that FX's entry lists: "project_packager.py, report only, not changed" (the CRLF refusal, 3 below) and "`figure_extracts.py ledger --verify` on a CRLF-saved extract" printing "ok ... remakes byte for byte" with no note (4 below); the other two are the runner's (1 and 2). FX's entry is not edited (the ledger is append-only), so those two limits still stand in it, and this entry closes them. Each is shown first at c9741e0, then fixed.

**The four, and what closes each:**
1. **The runner's hole.**
   - READ: `do_generated` runs eight `--check`s and, for one that passed, printed only `ok <tool>`. What a passing tool printed never reached the stage's log, which is what `inner_scan` reads.
   - MEASURED at c9741e0 (a scratch clone, this desktop, Git Bash): `bash verify/run.sh --require-all --only generated` gives `generated ok 76s`, "VERDICT: PASS, nothing skipped", exit 0, while the packager's `--check` there prints one plant "not run on this platform" (below). CLAUDE.md says a check skipped inside a passing stage is counted and named on the VERDICT line and fails `--require-all`.
   - Closed by `carry_skips` in verify/run.sh: after `ok <tool>`, each line of the tool's output that `inner_scan` would count is printed into the log as a SKIP line naming the tool. It calls `inner_scan` itself, so a line is a skip there exactly when it is one in any log; `INNER_SKIP_RE` and `inner_scan` are untouched, the tool still prints the marker and the runner only reads it, and the runner's comment block says so.
2. **The packager's line** did not begin with the marker. python/packager_check.py now prints `  SKIP  not run on this platform: <item>`; the summary, "(plus 1 that could not run on this platform, named above)", is unchanged.
3. **A CRLF checkout was refused for the wrong reason.**
   - A tracked file saved CRLF has, under `* text=auto eol=lf`, the same LF blob, and git's clean status for it "holds while the index entry's recorded size is the CRLF file's (the entry was written while the file was already CRLF)", while "a CRLF rewrite of a file the index recorded as LF shows ` M` with an empty diff" (VIW8's words, in the record of the side parcels of 2026-10-19, above). MEASURED again in a scratch repo configured as packager_check's is: ` M` at the first `git status` after the file is saved CRLF, an empty status after `git add -A`. So the clean state is the one after a `git add`, which FX's formats.py was in; a file an editor has just saved is modified to git, and the packager's first gate, `dirty-tree`, refuses it (known limits, below). `check_sidecar` hashes raw bytes, so on a clean tree it called a CRLF source `sidecar-mismatch` (verifier-VFX); a CRLF extract or a CRLF light document was never named as CRLF.
   - Closed by a new refusal, **`crlf-checkout`**, which `figure_extracts.tree_bytes` decides (the repository's one definition, from FX), and which, for a file the archive copies or whose digest a sidecar holds, comes before any digest is compared, so `sidecar-mismatch` cannot be the answer (for a file only STATUS.md reads it comes after the figure check, the PNG renders when they are made, and the other files' digests; below). It names the first five files and how many. docs/EXPORT.md has its row. The packager does not read CRLF as LF and package it (the brief: a larger change, with its own reproducibility questions).
4. **`figure_extracts.py ledger --verify` on a CRLF-saved extract** said "ok ... remakes byte for byte" with no note. `main` now reads the committed extract through `tree_bytes` and prints FX's `crlf_note` on stderr, as `make_ledger` does. That compare is the only `--verify` comparison of a tree file in the script (READ: `load` parses an extract without comparing bytes; the stress reader reads the run's raw metrics.jsonl and report.txt, which are not tree files).

**Which files the CRLF scan reads, and why.** The rule is: every file whose bytes reach the archive, its manifest or STATUS.md. Two halves, because the second cannot be listed ahead:
- **Before anything is compared** (`crlf_files`, 73 files in this tree, MEASURED): the 6 light documents (copied); the 3 data files the README's charts are made from (their digests go in the manifest); the 4 chart SVGs and the 30 figure SVGs and 15 sidecars in docs/img/figures (copied); and the 15 sources and extracts the sidecars name, which `check_sidecar` re-hashes (python/cft_golden/formats.py, hw/gen_layouts.py, docs/figures/{history,ledger,tree,stress}.json and nine text outputs under docs/studies). A source a sidecar records only as a read of part of a changing file (`reads`) is not re-hashed by the packager and is not looked at here.
- **After STATUS.md is built** (`crlf_read`, every file the reader has read by then, MEASURED: 119 in the self-test's `real_tree`, 123 in a real `build`, which also reads LICENSE, NOTICE and the two dark chart SVGs of docs/img/bench, none of which the self-test logs; all four are among the 73, so what is covered is the same; in both, 50 of the reader's files are not in the first half): docs/VALIDATION.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, verify/run.sh, tb/Makefile, formal/run.sh and 45 files under python/tests: the files STATUS.md's readers open (the ledger's headings, the roadmap, the runner's stage list, the bench list, the proofs, the test functions). If the reader failed, the CRLF refusal is given first, since a CRLF file may be why it failed.
- **Why the second half.** MEASURED, in a scratch copy of the 139 files the packager reads, `collect_figures` and `ST.build` as `build` calls them: with docs/VALIDATION.md saved CRLF they still succeed, with no refusal, and make a STATUS.md that is not the LF tree's (sha256 07ca6f617548... against f82a69af061e...) and holds 6 CR bytes; docs/ROADMAP.md CRLF gives another (d8fc1be4b4f6..., 1 CR byte), tb/Makefile another (e72ffffcb6b0...); verify/run.sh and formal/run.sh give the LF tree's. And c9741e0's whole `build()`, on that copy with the file saved CRLF and `git add`ed (so git called the tree clean), wrote an archive from a CRLF docs/VALIDATION.md and from a CRLF NOTICE with no refusal at all. So a scan of only the copied and hashed files would have left FX's likeliest trigger, docs/VALIDATION.md, building a different archive in silence. The packager's self-test (`real_tree`) applies the same second half, so `--check` says what a build would.

## 2026-10-20 - the stress driver's sweep reorganised: the host items off the card onto a CPU pool, collision-free seeds that continue across runs, and coverage counted per RTL tree (parcel DR2, Sonnet 5.5); **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**What Logan decided,** verbatim, 2026-10-20, on docs/studies/SWP-A-coverage.md (section 7, questions 1, 2 and 4):
- **Question 1** ("Do they [the 33 libcft host-code items] leave the card's weekend, and may the lead run them as CPU jobs on the box's idle threads (at `nice -n 10`) beside it?"): "Yes".
- **Question 2** ("Approve the stopgap fix of `seed_for` and the continuation of n across runs (rank 2), or go straight to the enumerated mode?"): "Stopgap now".
- **Question 4** ("Per image, or per RTL tree and generics (the single, quad and deep as one class)? ..."): "Per tree".
- The study counted 33 host items of the 68 the final run served. The driver's catalog has **47 host items of 90**, EX's exhaustive conversions included; the card's sweep keeps the 43 tile items.

**1. The host items leave the card** (hw/card_stress.py, hw/card_stress_lib.py).
- **The reading the brief asks to be checked holds (READ, with the greps MEASURED in the worktree at a07f7c0); no message to the lead was needed for it.**
  - host/include/cft.h 1378-1398 and host/src/clause5.c 11-35 say the host operations have "NO floating-point arithmetic at all", are "bit-identical on every backend by construction", and take the device as "context ... not a participant".
  - The code agrees. In clause5.c lines 565-1392 (convert, the integer conversions, logB, next, class, total order, remainder) `awk` finds no `cft_run(`, `step(`, `dev->`, `->hw`, `backend` or `cft_dev_`; the device-shaped calls are `cft_host_io` (nine call sites) and `cft_flags_emit`.
  - `cft_flags_emit` (host/src/device.c:3386) writes `dev->sticky_flags` and `*flags_out`: host memory. `cft_host_io` reaches the device only for an array the library recognises as a resident `cft_alloc` buffer, and `grep` finds no `cft_alloc` or `cft_buffer` in host/tools/clause5_soak.c or divsqrt_soak.c.
  - `grep` finds each host operation defined in clause5.c alone: nothing in device.c or a backend forwards it. The soak's drivers for them (clause5_soak.c 552-1982) call only `cft_next_up`/`cft_next_down`, `cft_logb`, `cft_class`, `cft_convert`, `cft_cvt_to_*`, `cft_cvt_from_*` and `cft_rem`, and the file calls none of `cft_run`, `cft_div`, `cft_sqrt`, `cft_add`, `cft_mul`, `cft_fma`.
  - `cft_open` (device.c:430) with a NULL artifact skips both `if (artifact)` blocks and returns a software device, and clause5_soak.c 2386-2398 reads `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` and treats an empty value as NULL.
  - So a host item run without `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` runs the code the card run ran, on the software backend, and prints `soaking the software backend`.
- **What was built.** `--host-workers N` (default **8**; 0: the host items do not run at all, and the card does not take them) threads of the driver, from the start of the run to its end, each starting one soak process at a time: the same `clause5-soak` on the same job line, under `nice -n 10` and `timeout` like every leg, with `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` and `CFT_XRT_TILES` **removed from the child's environment**.
  - **The card's sweep takes tile items only** (`plan_wave` and `pick_item` take a `reach`); `--quick`'s fourth quad item is now `rint64-rne`, because `nextup32` is the pool's.
  - A host job's log must say `soaking the software backend`: `parse_soak(cpu=True)` refuses one that names a DEVICE (`parse_error`, "a CPU job opened the card") and the pool stops itself.
  - One slice of an item at a time. Slices are sized as the card's (a probe of 2^20, then the measured rate x `--sweep-slice-seconds`, whole 2^20 steps, cut to the time before the deadline) but held at 2^36 counts, not 2^28: at 2^28 a fast host item (about 37 M/s, the study's class64 figure) gets 7-second slices, and the rotation, which equalises slices served, would give it 7 s a turn against a slow item's 600 s.
- **Why 8** (COMPUTED from the study's figures; a starting figure, BELIEVED, not run on the box). The box has 36 threads. The card's sweep takes at most four of them (a soak process a tile on the quad) and the battery one; the driver, the sampler and the report refresh take little; the rest is the lead's other work (gates, 25 to 30 GB links, other agents), which runs at `nice` 0 and outranks the pool's 10. Eight is a quarter of the threads, 12 of 36 with the card's four, and 3.8 times the throughput the host items had on the card (52.5 per cent of four job slots is 2.1 processes, assuming the four slots were full all the sweep time; the 52.5 per cent is section 2.3 of the study), while the card's four slots go wholly to the tile items (about twice their sweep time: section 5.7 of the study).
- **Records.** A host slice is a `leg` record of kind `sweep`, `image: cpu`, no `image_sha256`, no tile, `sweep.pool` = worker, machine, the tools' build id. status.txt has a `hostpool` line. The report lists `cpu / sweep (all items)` and no longer counts those legs as time "on the card" (they run beside it). New events: `host_pool`, `host_job_abandoned`, `host_pool_stopped`.
- **The run's rules hold for it.**
  - STOP, a signal, the deadline and the disk floor stop the pool as they stop the run, and so, since the second pass (below), does a moved tree: before it plans each slice a worker asks the main loop's own `should_stop()`, which compares `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit the run started from. **The first pass said a moved tree stopped the pool and it did not**: the workers asked `should_stop(git=False)`, and the tree test ran only in the main loop, between legs (verifier-VDR2's (b-1), READ in the code). A slice in flight is given `--kill-after` from the end of the last card leg, then terminated by PID and recorded as the event `host_job_abandoned`, **not as a leg**: a CPU job poisons nothing, so the card's "never in the middle" rule has no reason here, and a killed slice recorded as a `parse_error` would count toward disabling its item. It is not covered, so a resume serves it again.
  - `--resume` rebuilds the pool's coverage, seeds and rates from `metrics.jsonl`, since a host slice is a sweep leg like the card's. `--quick` waits for its three slices.
  - **A host job's failure is its item's, never the card's.** Its log is not read for "the card did not answer" (no `no_device`, which classify_infra would say for words like "library call failed"); nothing it does touches the consecutive-failure count, the recovery ladder or `card_lost`. A `driver_error` in the card's cycle terminates the card's children and leaves the pool's alone (`terminate_children(card_only=True)`).
  - **The estimates stay true:** `--quick`'s 24 to 28 minutes are the card's legs, and the pool's slices (2^18 each; `rem32` at the study's 0.46 M/s is 0.6 s) run beside them; a long run's slices are cut to the deadline like the card's, and `--deadline-grace` is about card legs.
- **MEASURED, dry runs** (the suite's scenarios; Windows, Git Bash, Miniconda Python 3.12.9; the POSIX parts in WSL cft2204): the quick run serves `nextup32`, `conv32to64-all` and `rem32` on `cpu` and eight tile slices on the card's images; the driver started with `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` in its own environment gives its host jobs neither variable (the stand-in prints what it was handed) and its card jobs their image and tile; a hung host job is terminated at STOP (the scenario asserts that the run ended within 9 + 2 + 15 s of STOP, during a 9-second card leg with a 2-second `--kill-after`: the leg's length, the grace, a margin; it did not record the actual figure) and at the deadline (within 20 s of it), with an event and no leg, and no host slice STARTED after STOP or the deadline (a second of margin); three `no such device` host jobs are three `parse_error`s of their item, which is then disabled, with `--max-card-failures 2` and no stop; a disagreeing host job is a recorded `fail`; a resumed run's first host slice starts where the stopped run's coverage ended; a card-cycle `driver_error` does not kill a 9 s host job in flight (it passes); under POSIX a host job runs at the suite's niceness + 10 and under `timeout -k`.

**2. The seeds** (hw/card_stress_lib.py, hw/card_stress.py).
- **The schedule.** The seed of an item's n-th random slice is `(item index << 40) | (n << 1) | 1` (schedule A of docs/studies/swp-a/seed_audit.py): odd already, so the tools' `| 1` changes nothing, and different for every (item, n) with n below 2^39, by construction (n is refused by name beyond that). The tools parse the seed with `strtoull(..., 0)` and set `rng_state = seed | 1` (READ, clause5_soak.c 2370 and 2421-2464, divsqrt_soak.c 462-468), a full 64 bits; base 0, so the driver passes decimal.
  - **The index is the item's place in a table of 54 names (`RANDOM_SEED_ORDER`), not its place in the catalog,** which loses items when a probe fails (a run on a libm without directed scalbn has fewer, and a position would shift every later item's seeds). A new random item is appended, and the catalog refuses, by name, one that is not in the table.
  - **MEASURED, seed_audit.py's method on the driver's own catalog** (`tool state = seed | 1`, count the distinct): 54 items x 605 slice numbers (0..599, 10^5, 10^6, 2^20, 2^31, 2^38) give 32,670 slices and 32,670 different states. The control, the OLD schedule over the study's grid (54 items x n = 0..56): 3,078 slices, 1,597 distinct states, 1,481 shared, **2,962 slices on a shared state - the line of seed_audit.out, reproduced**.
  - Each random slice's record says `seed_scheme: 2`; a record without it is the old schedule.
- **`--earlier-runs DIR[,DIR...]`** names earlier runs' output directories (explicit; nothing is searched for). Each random item's first n here is above the highest n of a **completed** slice (pass or fail) in any of them (and above this file's own, when resumed); `run_start` records the runs and the first n each item got. A slice that did not complete is served again by the run that left it, so its n is not a draw to avoid (a choice, below).
  - **Refused by name, before anything starts (exit 2):** a name that is not a directory, a directory with no `metrics.jsonl`, and a `metrics.jsonl` with a line that does not parse (a floor that is too low repeats draws without a word). A torn last line is allowed and noted.
- **A guard** refuses a planned slice whose tool state another (item, n) in this file or a named directory already started from, naming both; the same (item, n) again, a slice served after a failure, is allowed.
- **An old run resumed is safe.** `--resume` on a file the old schedule wrote continues each item's n from its own highest completed + 1, as it always did, and the new slices use the new formula. The two cannot meet: an old seed is `base_seed + 7919 n` (1,353,449,473 and up, then 3,305,111,553 and up; below 2^32 for n up to about 125,000), a new one is at least 2^40 except item 0's, `2n + 1`, which would need n of 676,724,736. **MEASURED:** the suite makes a file with a copy of the old code (the old formula, no guard, no marker: 8 slices, two items that started the tool from one state, `seed_scheme` absent), resumes it with this driver, and the new slices continue each item's n (from 2), say `seed_scheme` 2, are all different from each other and from every old state.
- **MEASURED,** run B naming run A: A's six slices are n 0..2 of two items; B's are n 3..5; the twelve tool states are different.
- **Not done, as the brief says:** the build-order-independent draw (the tools are HC's and CL's). **Not done, by scope:** exhaustive items still restart at encoding 0 in a new `--out`.

**3. Coverage per RTL tree** (hw/card_stress.py, hw/card_stress_report.py).
- **The run records its tree** in `run_start`: `tree.rtl` (`git rev-parse HEAD:rtl` of the checkout it runs from), `tree.host_src` (host/), `tree.cc` (the compiler's first version line), and `tree.rtl_dirty`, `tree.host_src_dirty` (git status of that directory, untracked included: an untracked .sv is compiled into a bitstream all the same, hw/rebuild-2022.sh). None where git cannot say. **MEASURED here:** rtl `44b963dd6ba2...` (the test compares with its own `git rev-parse HEAD:rtl`).
- **The report** has a section "SWEEP COVERAGE BY TREE" after the sweep's, which says its key: a tile item per **RTL tree**, the images (quad, single, deep) beneath it, each by what it covered alone, the tree's figure their union; a host item per **host/ tree and compiler** (the same host/ under two compilers is two classes), whether it ran on the pool or, before today, on the card. A modified tree is its own class; a run that recorded none is kept apart by its commit. A slice is counted under the **last `run_start` before it in its file**, so a resume from another checkout counts what follows under that checkout.
- **Several runs:** `card_stress_report.py RUN_DIR --also DIR ...` adds other runs to that section alone; each slice stays under its own run's tree, so two trees are never summed. The first sections are RUN_DIR's alone. A directory with no `metrics.jsonl` is refused by name.
- **MEASURED, on a synthetic pair of runs whose truth the test counts by plain loops:** tree A's `sqrt32-rne` is the union of the quad's [0, 2^28), the single's next 2^20 and the deep's first 2^20 = 2^28 + 2^20, with the images 2^28, 2^20, 2^20 beneath (their sum is 2^20 too many); tree B's disjoint slice stays 2^20 apart (a merge would show 2^28 + 2^21); the same host/ tree under two compilers is two classes; `--also` adds the second run's slice to tree A only, and a no-tree run is its own class by commit.
- **`tree_changed`:** a resume whose RTL tree differs from the file's last `run_start` records that event and says what it means: the driver continues from the whole file's coverage whatever its trees, so the report shows the new tree with only what ran after.

**A lost record on Windows** (found in the first dry runs of the pool; the lead asked for these details).
- **MEASURED, how it was seen:** with eight pool workers, a leg was logged `pass` in driver.log and absent from metrics.jsonl, with no torn line. The same scenario (the quick sweep with 22 items named: 8 card slices and 14 host slices) lost exactly one leg record in **4 of 6 runs** before the fix (the suite's run, 2 of a loop of 4, and the first of a loop that I stopped at the first loss); Windows 11 Pro 10.0.22631, Miniconda Python 3.12.9.
- **After the fix, not seen:** 14 of 14 host slices in **8 of 8** runs of the same scenario, and in every later run of it (the suite's `disable` group, which is that scenario, 12 checks each time, green in three Windows runs and four WSL runs: the per-group run and the two whole runs on Windows, and four whole WSL runs).
- **The cause (BELIEVED, from the behaviour and the fix; the CRT's source was not read):** `append_record` relies on `O_APPEND`, which on POSIX makes each `write` atomic; Windows' emulation seeks to the end and then writes, so two threads that open and write at once can write at one offset and one record overwrites the other. The sampler and the card's thread already shared the exposure, rarely.
- **The lock:** a `threading.Lock` in `append_record`, taken for the stamp, the open, the write and the fsync. **The pool's workers are threads of one process, so a threading lock is enough.** Nothing else appends to metrics.jsonl while the driver runs (the report reads it; `repair_tail` runs at the start, before the threads). **On the box (POSIX) `O_APPEND` is BELIEVED to make each write atomic (POSIX's rule for it, from memory; not read in this session and not measured on the box); the code takes the lock there too, unconditionally, so nothing rests on that belief**, at a cost of the write's time (an fsync), and the stamp taken inside the lock keeps the file's order the epochs' order.
- **The test** (`append_lock_checks`, 0.4 s, every platform): eight threads append at one instant, twelve rounds; with the write slowed to 5 ms inside, **no two threads are ever inside it** (the cause: red without the lock, on POSIX too), and every record is in the file, none torn, in epoch order (the symptom). **MEASURED in the second pass, the check's own shape without the lock (60 trials of 8 threads by 12 rounds):** on Windows records were lost in 60 of 60 trials (2,841 of 5,760) and the order was broken in 7; on WSL nothing was lost or torn and the order was broken in 53 of 60 (verifier-VDR2: 12 of 12); with the lock, 0 of 60 in every column on both. The plant (the lock removed) is red at both checks on both hosts, the cause check every time. **The first pass's figure here was wrong** ("4 trials of 60 damaged, no whole record lost"): my scratch script gave its two passes' files one name, so the pass without the lock appended to the files of the pass with it and the duplicates hid the loss (found when I re-measured after VDR2's note on the docstring).

**A lesson the plants taught: an item that moves from one code path to another can orphan a plant, and only the plants stage shows it.** Taking the 47 host items off the card changed which code every scenario that names one of them runs: the card's `run_wave` before, the pool's `run_host_slice` now. Two plants stopped proving what they were written to prove, and not one ordinary check went red, because nothing in the driver was wrong; the no-plants runs of that morning (551 and 568 checks) showed neither, their one failure each being something else (a load flake; the tree check where git cannot read the tree). My first whole-suite run with plants after the pool existed, in WSL (633 checks, 22 m 35 s, 2 failed), found both, by two different lines of the plants stage's own output:
- **`plant [...]: applies - ... found 0 times in card_stress.py; the plant did not apply, so it would prove nothing`:** a plant's edit text matches the code exactly once or the plant is refused. Mine ("the card's sweep picks host items too") did apply when I first ran it (10:43, when its scenario then crashed on a wrapper mistake of mine, which I fixed) and does not now: its edit text is one indent level (four spaces) deeper than the lines in `pick_item`, so the function's shape changed after that run, by my hand, and I did not run the plant again. The scenario never ran.
- **`plant [...]: its scenario FAILS, at the check written for it  caught by: nothing - every check passed under the plant`:** a plant that applied, was run through its scenario, and turned no check red. This one was parcel EX's (da2b52f, 2026-10-19; "the driver does not hold a slice to what it covered": the card's `cover = job["cover"]` made `None`). Its scenario, `scn_sweep_short`, served only conversion items (`cvtto32-all`, `conv32to64-all`, `cvtfrom64-all`), which are host items and now go through the pool, whose own `exp, cover = ...` line the plant does not touch. The card's path still holds a cover spec for the two tile items that have one (`scaleb32-all`, `scaleb32-wide`), but each of those also has an exact case count, which refuses a short slice first (the refusals recorded say "cases where the slice has", the case count's words), so the removal changed nothing that the stand-in's rules of the day could show. That was a real hole: the card's path of the rule had no check that could fail.
- **The fix (0ae1a13):** the same scenario now serves `scaleb32-wide-rne` on the card beside the three host items; the stand-in has a rule `badenc` (the right cases and an encodings clause one too few, a tool contradicting its own job, which only the cover spec can refuse) and the tile item's third slice uses it; the card's plant is caught at that item's checks, and there is a new plant for the pool's path, caught at the host items'. The failing check also names each slice's status and reason now.
- **For the next change that moves an item between paths:** run the plants, not only the checks, and read two lines of their output as a failure to be explained, "applies ... found 0 times" and "caught by nothing". Finding the first kind does not need the 22 minutes: a scratch script (scratchpad, not committed) read every plant's edit list from the source with `ast` and counted each old text in its file; before the fix it said "64 plants read, 1 edit(s) that do not match exactly once", after it "65 plants read, 0 edit(s) that do not match exactly once", and 68 and 0 after the merge (MEASURED, Windows, about a second each). The second kind needs the run, and was exactly the "caught by nothing" line.

- **(b-1) A moved tree did not stop the pool, and the first pass's records said it did.** READ, hw/card_stress.py: the workers asked `should_stop(git=False)`; the tree test needs git and ran only in the main loop, before each battery leg, each sweep wave and each cycle, and a card leg lasts minutes. VDR2's in-process probe: the worker's decision no stop, the main loop's `STOP tree_moved`, `pool_plan()` still planning a slice. No check of the suite named `tree_moved`. The docstring of `should_stop` itself said that the workers skipped git, and I wrote "so none starts after one" in the records about a list whose last member that did not hold for, without reading my own docstring again.
- **The fix (43660c2), as the lead decided:** before it plans each slice a worker asks `should_stop()` with the tree test, the main loop's own. **Cost, MEASURED:** `git rev-parse HEAD` 20 ms median (min 19, max 29) over 30 calls on Windows; a worker makes one call a slice start, and slices last from the first probe of an op (2^20 cases, a fraction of a second; 47 host items, so a burst of about 47 in the first seconds) to `--sweep-slice-seconds`: no interval, the test is per slice. A moved tree is latched in the driver, so no worker plans another slice, and the main loop, at its next check, ends the run as `tree_moved`, exit 3, and records it as it records any stop (one event, `run_end`'s reason). **Guaranteed and not:** no worker plans a slice after anyone has seen the stop; a slice planned in the same few milliseconds still starts, and a slice running when HEAD moves runs on (until `--kill-after` after the run's last card leg), as a card leg does. Each worker now says in driver.log why it stops.
- **A new option, `--check-tree-in-dry-run`:** a dry run has the tree test off by design (its `--root` may be a checkout somebody is committing to); the option switches it on, so that the suite can move HEAD of a scratch repository. Off by default; a real run is unaffected.
- **Tests (MEASURED, Windows; the plants one at a time):** `pool_tree_unit_checks` (in-process, 0.4 s: nobody is stopped before HEAD moves, so the checks can fail; the main loop's test says `tree_moved`, exit 3; a worker started after the move plans nothing and returns at once, with the same stop latched; a plain dry run does not test the tree; the scratch repository is gone afterwards) and `scn_pool_tree` (a process, 16 s: git enabled, a scratch repository as `--root`, a card leg of 12 s in flight, two host items running, HEAD moved by a commit during the leg: no host slice STARTS more than a second after it, and the run ends by `tree_moved`, exit 3, one event). Plants: the workers' tree test removed (red at both, 23 s), the dry run's switch ignored (red at the unit checks, 5 s), and the old plant "the host pool does not look for a stop" re-aimed at the worker's new line (red at its two checks, 39 s). The scenario's first version ended at the build step (`build_failed`): a scratch repository lacks the four files whose marker strings the build step looks for, so it holds copies of them.
- **(b-2) The docstring of `append_lock_checks`** (f76b7fc) said that only Windows shows the symptom and quoted the wrong figure above. It now says what each platform showed, from the measurements above.

**Known limits:**
- **The card was not touched and the box did not run this code.** The pool, the seeds and the tree record ran against the stand-in, in the dry run, on Windows and in WSL. That an XRT=1 `clause5-soak` started without `CFT_SOAK_ARTIFACT` opens no device is READ (`cft_open`'s NULL branch builds a software device and calls no XRT function, device.c:430 onward) and not run on the box. No real soak tool ran through the pool: `parse_soak(cpu=True)` is checked on three REAL logs of the same tools made on the software backend (the fixtures of 2026-10-16), and the stand-in prints the same lines.
- **8 workers is a starting figure** (COMPUTED from the study's job-second share, BELIEVED right): the box's load beside a gate was not measured, and the pool's own CPU cost on the box is not known. `--host-workers` moves it.
- **One slice of an item at a time**, so with fewer host items than workers (a `--sweep-items` naming two) the other workers do not start. The last `--min-slice-seconds` (120) before the deadline starts no host slice, as the card's sweep.
- **A host slice cut off by the run's end is lost work,** at most `--sweep-slice-seconds` (600 s) of one core a worker; the event `host_job_abandoned` names it.
- **Exhaustive items still restart at encoding 0 in a new `--out`;** only the random items' n continues (rank 6, the ledger, is the exhaustive items' answer). `--earlier-runs` counts COMPLETED slices (pass or fail): a slice that did not complete leaves its n free, so the next run may redraw it up to the point it was cut off (harmless; the literal "used" would have skipped it: a reading, below).
- **The tree is the one the driver runs from,** not proved to be the one the images were built from (true for rev8 and f0693b2, MEASURED; the images' SHA-256 is beside it). The tree hash is rtl/'s alone: the three images' generics differ and are kept apart only by the images beneath. `--resume` goes on from the whole file's coverage whatever the trees (`tree_changed` says so); use a new `--out` for a new tree.
- **`--also` counts a directory named twice twice** in slices and cases (coverage, a union, is unaffected).
- **Where git cannot read the tree** (a worktree's .git file names a Windows path, read from WSL) the driver records no tree, and the suite skips the one check that compares it, by name, and its plant. The Windows run does it.
- **The stand-in's `badenc` is a tool contradicting its own job,** which a real soak does not do; it is there so that the cover spec's check on the card's path can fail at all (see the lesson above).
- **The scratch check that finds a plant whose edit no longer applies is not in the suite** (scratchpad, not committed): the suite finds it only in its plants stage, at the end of a 22-minute run. A cheap mode of the suite that reads the plants' edits and counts them is a follow-up for a later parcel; the lead decides.
- **The lost record was fixed on the strength of 4 of 6 and 0 of 8+** (above); the Windows CRT's append emulation is BELIEVED the cause, not read. The cause check is deterministic, and the symptom check is red without the lock in 60 of 60 trials on Windows and 53 of 60 on WSL (MEASURED in the second pass; the first pass said 7 in 100, from the script with the file-name mistake).
- **Failures seen only under load, each once, each passing alone, none chased (the lead's word):** to be read as the suite's sensitivity to a busy desktop, not as defects found. (1) The hang scenario's first check (`scn_telemetry_hang`, DR1's): DR1's own, in a Git Bash `--no-plants` run (DR1's entry above), and mine, in my first full Windows `--no-plants` run (551 checks, 1 failed, 3 skipped, 635 s, while DR1's WSL suite ran beside mine; 5 of 5 alone afterwards: the scenario three times, the group twice). (2) `stopfile`, its 3 checks, in verifier-VDR1's Git Bash `--no-plants` run that took 553 s against 399 s; 5 of 5 alone (READ in the lead's message, not seen by me). (3) Mine, once in three runs of the extended `scn_sweep_short`, right after my WSL suite had ended and with other sessions' suites running: the second check of `cvtto32-all-rne` ("the same slice [0, 2^20) was served again each time, and then passed"); two reruns passed, and the check's detail names each slice's status and reason now, so a recurrence says what happened.
- **python/figure_extracts.py, for the lead (not changed, not mine).** `--verify` with the lead's inputs is rc 0, five ok. On a copy of the lead's metrics with the new `run_start` keys and 169 `cpu` host legs added, `make_stress` reduces without error (it raises when its numbers disagree with the report module's, and did not); its legs go 4,086 to 4,255 and its sweep legs 3,287 to 3,456. One thing it would get wrong for a REAL pool run: `activity_at` (the card's power by what was running) counts a `cpu` sweep leg as "sweep, host items only", but a cpu leg runs beside the card, which may be idle or in a battery leg. It wants `r["image"] != "cpu"` in what it takes as `sweeps_run`. That is FX's file.

**What the brief got wrong:**
- **Its file list** left out hw/card_stress_standin.py, hw/test_card_stress_report.py and hw/test-card-stress.sh. The pool needed lines in the stand-in (what a soak job was handed, so that a test can see a host job got neither variable; later the rule `badenc`); the report's own test lists the report's sections (eight now), and since test_card_stress.py runs that test as a plants control, leaving it would have turned the control red; the wrapper's header names the groups.
- **"About 300 to 600 changed lines with tests"** was a third of what the three parts and their plants took: 1,929 insertions and 165 deletions in eight files (a07f7c0 to b5462f7, the tip before the merge, counted before this entry and the README), 1,753 and 140 of them in the six Python files, and 22 new plants (43 at a07f7c0, 65 at b5462f7; 68 after the merge, with DR1's three). The lead accepted the size.
- **"The run records the RTL tree: `git rev-parse HEAD:rtl` of the tree it runs from"** is the checkout's tree, which the brief does not say differs from the images' in general; it also says nothing of a host where git cannot read the tree (WSL on a Windows worktree), where the record is null and the suite's one check of it is skipped by name.
- **"n for each item then starts above the highest n those directories used"** I read as the highest n of a completed slice (the report's own `highest_seed_n` and `sweep_coverage` read it so); a slice that did not complete is served again by its own run.
- **"(item index << 40)"** did not say index in what. By the catalog's position it would shift when a probe drops items; I used a table by name, and the catalog refuses an item that is not in it.
- **"Host items run ... all through the run"** did not say what `--quick` does: the smoke serves three host items once each and waits for them, or the host items named by `--sweep-items`.
- **It did not say what the report's "on the card" time does with the pool's legs;** left alone it would have counted them, and been near 100 per cent for ever.
- **"Run the full suite and `--no-plants` from Git Bash or WSL"** did not say that WSL cannot read the git of a Windows worktree (its .git file names a Windows path), so that the tree-record check cannot run there; the Windows run is the one that does it.
- **"A plant red then green for each"** is a check at one moment; the brief did not say that a later change can leave a plant meaningless (the lesson above). The plants stage is where that is found, and only if its output is read for "applies ... found 0 times" and "caught by nothing".

## 2026-10-20 - the soak tools' pass size as a build-time override (parcel CK, Sonnet 5.5): `make SOAK_CHUNK=n soak-chunk` builds `divsqrt-soak-cn` and `clause5-soak-cn` against a library of their own compiled `-DCFT_CHUNK=n`; `BATCH` is overridable and the chunked tools name it; the default build is byte for byte unchanged; **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**Why.** The lead's BATCH runs of 2026-10-20 (MEASURED, the lead's; READ here, box/batch-chunk/chunk-run.log of the round's records, which are not in the repository): on one tile of the quad at revision 8, from a clone of 881bbcb, BATCH and `CFT_CHUNK` both 16384 ran rint32 2.81 times as fast as at 4096, rint64 2.00, scaleb32 1.25 and division and square root 1.13 to 1.22, with 0 mismatches; BATCH alone changed nothing, since each call was still four passes. Logan, 2026-10-20, answering the lead's question whether the stress driver's soak builds should use a larger pass size: "Build time override for now with future plans to make adjustable more easily" (READ, the brief; docs/ROADMAP.md, "Decided 2026-10-20", on lead-fma-doc). This is the override. The adjustable form, and the driver's use of the tools, are not built (the latter is parcel DR3's). Marks: MEASURED (a run of this parcel's, with its command), READ (a file, named), COMPUTED (arithmetic on those), BELIEVED (this parcel's, unverified).

**What was built** (MEASURED, `git diff --stat aa62f14` and `wc -l` at the commit). `host/tools/divsqrt_soak.c` (+17) and `host/tools/clause5_soak.c` (+18): `#ifndef BATCH` around the `#define BATCH 4096`, and behind `#if BATCH != 4096 || CFT_CHUNK != 4096` a second stderr line, `soaking with BATCH <n> and CFT_CHUNK <n> (the defaults are 4096)`, after the `soaking the ... backend` line. The backend line itself is untouched because hw/card_stress_lib.py matches it with `^...$` anchors (READ, lines 368 and 369). `host/Makefile` (+147, most of it the block's comments): `SOAK_CHUNK`, the goals `soak-chunk`, `divsqrt-soak-c<n>$(EXE)`, `clause5-soak-c<n>$(EXE)` and `libcft-c<n>.a`, the objects in `soak-c<n>/`, the refusals and `clean-soak-chunk`, which removes each of the 16 allowed sizes' products by exact name and only when each is the right kind of thing: a binary or archive when it is a regular file and no symlink, an object directory when it is a directory and no symlink; anything else of those names stays (a symlink to anything, a dangling symlink, a FIFO, a directory named like a binary, a file named like an object directory), and a regular file with a product's exact name is the build's to remove. `.gitignore` (+20 with its comment): six patterns, the products' SHAPE (`host/divsqrt-soak-c` and `host/clause5-soak-c` followed by exactly four digits or exactly five, `host/soak-c` and four or five digits with a closing slash), **a file the brief did not name**: its own comment says a new tool needs a line there, and without it a build leaves untracked files and every later build id reads `untracked=present` (READ, the comment on cft-segrun, 2026-09-28); the `.exe` forms and the archives are taken by the `host/*.exe` and `host/*.a` that were there. `host/tests/soak_chunk_check.py` (942 lines, the test; it lives in host/tests because it tests host/Makefile and two host tools, where hw/'s tests drive them and need the stress driver's library). `docs/CARDDAY.md` (+118, the section "The soak at a larger pass size"), this entry, and docs/README.md recounted. No file of the library, `hw/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/ROADMAP.md` was touched.

**CK-2: the build** (MEASURED). The dry run of `make SOAK_CHUNK=16384 XRT=1 XRT_ROOT=/opt/x/xrt C5DEFS=-DCFT_SOAK_HAVE_ROUNDEVEN=1 soak-chunk`: every library object, `src/backend_xrt.cpp` included, compiled `-DCFT_CHUNK=16384` into `soak-c16384/src/`; `rm -f libcft-c16384.a` then `ar rcs` of exactly those objects; each tool `-DCFT_CHUNK=16384 -DBATCH=16384`, linked against `libcft-c16384.a` and the XRT libraries, `C5DEFS` on `clause5-soak-c16384` alone; and no default name (`libcft.a`, `src/*.o`, `divsqrt-soak`, `clause5-soak`) anywhere in it. The real build (`make -j6 SOAK_CHUNK=16384 soak-chunk`, 3 s; three sizes and the default tools in one tree 10 s): the three products and 16 objects exist and **the default `libcft.a`, `src/*.o`, `divsqrt-soak` and `clause5-soak` do not**; the sizes sit side by side; the warnings are the two `ignoring #pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS` lines the default build gives under gcc 11. **Refused by name**, twelve values, the empty string and the unset case, each stopping at parse time with the value in the message: unset, empty, 4097, 0, -4096, abc, 8191, 65537, 69632, 131072, 0x4000, 016384 (an octal constant to the compiler), `16384 8192` and 4096.0; a goal that names another size (`divsqrt-soak-c8192` under `SOAK_CHUNK=16384`) is refused naming both; the 16 values 4096 to 65536 give a dry run. **The pass size, seen from outside** (MEASURED): a probe linked with `-Wl,--wrap=cft_run` against each archive sees every pass the composed operations issue. Over 65,545 fp32 operands, passes (all at most the archive's size, and some of exactly it): division 323 at 4096, 171 at 8192, 95 at 16384; square root 493, 261, 145; rint 68, 36, 20; scaleB 17, 9, 5. **The library has no limit on `CFT_CHUNK` that I found** (READ): `#if CFT_CHUNK < 1` is the only check (cft_config.h:376); the scratch is `malloc` of `CFT_CHUNK` times the element size (divsqrt.c lines 272 to 281, 1103 to 1110, 1511 and 1512; clause5.c lines 264 to 267 and 417), no index in either file is narrower than `size_t`, the remote frame cap is 1 GiB (remote.h:49), the kernel's `n` argument is 64 bits (hw/kernel.xml lines 41 to 43), and runs past 32,768 lanes have been made (backend_xrt.cpp's `stage_mask` note: atlas-engine's card day, 2026-09-17; 2026-09-18 is the date of the fix). **So 65536 is the brief's bound, and the Makefile says so**; nothing above 16384 has been run on a card.

**CK-4: the evidence** (MEASURED, `ck4_evidence.py`, WSL cft2204, niced, one process at a time; the script, results.jsonl and summary.txt are in the round's runs-CK directory; 940 runs of the tools, 580 s). The default tools and the `SOAK_CHUNK=16384` ones over the same slice: **352 of 352 verdict lines identical** (cases, value and flag mismatches, encodings, skipped), all with 0 mismatches, stdout byte for byte, and the chunked stderr the default's with the one line added after the backend line. They are: the driver's own 90 sweep items (`sweep_items` of hw/card_stress_lib.py) at two slices each (180); HC's three hard-case modes under every attribute they take, at the start of every segment of each space and the end and middle of the long ones, and at the space's end (128); CL's five class modes, rint64-class and scaleb64-class among them, under every attribute, over the whole space and from a third of it (44). Slices were 135,169 operands (eight full 16384 batches and a tail; 33 default batches), 20,481 for the heavier exhaustive modes and 17,409 for `scaleb32-wide`. **Sabotage** (`CFT_SOAK_SABOTAGE=1`; the sweep's 90 items, 6 of HC's and 22 of CL's): **every one of the 118 fails at both sizes** (exit 1, a nonzero mismatch count) with the same cases. **The flag-mismatch count is 0 at both sizes in all 118**: the brief expected it might differ, and it cannot here, because the sabotage flips a result bit and never a flag. What differs is the VALUE-mismatch count, which is equal in 6 of the sweep's 90 (the five sqrt32 runs and div64-rup), in all 6 of HC's and all 22 of CL's, and different in the other 84. READ and MEASURED, the reason: the sabotage flips the first result of every library call, so a mode that checks a call as a whole counts about once a call (rint32 over 135,169 operands: 68 at 4096, 18 at 16384; scaleb32-wide 2,840 and 1,136; the default count over the chunked one has a median of 3.78 over the 73 items where it is smaller), and divsqrt's modes re-run a failing batch one element at a time, where each single-element call is flipped again; a batch whose first result is a NaN is not seen to fail (the flip keeps a NaN a NaN), so the larger batch loses fewer of them and counts **more** (11 items: div32 under four attributes, div64-rne, rtz, rdn, sqrt64 under four; div32-rne 113,528 at 4096 and 124,854 at 16384).

**What the chunked tools give up** (found by reading and by these runs; the brief named the first). (1) **Flags are compared per batch**, so a flag defect on one operand among others that raise the flag is hidden, and a larger batch widens the OR: with p the share of operands raising it and independence assumed, another operand raises it in a batch of n with probability 1 - (1 - p)^(n - 1) (COMPUTED): p = 1/10,000, 34% at 4096 and 81% at 16384; p = 1/100,000, 4% and 15%. Parcel CL measured the effect itself (its entry above). The lane-exact class items stay as they are: the `*-class` modes run an operand a call (`CLS_BATCH`, 1) whatever BATCH is. I planted no flag defect to show it at the two sizes (a mutation harness is out of scope), so the 34/81 and 4/15 are arithmetic, not a measurement. (2) **A random scaleB slice's case count follows BATCH**: `scaleb32` and `scaleb64` take `count` as cases and run n = min(count, BATCH) operands a batch against the list's 17 or 27 exponents (clause5_soak.c `drv_scaleb`), so cases are `count` rounded up by whole batches: `scaleb32 100000 5 rne` ran 139,264 cases at 4096 and 278,528 at 16384 (MEASURED). A count of 17 (27) times 32,768 is the same at both; every other random mode takes `count` as operands. A driver that expects a slice's cases to be near its count, or sums them to an exact figure, must read the verdict's number. (3) **The same seed is another operand set in `cvtfrom32` and `cvtfrom64`** (READ: a full batch of draws for each of four source types), so a record of a chunked slice does not reproduce at 4096 by seed; the single-array modes and div, sqrt and rem draw the same sequence at any BATCH. The case counts agree (MEASURED). (4) **A call of a few operands is slower**: MEASURED, 200,000 calls, two repetitions, `cft_rint` at fp64 over 1 operand 767 and 837 ns at 4096 against 4,320 and 5,620 ns at 16384, over 4 operands 2.5 and 2.8 against 6.4 and 6.9 microseconds; `cft_div` over 1 operand 16.0 and 18.6 against 21.3 and 21.8 microseconds; `strace -c` counts `brk` at 4,003 against 21,001 over 4,000 rint and 1,000 div calls (the heap growing and trimming around the scratch each composed call allocates, READ: 410 KB at 16384 and 102 KB at 4096 for rint at fp64; an earlier note of mine said mmap, and was wrong). CL's class modes, one operand a call, took 4.5 s against 11.6 s summed over their 44 runs on the software backend; the sweep and HC runs took 56.3 and 93.9 s at the default and 56.7 and 93.7 s chunked, so a big batch costs nothing on the software backend. On the card a call is several passes of about 260 microseconds (the study, BELIEVED), so the 4 microseconds is under 1% there.

**Sent back once, and fixed (verifier VCK, at 318b597; no (a), one (b)).** `make clean` removed a `divsqrt-soak-c16384.log`, which is no product: `clean` used the globs `divsqrt-soak-c[0-9]*`, `clause5-soak-c[0-9]*`, `libcft-c[0-9]*.a` and `soak-c[0-9]*/`, and the `[0-9]` fixes only the first character after `-c` while the `*` takes anything; `.gitignore` had the same three globs. Nothing real was removed (no tracked path matches them, no tool of the repository writes such names), but six statements of mine were false for that name shape: 6098f21's message, the Makefile's comments ("found by name pattern, and no more", "the `[0-9]` keeps it to products"), CARDDAY's "and no more", the test's "the patterns are not wider than the products", and the clean group's "files that only look like them", whose decoys had no digits and so could not see it: I had chosen decoys that did not resemble a product, which confirmed my belief instead of trying to break it. **Fixed in 98a1ac6, a new commit.** (1) `clean` removes exactly the products of the 16 sizes the Makefile allows: a `foreach` over `SOAK_CHUNK_OK` gives each size's two binaries in both forms, its archive and its object directory, by exact name (MEASURED, `make -n clean`: one `rm -f` of 80 names and one `rm -rf` of 16 directories); a `divsqrt-soak-c16384.log`, a `clause5-soak-c16384.txt`, a `libcft-c16384-old.a`, a `soak-c16384-notes/` and a `divsqrt-soak-c12345` (digits of a size the Makefile refuses) survive it. (2) `.gitignore` is tightened to the products' shape, one pattern per digit count, the first of the two options offered: the products have exactly two digit counts (four for 4096 and 8192, five for the other fourteen), and the exact form, one pattern per allowed size for each tool's binary and for the directory, would be 48 lines to keep in step with `SOAK_CHUNK_OK`. **It is wider than the list of sizes** (a four- or five-digit name that is no allowed size is ignored, and `clean` leaves it), and the comment in .gitignore says so. **And two of the decoys stay ignored, by rules that were there before**: `host/divsqrt-soak-c16384.log` by `*.log` (.gitignore line 34) and `host/libcft-c16384-old.a` by `host/*.a` (MEASURED, `git check-ignore -v`). (3) The test: 11 clean decoys that begin like a product and carry a size's digits (the four the send-back named among them), a synthetic set of the products of all 16 sizes beside the tree's own build (so the `foreach` is seen to reach 65536, which the build does not make), the ignore check with the matching pattern, and, each after a control that passes, the plants (g), (h) and (i) above. **Against 318b597 itself** (MEASURED, WSL, the bundle clone): the ignore check run in a scratch repository holding 318b597's own `.gitignore` reports 6 problems (the `clause5-soak-c16384.txt`, the `soak-c16384-notes/keep.txt`, the `clause5-soak-c16384-old`, a six-digit `divsqrt-soak-c163840` and a three-digit `divsqrt-soak-c409` all ignored by the old globs, and the `divsqrt-soak-c16384.log` taken by `host/divsqrt-soak-c[0-9]*` and not by the blanket `*.log`) and 0 against 98a1ac6's; the `build` and `clean` groups run with 318b597's `host/Makefile` and everything else the new tree: `clean` is RED ("clean removed what it did not make": `clause5-soak-c16384-old`, `clause5-soak-c16384.txt`, `divsqrt-soak-c12345`, `divsqrt-soak-c16384.log`, `libcft-c16384-old.a`, `soak-c16384-notes/`, and the files of the directory), and the same run with the new Makefile passes (8 checks, 0 failed). **Sent back a second time (verifier VCK's re-check of 67fd3f6: one (a), four (b)s), and fixed in 1dd88ac, a new commit.** (a) `make clean` removed a REGULAR FILE named exactly like a size's object directory (a file `soak-c8192`): `rm -rf soak-c4096 soak-c8192 ...` has no trailing slash and takes a file as readily as a directory. aa62f14 had no rule and 318b597's `rm -rf soak-c[0-9]*/` took directories only, so 67fd3f6 had made it worse in this one respect, and the clean group had no decoy of the shape, so its "the tree is as it was" could not fail for it. **Sent back a third time (verifier VCK's third pass at 5446351: one (a), two (b)s), and fixed in 6395650, a new commit.** (a) `make clean` removed a symlink to a file, a dangling symlink and a FIFO named like a binary or an archive (VCK's: `divsqrt-soak-c8192`, `libcft-c20480.a`, `libcft-c24576.a`), which aa62f14 kept, because the test on the binaries and archives was `[ ! -d "$f" ]`, which protects only directories. The rule, now stated once and in every sentence that describes it (the Makefile's two comments, CARDDAY, the test's docstring, this entry): **for each allowed size, a binary or archive goes only when it is a regular file and no symlink (`[ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]`), and the object directory only when it is a directory and no symlink; anything else of those names stays (a symlink to anything, a dangling symlink, a FIFO, a directory named like a binary, a file named like an object directory), and a regular file with a product's exact name is the build's to remove, which is what `clean` is for.** (b1) "only if it is the kind of thing a build makes" (Makefile, CARDDAY, the test's docstring, this entry) was false for the links and the FIFO; it is replaced by that rule in all five places. (b2) The second paragraph above had a sentence that a trailing slash on an exact name "would make `rm` fail on a regular file". **That sentence was the lead's**: the second send-back handed it to me without a measurement, and I wrote it into this entry and my report without one. It is false. MEASURED by VCK in WSL, and by me (GNU coreutils 8.32, WSL cft2204): `rm -rf soak-c8192/` on a regular file exits 0 and leaves the file (under `-f` GNU rm treats ENOTDIR as it treats a missing file), and `rm -rf lnk/` on a symlink to a file exits 0 and leaves the link and the file. So a trailing slash would have been a fix for the file named like a directory; the shell test stays because the rule above is wider than that, and because a trailing slash is dangerous for a symlink to a directory (MEASURED by me, same machine): `rm -rf lnk-dir/` on a symlink to a directory exits 0, leaves the link and the target directory, and removes the FILES IN THE TARGET (both of two gone), where the shell test with `! -L` does not touch a symlink. **Why I missed (a) again:** I narrowed the test to the case that had just been shown (a directory) instead of stating the rule for the whole class, regular file or not, and I had not asked what a build can leave in the name's place. The decoys added (`SPECIAL_DECOYS`, sizes the tree does not build; the synthetic products skip their names): a symlink to a file named like a binary (`divsqrt-soak-c57344`), a dangling symlink (`libcft-c53248.a`) and a FIFO (`libcft-c49152.a`, `os.mkfifo`) named like archives, a symlink to a directory named like a binary (`clause5-soak-c45056`) and one named like an object directory (`soak-c40960`); a platform with no `mkfifo` or symlinks skips that decoy by name. **Against 5446351 itself** (MEASURED, WSL, the bundle clone): the `build` and `clean` groups (8 checks) with 5446351's `host/Makefile` and everything else the new tree: `clean` is RED ("clean removed what it did not make": exactly VCK's three, `divsqrt-soak-c57344` the symlink to a file, `libcft-c49152.a` the FIFO and `libcft-c53248.a` the dangling symlink), and the same run with the new Makefile passes (8 checks, 0 failed; the clean check alone, with every decoy, GREEN). Plants (l) and (m) put each earlier form back into the new Makefile and are red at the clean check. HC's `unchanged` group against aa62f14 at 6395650: 59 of 59 invocations identical (86 s); CL's: 259 of 259 (39 s); the four object sha256s of CK-1 are unchanged (neither the Makefile nor the tools changed after 6395650: f2af491 lengthens a message of the test from 12 names to 40 and changes nothing else). The whole test at f2af491, from a second bundle clone: 49 checks, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 101 s.

**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge).
- **Nothing here has touched the card or the box**; the XRT=1 build was only dry-run (an XRT=1 compile needs XRT's headers). That a 16384 pass runs on the card is the lead's measurement above, at one tile of the quad; 8192, 32768 and 65536 have not been run on one.
- **65536 is the brief's bound, not a limit found** (above), and the multiple-of-4096 rule is the brief's too; the Makefile's message and comment say so.
- **The flag-granularity loss is arithmetic here**, a planted flag defect at 4096 and 16384 would measure it.
- **On this desktop's MSYS make `EXE` is empty** (MEASURED, `make -p`; I did not find out why, and the default `divsqrt-soak` has the same property), so a Windows build of these targets was dry-run only, with `EXE=.exe` given, in the test; nothing was compiled on Windows (the soak needs a 64-bit Linux).
- **The test is 942 lines and the build 182** (the brief's ceiling was 100 to 300 changed lines; the test was 713 before the fixes): the test holds nine groups and thirteen planted breakages.
- **`.gitignore` is a shape and not the list of sizes**, so it ignores a four- or five-digit name that is no allowed size (`host/divsqrt-soak-c1234`, `host/divsqrt-soak-c12345`), which `make clean` leaves; the test holds exactly that (the name ignored by a pattern of this build, kept by clean) so that the sentence "no pattern takes a name that only begins like one" is stated with its exception everywhere, and the comment in .gitignore states it. The exact form (48 patterns) would need keeping in step with `SOAK_CHUNK_OK`.
- **The stress driver does not use the chunked tools** (parcel DR3's), so a sweep slice's expected cases for scaleB random items is a thing it must change (above, item 2).
- **A test can only see the tool's own BATCH and CFT_CHUNK on stderr**; that the tool was linked against its own archive is held by the recipe check, and what the archive does by the probe, not by the tool binary itself.

  - VDR1's (b-1): the empty-wave message called a campaign finished when it was not;

The wave-8 Sonnet verifiers' first passes took 70 to 119 minutes on that wave's parcels (median 94; that wave's record), so Haiku's were about a quarter as long by the medians; the parcels differ, so this is not a measured comparison.

## 2026-10-21 - the transcendentals story made true where the project tells it: six of the thirty-nine also run on the tile (README, docs/TRANSCENDENTALS.md, CAPABILITIES.md, docs/HOSTAPI.md), README's "Where this is going" restated, its "Built on it" count corrected, and what was checked and left alone (parcel RM, Sonnet 5.5); **documents only: nothing was run on the card or amd-arc-box, and no new measurement was made**

**What Logan said,** verbatim, on 2026-10-21, setting the week: "the remainder of this week will be focusing on whats present and polishing/refining things that were able to slip by. I believe the main project readme has some stale info about transcendentals still". This is that week's first parcel.

**Why** (READ):
- The thirty-nine functions of table 9.1 have been host operations of libcft since 2026-09-02 to 09-04 (ABI 0.3 to 0.7), and the documents that tell their story said so, truly, and called a tile path a plausible later optimisation: README.md, docs/TRANSCENDENTALS.md, CAPABILITIES.md and docs/HOSTAPI.md.
- M1's build (2026-10-13 to 2026-10-19) made six of them - exp, expm1, exp2, log, log1p and log2 - routines of the tile, compiled by `cftc` for revision 8's targets from 2026-10-15 (its output version 6), marking a lane whose last bit they cannot decide, and run on the card on 2026-10-19 (the seventh wave's closing entry, above).
- README's "Where this is going" was a snapshot, last changed on 2026-09-23 (`git log -L` over its lines at 0b7c959: f3ea02d on 2026-09-16 for its sentence on the outside workload, f49b09b and 1ece3a4 on 2026-09-23 for its figure).

**What each passage said, and what it says now** (READ at 0b7c959; each new statement's source is named):
1. **README.md.**

## 2026-10-21 - a design study of the card scheduler (parcel SD, Sonnet 5.5): `docs/studies/SCHED-A-card-scheduler.md`, with five scripts and their captured runs in `docs/studies/sched-a/`; **none of it has touched the card or amd-arc-box**

**Why.** Logan, 2026-10-21, verbatim: "Every night from 6pm-8am we can run the card on wherever it hasnt reached yet, perhaps a parcel for setting up a 'scheduler' which could be utilized in the future as well for staging program runs etc while retaining metrics about the card and performance, rather than having to rely on scripts as we have so far. Could be beneficial if more cards ever exist in the future, allowing 1 scheduler to manage many cards on a machine for user simplicity." And: "Go ahead and start the design study now since its not specific to any prior steps". The study checks what exists (the stress driver and what it does not do, the lead's seventeen box scripts, the card and the box, the remote backend, what reads the driver's output, the sweep study's ledger plan, the data volumes), states fourteen requirements, weighs the options for architecture, jobs, code, cards, coverage, the metrics store, the interface, deployment and failure, recommends a first version, plans its build in parcels with their plants, and puts thirteen questions to Logan. Nothing in it is built, and nothing under host/, hw/, rtl/, python/, programs/ or tb/ changed. Marks as in the study: MEASURED (a run of this parcel's, named), READ (a file or a record, named), COMPUTED (arithmetic on those), BELIEVED (unverified).

**What the instruments measured** (the desktop, Windows, Miniconda Python 3.12.9, `python -B -I`, one process at a time, 0.6 to 42 s each; each exits nonzero when a check fails and carries controls that must go red; the inputs are the lead's local copies of three runs' `metrics.jsonl`, SHA-256 e7989f88efde... (the 60-hour run), cd0aec75c8fa... (the overnight run of 2026-10-19, night 1) and 38f243c792c7... (the whole two-night file the batch copied back from the box, equal to the box's sum, whose first 751 lines are night 1's and whose last 557 are night 2's, the run of 2026-10-20 to 21; the probes read it as `FILE@1` and `FILE@2`), and the lead's box scripts, none of them in the repository; the probes write LF on every platform):
- **`volumes.py`:** a night's `metrics.jsonl` is 1.44 MB (night 2, 12.093 h, 1,244,103 B), 1.62 MB (night 1, 12.395 h, 1,431,954 B) or 1.83 MB (the 60-hour run, 61.047 h, 7,982,931 B) for a 14-hour window, 526, 590 or 668 MB for 365 nights; telemetry is 76.2, 66.9 and 59.0 per cent of the bytes at 5,446 to 5,448 B a sample, and a compact record of the six values the figures read, with load and memory, is 227 B (24 times smaller); the host's load1 median was 3.28, 2.88 and 3.22 beside the card run, and at least 43,420 of 48,061 MB of memory stayed available; the driver's samples of `/data`'s free space read 17.34 GB (night 2), 18.60 GB (night 1) and 20.69 falling to 20.04 GB (the 60-hour run); the two directories the lead copies a batch's records into hold 28,807 bytes in 5 files (the overnight run) and 223,805 bytes in 61 (the day of the coverage wave's gate and card checks), with no `metrics.jsonl` and no `logs/` among them, while the third copy's directory holds the two-night file and no `logs/`. Three damaged copies each turn a check red, and a run a file does not have is refused.
- **`latency.py`:** how long a stop request waits for the driver's next safe point, from the legs' own intervals: a mean of 245.1 s (night 2), 212.4 s (night 1) and 151.7 s (the 60-hour run), a 95th percentile of 541.3, 524.2 and 481.2 s, a sweep wave averaging 539.7, 272.8 and 131.8 s, the longest leg 660 s on night 2 (685.8 s, the 60-hour run's selftest), and one `acceptance-rev8` leg of 2,188.6 s in cycle 1 of the 60-hour run against a median of 349.2 s in its other 43 visits; the first activity of a run starts 1.4 to 1.9 s after its `run_start` record. The wave counts (51, 105 and 1,076) equal the sum of 1/jobs over the legs, and a seeded Monte Carlo agrees with the exact mean; two planted slips, and a host slice counted as a card activity, are each caught.
- **`guard_probe.py`:** the driver's own `card_user` and `find_card_users` on twelve command lines and a synthetic table of processes: an idle `cft-serve --artifact` is a card user, a gate is allowed, a shell whose text holds a pattern is not one; the lead's `pgrep -fc` pattern, put through the same twelve, gets six wrong (it misses four card users the driver names and flags two processes that use none).
- **`script_census.py`:** the lead's 17 scripts (744 non-blank lines) by what each does: 16 clone from a bundle and assert HEAD, 15 assert a clean status, 7 assert the rtl/ tree, 6 build with `XRT=1` and check `ldd`; nine use the card, each with its own guard (eight `pgrep -fc` patterns, seven different among them, and one status-file guard). A pattern that cannot match and a renamed `pgrep` are caught.
- **`coverage_state.py`:** by the driver's own `sweep_coverage` and `first_gap`, with the trees derived by `git rev-parse` (the first two runs recorded none; night 2 recorded its own, equal to git's): the three runs stand on rtl 44b963dd; 14 of the 18 tile exhaustive items are complete across them; the four `scaleb32-wide` items stood at 5.566 to 6.079 per cent after night 1 and at 19.116 to 19.702 per cent after night 2, which ran alone on them for its 12.09 run hours and gained 13.55 to 13.94 points of their space, 1.12 to 1.15 an hour, in the upper half of the 0.84 to 1.24 that night 1's slot-seconds bracketed (so they finish during the night ending on the morning of 2026-10-27 at that pace, BELIEVED steady); no host slice ran on night 2; all 18 host exhaustive items again cost 4.3 core-hours; all 18 tile items again 194 slot-hours (6.1 to 8.8 nights of 14 hours, 7.0 to 10.1 of the 12.2 run hours a night has given). The union is held to an independent merge; a removed slice, a wrong sum, idle hours counted as run hours, an item with no rate, a recorded tree that is not git's and a run the file does not have are each caught or refused.
- **Also MEASURED, by `git` on this tree:** the rtl/ tree is 44b963dd at f0693b2, 881bbcb and 0b7c959, the host/ tree is 8a138d18, 276ed15a and 4d9905f8, host/src and host/include are byte-identical at all three (60685ae4... and 6b0dc232...), and of the 88 commits between 881bbcb and 0b7c959, 15 touched host/, none of them host/src or host/include, and none touched rtl/ (all of this in `coverage_state.out`).

**Findings the brief did not ask for** (each in the study, with its mark): the driver's guard is not a lock (BELIEVED from the code, not run); the nightly's `--resume` is blind to trees in its planner while the report is not, so the 14 host exhaustive items night 1 completed were not re-run for the new host/ tree (MEASURED on night 2's records: it ran no host slice); the lead's 22-item `--sweep-items` list is a hand-kept ledger that empties (the four wide items finish during the night ending on the morning of 2026-10-27 at night 2's measured pace, COMPUTED, BELIEVED steady), after which the card's waves are empty unless the list is changed; the word "scheduler" is the library's tile scheduler in docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/HOSTAPI.md; and the soak tools pass device index 0 to `cft_open`, which takes an index, so a second card needs a selector the scheduler does not supply.

**What my own drafts got wrong, and what changed** (before the first commit):
- `latency.py` first grouped a cycle's sweep legs into waves by a five-second start rule and found 102 waves where the legs' own `jobs` field gives 105; the grouping is now by overlapping intervals, held to the sum of 1/jobs, with a plant.
- `coverage_state.py` first read a pace from the last six hours and said that only the four wide items ran in them; the other items ran until 11.9 of the 12.4 hours. The method is now the file's slot-seconds with a range, and the false sentence is gone.
- `guard_probe.py`'s control first put `.xclbin` into the lead's pattern and overstated what it flags; it now uses the lead's pattern alone.
- `script_census.py`'s HEAD pattern also matched `HEAD:rtl`, found by its own positive and negative lines.
- In the study: the end of the finite campaign (to 2026-10-29 with the preamble counted), a year of run directories (2.2 GB: the `du` includes the metrics), the report's limit (about 2 GB, not 1.6), the `dt-i` pair (13 to 21 s, not 30), "four days" for the 24 hours between 881bbcb and 0b7c959, the lead's A/B marked READ and not MEASURED, a sentence on both ends of the transport that had no support, the telemetry share ("three fifths to two thirds"), and a second driver "refused by the guard" (now BELIEVED, with its reason).

night 2 is now measured on the third copy (VSD's figures for it, 1,244,103 B over 12.093 h, 1.44 MB per 14 h, 526 MB a year, telemetry 76.2 per cent and load1 median 3.28, are the probe's too), and the three runs and the ranges they make stand wherever the figure was. **B-2 (VSD's):** the safe-point wait was quoted from two runs; **The choices, each with its reason.**
1. **The space generalised in `Item`, not special-cased:** one field, `space`, and every use of 2^32 on a path an item takes reads it (`first_gap`, the status sums, the report's totals); the ones that did not (`_sweep_defect`'s bound, the hex ranges) are bounds every space is under. The items are appended, so no older item's place in the rotation, no seed index and no campaign id moved.
2. **Expected cases, where exact:** a class mode but `cvtto64-class` makes exactly k x E cases and skips none (`exact`, `expected_cases` recorded). A hard-case mode's and `cvtto64-class`'s cases are not a function of the slice, so each slice is held to cases + S = k x E, and each item to its whole-space figures when it becomes wholly covered (`whole_space_ok` or `whole_space_mismatch`): HC's `hard-count` totals (MEASURED again here, below), CL's counts.
3. **The records' flag.** `--records`, with `--sign-key KEYFILE` (signs) or `--device-key HEX` (unsigned, for `sweep_record.py sign`): version 1 puts the device in every record and `Exporter` needs a public key, so `--records` alone is refused by name. Each record the driver appends goes to the sink after the append (`Driver.rec`). A refused leg is an event naming the refusal, and the run goes on.
4. **The chunk rule.** A random stream is the tool state (seed | 1), and for `cvtfrom32` and `cvtfrom64` the batch too: another batch gives the same draws to other source types (MEASURED, below). The seed guard and `--earlier-runs` follow it: a chunked cvtfrom slice is not a repeat of a default one and is not claimed distinct from one it repeats (a chunked slice of any other item IS a repeat of a default slice from the same state, whose draws are the same at any batch); coverage by tree keeps every random item's chunked and default slices in rows of their own. Random scaleB's cases at a BATCH are held exactly under `--sweep-chunk`, and not otherwise, so that a run without the flag holds no random count it did not hold before (a default run is not byte for byte the old one: the 35 new items run in default sweeps by design; verifier-VDR3's note N2, restated at the merge).

**The plants, and the lessons of running them.** Each behaviour the brief names has a plant that turns a check written for it red: the 45 plants of this parcel (115 in the plants stage, 70 at 827c3cf) are in `hw/test_card_stress.py`, by the group whose checks they name: 11 for the items (`items`; one through `commands`), 16 for the pass size and for nothing changing without the flag (`chunk`; two of them through `records`' real run), 14 for the records, the older campaigns' ids and the case total `verify` prints (`records`), 4 for the notes (`notes`; two run through `standin`). **Not every check has a plant of its own,** and this entry does not say "each": of the 115 check sites in the 14 new scenario functions (counted by `ast`, scratch `union2.py`), 47 are the intended check of some plant, and in the full run's log, read by the prefix of each name (it prints 110 characters, so APPROXIMATE), 55 are seen red under at least one plant and 60 under none: the per-log refusals under an item's rule, the pass-size parser's refusals of a damaged line, `--records`' argument refusals, the setup checks of a scenario. They are assertions of the kind the 55 are and fail when what they assert does not hold (a damaged log is refused, an argument is an error), but no plant of this parcel shows it; recorded as a known limit. Running them one at a time (Windows, `CARD_STRESS_PLANT=<name>`) found four whose scenario CRASHED instead of failing its check (a check that did arithmetic on `None`, one that opened a file a broken driver had not written, a refusal escaping the sink into a check that did not expect it, an index into a list a plant had shortened) and one caught by nothing (the report scenario ran the REAL report, not the plant's copy); reading the others for the same fault showed the stand-in's tables were read from a cached import of the real one, which would have hidden a plant in a full run. The checks now read their own copy (`src`), load the stand-in from its file, and a missing file or an item with no rule is a red check. **Where this departs from the brief, and why.**
1. The brief says `--records` writes records "through SG's `Exporter` and `leg()`": every host-pool slice is **refused by `leg()`** (version 1's subject needs an image and its xclbin hash; `cpu` is in no `run_start.images`). They are counted and said once, and the case total `verify` prints equals the driver's coverage of the CARD slices, not of all slices. Signing a host item needs a format change: Logan's.
2. The brief did not foresee the need of a device key for unsigned records (`--device-key`), nor that SG's `campaign_body` said 2^32 for every item (fixed at the lead's word, above).
3. `--records` is exercised end to end on a run that is not a dry run only over test doubles (a scratch tree whose tools, `make` and `ldd` are shell scripts running the stand-in), POSIX only; on every platform by replaying a real dry run's records through the sink with the one field that says "dry run" changed in a scratch directory. Neither weakens the exporter's refusal: the same stream is refused as it stands (checked), the driver refuses `--records` with `--dry-run` at the command line, and no switch of either offers the change.
4. The brief's `expected cases for random scaleb` was a count the default driver never held for a random slice; it is held only under `--sweep-chunk`.

**Known limits, recorded** (Logan's rule: they merge).
- The host-pool slices are not signable (above), and version 1's record has no field for the pass size: a chunked run's streams are told from a default run's by `metrics.jsonl` only.
- `python/figure_extracts.py`'s `STRESS_TILE_OPS` does not list the five new tile modes, so its stress extractor refuses (loudly: "OP_REACH and STRESS_TILE_OPS disagree about the served op") a run that served them, until its list gains them; the filter for `cpu` legs, the one change made there, does not alter the committed figures (below). The report's malformed-record test (`_sweep_defect`) still bounds an interval by 2^32 for every item, so a hand-edited record past a new item's space and under 2^32 would be counted as coverage; the driver writes none.
- `--sweep-chunk` applies to the pool's slices too, where a larger chunk gains nothing (the software backend has no passes) and compares flags over more operands (CK's finding iii); the report says each slice's batch. A class item compares flags per operand call whatever the batch.
- The new items are served after every older tile item has had a slice (they are last in the catalog); `--sweep-items` serves them first. The card's waves wait for their slowest job, so a short class job idles its tile (CARDDAY has the figure).
- `buildreal`'s scratch copy takes a checkout's built products (the known limit of 2026-10-20): the full suite was run in a clean clone, where its two checks pass.
- 60 of the 115 check sites in the new scenario functions are not seen red under any plant (the paragraph on the plants gives them and the method), and the brief's "each new check with its plant" is met for the 47 that are a plant's intended check and shown for 55 in all, not for every check. A plant per refusal is the remedy (about one edited line each in the driver or the library, BELIEVED); it was not written within this parcel's box, which the real-run plants' fault and the second full run used.
- Nothing was run on the card or the box. The XRT=1 build of the chunked tools, a card run of the new items and records written on the box are the lead's.
